name: Citystars Mall
description: Citystars Mall, located in the Nasr City district of Cairo, is one of the largest shopping and entertainment destinations in the Middle East. The retail heart of the integrated Citystars Heliopolis development, it houses over 700 stores spread across multiple levels, anchored by international brands alongside Egyptian boutiques. Beyond shopping, the complex offers a vast food court, a cinema, family entertainment zones, and three connected international hotels. Its glacial air-conditioning and sheer scale make it a popular refuge from Cairo’s heat, with visitors often spending hours navigating its sprawling floors. Holding a strong rating from well over 100,000 reviews, Citystars remains the benchmark shopping-mall experience in the city for locals and tourists alike.
address: 2 Omar Ibn El-Khattab, Masaken Al Mohandesin, Nasr City, Cairo Governorate 4451620
reviews:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ You didn't come to Cairo to get lost — and yet here you are, completely lost in Citystars

If the Pyramids are Egypt's ancient wonder, Citystars Mall is its modern one. This place is genuinely enormous — not "big for a mall" enormous, but "I've been walking for 20 minutes and I'm still on the same floor" enormous. Over 700 stores spread across multiple levels, and somehow every single one of them is worth looking at.

The mix is impressive: international brands sitting right next to Egyptian boutiques, a food court that could feed a small city, a cinema, an entertainment zone, and restaurants covering everything from Koshary to sushi. Air conditioning? Absolutely glacial — a blessing when Cairo is doing its usual 35°C routine outside. 🧊

A few tips: go on a weekday morning if you hate crowds (weekends are a full contact sport), wear comfortable shoes (non-negotiable), and don't skip the food court — local fast food chains you won't find anywhere else.

Whether you need something specific or just want to escape the heat and walk in circles for three hours like everyone else — Citystars delivers. The benchmark for malls in Cairo, full stop. 🏙️

I usually wait until checkout to write a review, but this time I just couldn’t wait.

As an IHG member since 2015 who has stayed at many IHG hotels worldwide, I can confidently say the warmth and hospitality here have been outstanding and a big part of that is thanks to Ms. Shaima at the lobby restaurant.

Her beautiful smile and genuinely welcoming nature immediately caught my attention and made me feel so welcomed. She’s an absolute gem, and the entire F&B team should be incredibly proud and lucky to have her.

The Iftar and sahoor have been absolutely delicious big shout out to the chefs for the amazing food. My room is super comfortable and every time I’ve requested something it’s been brought promptly with a smile.

And the location honestly the best part, right in the heart of Citystars making everything so convenient.

I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Giza Necropolis
description: Famed archaeological site featuring the Great Pyramids, the Great Sphinx & other well-known ruins.

reviews:
The Experience of a Lifetime (February 2026)
Visiting the Great Pyramid of Khufu (Cheops) is a bucket-list item that finally feels like a world-class tourist experience. If you’ve been hesitant due to old reviews about crowds or chaos, the current 2026 setup is a game-changer.
[The Highlights]
* Safety & Atmosphere: I was pleasantly surprised by how safe and organized the entire plateau felt. The security presence is professional and unobtrusive.
* Crowd Control: Despite being a world wonder, it didn’t feel "bottlenecked." The site is vast, and the new visitor flow management is working wonders.
* Free Electric Buses: A massive plus! There are now free shuttle buses that run frequently around the area, making it easy to get from the panoramic viewpoints back to the pyramids without a long trek in the sun.
[The Secret Weapon: Our Guide]
If you want to truly understand the history, book through Memphis Tours and ask for Saad Zaki. He is absolutely amazing—knowledgeable, patient, and knows exactly how to navigate the site to get the best photos without other tourists in the frame. Having a private guide made the history of the 4th Dynasty come alive.
[Pro-Tips for 2026]
* Timing is Everything: Arrive before 9:00 AM. You’ll beat the heat and, more importantly, the long lines that start forming by midday.
* February Weather: It’s the perfect month to visit—crisp air and clear skies, though the sun is still strong.
* Footwear: Even with the new buses, you’ll be walking on uneven sand and rock. Wear closed-toe shoes!
Best for: History buffs, families, and solo travelers. This is an experience everyone should have at least once!

Sobhy Kaber is one of Cairo's most famous traditional Egyptian restaurants, known for its authentic grilled meats and classic home-style dishes. It is especially popular among locals and visitors looking for a genuine Egyptian dining experience.

The restaurant was founded in the mid-1990s by Sobhy Kaber, originally as a small local eatery in the Shubra area of Cairo. The founder's goal was simple:
to serve traditional Egyptian food with generous portions, strong flavors, and consistent quality, similar to what families eat at home.

Through word of mouth, not advertising, the restaurant grew rapidly in popularity. What started as a modest neighborhood grill eventually became a Cairo food landmark, attracting customers from all parts of the city.

One of its biggest attractions is the generous serving size, which helped build a loyal customer base. It became widely known as a place where "Cairo locals eat," which made it especially appealing to tourists seeking non-touristy food.

In recent years, the restaurant gained additional attention due to public discussions around its ownership and financial disputes, which kept the name in the spotlight.

The food was really tasty and hardy, the portions were great, the prices were reasonable and overall a solid Egyptian cuisine’s experience.

name: Mall of Arabia
description: Huge shopping complex with brand-name stores, a food court, movie theater & fountain display.
address: First 6th of October, Giza Governorate 3236220
reviews:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ One of Cairo's Original Mega-Malls — And It Still Delivers

Mall of Arabia isn't trying to be the newest, shiniest thing in Cairo — and that's exactly why it works. This place has been holding it down for years, and you can feel the legacy the moment you walk in. It's massive. Like, "I-got-lost-twice-and-I'm-not-even-mad" massive. The layout is spacious enough that you can actually breathe while you shop, which is more than I can say for some of the newer, overcrowded spots.

The shop mix is solid — you'll find everything from international brands to local favorites, plus a well-stocked supermarket if you need to stock up on snacks for later. The food court? Legit. Multiple restaurants, good variety, and actually tasty options (not just sad mall food).

What I love: It's a one-stop shop. Shopping, dining, groceries — done. The vibe is relaxed, the AC actually works, and it never feels like a tourist trap.

💡 Pro tip: Weekdays are your best bet — weekends get busy but never chaotic. Park near the main entrance if you're planning to hit the supermarket last.

If you want the classic Cairo mall experience without the hassle, Mall of Arabia is still very much in the game. 🛒🍽️✨

This mall offers a modern and spacious shopping experience, ideal for both locals and visitors. It features a wide variety of international and local brands, covering fashion, electronics, beauty, and everyday needs. The layout is well … More

Yesterday, we visited the Mall of Arabia, and the first impression was nothing short of overwhelming—in the best possible way. The mall is absolutely massive, with around 20 gates and an exceptionally large parking area. Despite its huge size, accessibility is very smooth, and finding parking is not a problem at all, which is a big plus for visitors.

Located not very far from Cairo, the Mall of Arabia is definitely worth visiting if you are in or around the city. It feels like a complete world of its own, offering an impressive variety of international brands from all over the globe. From fashion and electronics to lifestyle and luxury labels, this mall truly caters to shopaholics. If you love shopping and exploring branded outlets, the Mall of Arabia is absolutely the place for you.

That said, we personally didn’t shop much here. We were more interested in buying cultural and traditional items rather than branded products, so we focused more on exploring the mall and enjoying its overall vibe. Even without shopping, the experience was enjoyable because the mall is well-designed, spacious, and lively.

One of the highlights of our visit was the food court. It is very large and offers a wide variety of food options, including traditional and local cuisine alongside international fast food chains. We tried some traditional dishes, and the taste was up to the mark—fresh, satisfying, and well-prepared. Another pleasant surprise was the pricing: the food here is quite reasonable and not overly expensive, especially for such a grand mall.

Overall, the Mall of Arabia is more than just a shopping destination—it’s a full experience. Whether you want to shop, eat, walk around, or simply spend quality time, it’s a place worth visiting, especially if you’re in Cairo or in 6th of October city.

name: The Egyptian Museum in Cairo
description:
The Museum of Egyptian Antiquities, commonly known as the Egyptian Museum (al-Matḥaf al-Miṣrī, Egyptian Arabic pronunciation: [elˈmætħæf elˈmɑsˤɾi]) and also called the Cairo Museum or the Egyptian Museum in Cairo (EMC), is a national history museum in Cairo, Egypt.
An Egyptological museum, it houses the largest collection of Egyptian antiquities in the world, including over 170,000 items. The Egyptian Museum occupies a building constructed in 1901 on Tahrir Square and is one of the largest museums in Africa as well as the first national museum of the Middle East.

The Egyptian Museum of Cairo is intense, fascinating, and honestly a bit overwhelming (in the best possible way). It’s packed with history, artifacts, statues, mummies, and treasures everywhere you look. This is not a minimalist or modern museum; it’s raw, dense, and incredibly rich, which somehow makes it feel even more authentic.
You’re literally walking through thousands of years of history in one place. Some rooms feel almost chaotic, but that’s part of the charm, you realize how much Egypt has to show. Seeing things like royal statues, ancient jewelry, and historical pieces up close is very powerful.
As a tip, go with a guide or hire an audio guide if you can. Without context, it’s easy to get lost or miss the importance of what you’re seeing. With explanations, the experience becomes 10x better.
Don’t try to see everything. It’s impossible. Pick highlights and enjoy them calmly. Wear comfortable shoes, there’s a lot of walking and standing.
It can get crowded, so early morning is best. Take breaks when needed; museum fatigue is real here.
It’s not fancy or polished, but it’s real, historic, and deeply impressive. If you want to truly understand ancient Egypt, this museum is essential. Heavy, fascinating, and absolutely worth it.

name: Koshary Abou Tarek
description: Koshary Abou Tarek, located at 16 Marouf Street in Cairo’s Qasr El Nil district, is a celebrated eatery specializing in koshary, Egypt’s national dish. Founded in 1950 by Youssef Zaki — better known as Abou Tarek — the restaurant grew from a humble street cart into a multi-story culinary landmark that draws both locals and tourists from around the world. The signature koshary combines rice, macaroni, lentils, chickpeas, and crispy fried onions, all topped with a flavorful tomato-based sauce and a dash of garlic vinegar. The bustling establishment spans several floors, with patrons often enjoying their meals upstairs for a uniquely Cairene dining experience. Known for its affordability and remarkably quick service, Koshary Abou Tarek has earned a worldwide reputation — even ranking among TasteAtlas’s most legendary restaurants — for delivering authentic Egyptian comfort food in a vibrant setting.

name: Giza Zoo
description:
The Giza Zoo (Ḥadīqat Ḥaywān Al-Gīzah) is a zoological garden in Giza, Egypt. It is one of the few green areas in the city, and includes Giza's largest park. The zoo covers about 80 acres (32 ha), and is home to many endangered species, as well as a selection of endemic fauna.
The first to be built in the Middle East and Africa, rare species have been successfully bred in the zoo—including the first California sea lion to be born in the region.

name: Al-Azhar Park
description:
Al-Azhar Park (Ḥadīqat al-Azhar) is a public park located in qism al-Darb al-Ahmar, in Historic Cairo, Egypt.
Among several honors, this park is listed as one of the world's sixty great public spaces by the Project for Public Spaces. The park was created by the Historic Cities Support Programme of the Aga Khan Trust for Culture (AKTC), an entity of the Aga Khan Development Network. The park was developed at a cost in excess of USD $30 million, its funding a grant to Cairo from Aga Khan IV, a direct descendant of Prophet Muhammad through his daughter, Fatima, and cousin/son-in-law, Ali. He is therefore a descendant of the early Fatimid Caliphs of Cairo.
address: 10 Salah Salem St, El-Darb El-Ahmar, Al-Darb Al-Ahmar, Cairo Governorate 4294010
reviews:
Al-Azhar Park is such a breath of fresh air in the middle of Cairo. It’s calm, green, beautiful, and one of the nicest places to slow down and reset after busy sightseeing days. You forget for a moment that you’re in such a hectic city.
The park is very well maintained, with gardens, fountains, walking paths, and open spaces that invite you to sit, relax, and enjoy the views. From different spots, you get amazing panoramic views of Cairo, including historic mosques and old neighborhoods(it’s especially pretty around sunset).
There are cafés and restaurants inside the park, perfect for a coffee, a light meal, or just sitting and enjoying the atmosphere. Everything feels clean, organized, and safe.
As a tip, go in the late afternoon to enjoy cooler weather and sunset views. Wear comfortable shoes if you plan to walk a lot—it’s bigger than it looks.
Bring water, especially on hot days. It’s a great spot for photos, picnics, or just resting between tours.
Perfect if you want something non-touristy but still special.
Overall, Al-Azhar Park is peaceful, elegant, and very enjoyable. A lovely contrast to the chaos of Cairo and a place I’d definitely recommend if you want a more relaxed, local-feeling experience.

The Saladin Citadel was an truly astonishing monument and easily one of the highlights of our trip to Cairo. The engineering brilliance on display is staggering, particularly the Mosque of Muhammad Ali inside. Even having seen the Taj Mahal, I found this mosque to be one of the most exquisite marvels of history I have ever witnessed. While it is a bit of a blow to the site's "authenticity" to know that many of the stones were repurposed (or as we heard, "stolen") from the Giza pyramids, one must remember that this was the norm in those days—where the rule of law was simply the rule of the powerful.

The visitor experience was a mix of modern convenience and old-world "hustle." Despite the crowds at the entrance, ticketing was relatively easy. It is important for future visitors to know that paying with a credit card is much easier than tendering cash, as the site has moved toward a cashless system.
However, be wary once you are inside. The government-approved electric golf carts are run by men who, in my experience, will try to scam you. They pressure you to pay an upfront "tip"; I strongly advise against this. If you pay them at the start, they often stop showing up for you. You have to "keep it interesting" and make them feel that a reward is coming at the end to ensure they actually provide the service.

The National Military Museum was also fascinating, specifically the collection of ancient USSR weaponry and aircraft. However, the presentation felt a bit like a "propaganda machine"—the subtle (and not-so-subtle) nationalistic messaging was a bit of an overkill. Even here, the issue of solicitation persists; a cop at the entrance blatantly asked me for a "tip." I had to remind him that in most countries, giving a "tip" to a police officer is regarded as a bribe, which finally made him walk away.

For some reason, this mall always brings back the early-20s version of me every time I visit—lol.

Indeed, this is Cairo's most ancient shopping arcade, making no attempt to vie with the glittering modern edifices that have since arisen. Its interior and very atmosphere are imbued with a certain nostalgic charm. Yet herein lies its peculiar appeal—and, one might argue, its supreme virtue: unadulterated practicality.

It caters to every mundane necessity, housing a collection of haberdasheries for one's daily attire and a variety of victualing establishments where one might procure a modest repast. Let it be known, however, that one should not anticipate haute couture or epicurean dining.

The undisputed triumph of this establishment, however, is its carriage park—a capacious arena where a berth is ever readily available. For those wearied by the urban pandemonium and the perpetual dearth of parking, it is nothing short of a sanctuary. I should heartily commend it to any soul who prizes convenience above the pursuit of luxury.

name: The Great Pyramid of Giza
description:
The Great Pyramid of Giza is the largest of the Egyptian pyramids and the most famous landmark of the Giza pyramid complex in Giza, Egypt. It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and the only wonder that has remained largely intact. The Great Pyramid served as the tomb of Egyptian Pharaoh Khufu ("Cheops"), who ruled during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom. It was built c. 2600 BC over a period of about 26 years.
Initially standing at 146.6 metres (481 feet), the Great Pyramid was the world's tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years. Over time, most of the smooth white limestone casing was removed, which lowered the pyramid's height to the current 138.5 metres (454.4 ft); what is seen today is the underlying core structure. Each side of the base was measured to be about 230.3 metres (755.6 ft) in length, giving a volume of roughly 2.6 million cubic metres (92 million cubic feet), which includes an internal hillock. The dimensions of the pyramid were 280 royal cubits (146.7 m; 481.4 ft) high, a base length of 440 cubits (230.6 m; 756.4 ft), with a seked of ⁠5+1/2⁠ palms (a slope of 51°50'40").
The Great Pyramid was built by quarrying an estimated 2.3 million large blocks, weighing 6 million tonnes in total. The majority of the stones are not uniform in size or shape, and are only roughly dressed. The outside layers were bound together by mortar, primarily local limestone from the Giza Plateau was used for its construction. Other blocks wer...
address: Al Haram, Nazlet El-Semman, Al Haram, Giza Governorate 3512201
reviews:
Visiting the Pyramids of Giza was an incredible experience and absolutely worth it. Standing in front of these ancient wonders truly reminds you of how rich, vast, and powerful human history is. No matter how many pictures you’ve seen, nothing compares to seeing them in person—it’s simply excellent.
That said, a few practical tips can make the experience much smoother. There are local vendors outside who may try to overcharge or mislead visitors, especially for horse and camel rides. It’s important to know that the prices for camel and horse rides are fixed. Once you are inside the complex, you can choose directly from the official lineup—there’s no need to engage with anyone outside, as that’s where most people end up getting overcharged.
I would also strongly recommend booking entry tickets online in advance, as the site can get quite crowded and this saves time and hassle.
For those planning to go inside a pyramid, consider visiting one of the smaller pyramids instead of the Great Pyramid. Entering the main pyramid can be very exhausting and physically demanding, while the smaller ones offer a similar experience with much less effort.
Overall, despite a few minor inconveniences, the experience was absolutely amazing and unforgettable. The Pyramids of Giza are a true wonder of the world and something everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime.

name: Cairo Tower
description:
The Cairo Tower (Borg El-Qāhira) is a free-standing concrete tower in Cairo, Egypt. At 187 m (614 ft), it was the tallest structure in Egypt for 37 years until 1998, when it was surpassed by the Suez Canal overhead powerline crossing. It was the tallest structure in North Africa for 21 years until 1982, when it was surpassed by the Nador transmitter in Morocco. It was the tallest structure in Africa for one year until 1962, when it was surpassed by Sentech Tower in South Africa.
One of Cairo's well-known modern monuments, sometimes considered Egypt's second most famous landmark after the Pyramids of Giza, it stands in the Gezira district on Gezira Island in the River Nile, close to downtown Cairo.
address: Kasr Al Nile, Zamalek, Cairo Governorate 4270024
reviews:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Cairo's best kept secret is hiding in plain sight — on top of a giant concrete lotus flower

Cairo Tower will absolutely mess up your sense of scale. You walk in, wait a bit (bring patience — and maybe a snack), take a lift up 187 metres, and suddenly 22 million people spread across the desert haze below you like the world's most chaotic carpet. The Pyramids on one side, the Nile winding through the city on the other — it's the kind of view that makes your phone camera feel inadequate.

Now, the wait. Yes, it can test you. Especially on weekends. But here's the pro tip nobody tells you: come at night. The city transforms completely — the Nile turns into a black mirror with a thousand reflections, and Cairo glows amber as far as you can see. Worth every minute of standing in that queue. 🌙

Skip the café inside (overpriced) — come for the view, stay for the sunset, and let the night completely redefine what "spectacular" means to you. A mandatory stop in Cairo. 🗼

name: Great Sphinx of Giza
description: Iconic stone monument that is more than 4,500 years old & has a human face on a lion's body.
address: Al Haram, Giza Governorate 3512201
reviews:
DWARFED BY TIME - A MORNING WITH THE GREAT SPHINX

We visited the Great Sphinx of Giza on a weekday morning in January 2026 as part of a large group touring Egypt. Approaching through the ancient temple complex near the second pyramid of Khafre added a sense of ceremony to the experience. As we walked closer, the Sphinx slowly revealed itself in full grandeur, set dramatically against the imposing backdrop of the pyramid behind it viz. Khafre ( the second pyramid of Giza which appears taller than the Great Pyramid of Khufu as Khafre is located in higher ground).

Photographs and documentaries do not prepare one for the sheer scale of this monument. Standing before the Sphinx, I felt unexpectedly small—almost insignificant—dwarfed not only by its colossal size but also by the weight of its 4,500-year legacy. Carved from a single limestone outcrop, the fusion of a lion’s body and a pharaoh’s head radiates power, serenity, and mystery in equal measure.

The calm of the weekday morning allowed us to absorb the site without excessive crowds. Though our visit lasted under an hour, the impact was lasting and the image lingers in my thoughts long after the visit. The Sphinx is more than a sculpture; it is a silent witness to millennia of human history. Seeing it up close, framed by the timeless desert and the pyramid of Khafre, was a humbling and unforgettable experience. This should figure in the itinerary of everyone visiting Egypt.

When it comes to sightseeing in Egypt, the Great Sphinx of Giza is just as iconic as the pyramids.

It is located near the entrance to the pyramid complex, so most visitors naturally see it as part of the same visit.

I had seen it many times in photos and videos, but standing in front of it in person was a completely different experience.

It felt much larger than I had imagined, and its presence was truly overwhelming.

Despite centuries of erosion, its form remains, and you can really feel the weight of history.

Looking closely at the details of the carving and the expression on its face, it feels less like just a tourist attraction and more like you are standing before a true ancient monument.

The area is crowded with visitors and can be quite lively, but it is still a place worth seeing at least once with your own eyes.

Visiting together with the pyramids makes you strongly realize that you are truly in Egypt.

name: The Grand Egyptian Museum
description:
The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM; el-Matḥaf el-Miṣriyy el-Kebir) is a national archaeological museum in Giza, Egypt. Dedicated to Ancient Egypt and its culture, society, and artifacts, the GEM is the largest museum in the world for a single civilization.
Located about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) from the Giza Pyramid Complex, the museum houses a collection of Egyptian artifacts from various periods of Egyptian civilization, from the Predynastic Period to Roman Egypt. There are an estimated total of over 100,000 artifacts, including at least 20,000 that were displayed for the first time ever, such as the complete King Tutankhamun collection comprising 5,398 pieces, on display in a 7,500 m2 (81,000 ft2) section of the museum. Some newly-restored pieces will be displayed for the first time, such as the second solar ship of Khufu, the collection of Queen Hetepheres (mother of King Khufu), and the collection of Yuya and Thuya (parents of Queen Tiye).
The museum covers a total area of 500,000 m2 (5,400,000 ft2), with a built-up area of 167,000 m2 (1,800,000 ft2) and floor area of 81,000 m2 (870,000 ft2). It will also host permanent exhibition galleries, temporary exhibitions, special exhibitions, a children's museum, and virtual and large-format screens with a total floor area of 32,000 m2 (340,000 ft2). The GEM was first announced in 1992, actual construction began in 2005, and it was fully completed in 2023 at a cost of $1.2 billion. Trial opening be...

My visit to Grand Mall Maadi was an okayish shopping experience, but it was definitely shaped by the timing and the local environment. I arrived on a Friday morning at 10:00 AM, which I quickly realized was a mistake as not many stores were open yet. It was also surprising—and a bit off-putting—to see people smoking freely inside the mall, which isn't something you expect in a modern shopping center.

The biggest hurdle was the payment situation. Some stores didn't accept USD or credit cards, which was a major inconvenience. Luckily, there was a bank on-site, but even then, the machines failed to dispense local currency. I found myself in a bit of a bind, which a local man tried to take advantage of by offering a very high exchange rate for EGP. Fortunately, I was able to negotiate and managed to get a reasonable rate, but it was a stressful situation I’d rather have avoided.

If you plan on visiting, I’d strongly recommend that you carry EGP (Egyptian Pounds) with you. Relying on the mall’s ATMs or hoping for card acceptance is risky, and having cash on hand will save you from the hassle of negotiating for currency in the middle of your shopping trip.

name: Baron Empain Palace
description: Stately & abandoned Indian Hindu temple featuring a carved wooden spiral staircase & gardens.
address: El-Orouba, El-Montaza, Heliopolis, Cairo Governorate 11757
reviews:
Baron Palace is truly an architectural masterpiece. Even as a casual visitor, you can’t help but admire the level of detail, but I’m sure architects and design enthusiasts would find the architectural sketches, influences, and history especially fascinating.

The entire place is surrounded by an air of mysticism and mystery. The mix of Indian and Buddhist sculptures, motifs, and engravings covering the palace walls gives it an almost otherworldly feel, unlike anything else you’ll find in Cairo.

Very disappointing experience at JW Marriott Hotel Cairo while checking the venue for a potential wedding booking with my sister and her wedding planner.

There was a wedding taking place, and we were respectfully observing the setup, DJ, lighting, and overall atmosphere to evaluate the venue live, something that is completely normal when considering a wedding location. The venue manager, Gamal Abdel latif, initially approached us and asked if we needed assistance. We politely explained that we wanted to look around first and would come back to discuss details afterward.

A few minutes later, while we were quietly observing the venue, he abruptly waved at us to leave in an extremely rude and dismissive manner simply because we were not actively speaking to him at that moment. I asked him to step outside to discuss the issue calmly, but his attitude remained unprofessional and hostile. He insisted we were not allowed to check the venue unless accompanied by him at all times, despite the fact that we had already informed him we would speak with him shortly.

What made the interaction even more frustrating is that when we initially asked him about details related to the wedding setup, he stated that he “doesn’t know anything” and that another team handles those matters which made his aggressive behavior even more unnecessary and confusing.

I regularly visit Marriott properties around the world and have toured multiple hotels and wedding venues before. I have never experienced this level of disrespect, poor hospitality, and lack of professionalism. A luxury hotel brand should know that staff attitude is part of the customer experience, especially when dealing with potential wedding clients making major decisions.

This interaction completely changed our perception of the hotel, and unfortunately I would never consider booking such an important event at a venue where guests are treated this way.

So glad to finally see Cairo Stadium revamped and accommodating more than 75,000 spectators on a game days.

Food and beverage as well as toilets are located all around the stadium in all seating categories as well as outside in the FAN ZONE.

To enter the stadium during a game day, the EFA now follows the standard for a FAN ID in all major competition matches held in Egypt. These can be obtained online; however, they do not offer tourist visits to the stadium like other famous stadiums around the world.

It also took 40 minutes just to exchange one drink for another.

When the food finally arrived, it was cold—completely cold. This showed that the issue wasn’t in the kitchen, but in the service. The food had clearly been prepared well in advance, and we could have received it on time if the service had been better.

In the end, although the food itself was nice, I will never return because of the poor service. There are plenty of other restaurants offering grilled options where the service is far more professional.

name: Abdeen Palace Museum
description: Abdeen District is the home of Abdeen Palace, a 19th-century Cairo palace built by Khedive Ismail and served as the Egyptian royal household's primary official residence from 1874 until the 1952 Egyptian revolution. Since then it has been one of the presidential palaces. The palace is centered in its eponymous district, administratively part of the Western Area of Cairo, and part of the Khedival Cairo Area of Value to the west of Historic Cairo.
address: 26VW+7VP Street Gmah, El-Gomhoreya Square, Rahbet Abdin, Abdeen, Cairo Governorate 4281035
reviews:
Visiting Abdeen Palace felt like stepping directly into a living chapter of Egypt’s royal history. The palace grounds alone are worth the trip—the gardens are beautifully maintained, highlighted by magnificent gazebos. One of the most striking features is the surreal fig tree, said to have been imported specially from Bangladesh by the king himself.

Inside, the palace is a treasure trove of carefully preserved rooms showcasing an extraordinary collection of the kings’ possessions. From intricately crafted weapons to personal items that offer a glimpse into their daily lives, each room tells a story. What makes the experience even richer is the inclusion of artifacts from other notable figures throughout Egypt’s history, creating a layered narrative that spans eras.

Overall, Abdeen Palace is not just a museum—it’s a journey through Egypt’s royal legacy. Beautiful, informative, and genuinely awe-inspiring.

name: Orman Garden
description:
The Orman Garden at Giza, Cairo is one of the most famous Botanical gardens in Egypt. It was founded in 1875 during the reign of Khedive Isma'il Pasha. He established the garden on a larger site than it presently occupies as part of the Palace of the Khedive. A great lover of gardens, the Khedive entrusted the design of the garden to the French landscaper Jean-Pierre Barillet-Deschamps. It became a public botanical garden in 1910/1917 and put under the Ministry of Agriculture management.
The garden covers about 28 acres. Today, the garden contains a rock garden, a rose garden, cactus gardens, and probably the most notable feature, the lotus pond.
Orman Garden is west of the River Nile and east of Cairo University in the Giza Governorate. "Orman" is a Turkish word, which means "the forest".
A small botanical museum attached to the garden shelters herbaria dating from the Ismail khedive and furniture from the king Farouk.
address: Square, Ahmed Zewail, Oula, Al Giza, Giza Governorate

name: Al-Hakim Mosque
description:
The al-Hakim Mosque (Masjid al-Ḥākim), also known as al-Anwar (lit. 'the Illuminated'), is a mosque in Cairo, Egypt. It is named after al-Ḥākim bi-Amr Allāh (985–1021), the 6th Fatimid caliph and 16th Ismāʿīlī Imam. Construction of the mosque was originally started by Caliph al-ʿAziz, the son of al-Muʿizz and the father of al-Ḥākim, in 990 CE. It was completed in 1013 by al-Ḥākim, which is why it is named after him.
The mosque is located in Islamic Cairo, on the east side of al-Muʿizz Street, just south of Bab al-Futuh (the northern city gate). In the centuries since its construction, the mosque was often neglected and re-purposed for other functions, eventually falling into ruin. In 1980, a major restoration and reconstruction of the mosque was completed by the Dawoodi Bohras, resulting in its reopening for religious use.
Architecturally, the mosque consists of a hypostyle prayer hall and a wide internal courtyard (sahn), accessed via a projecting entrance portal. Its most notable features are its two unusual minarets: the original minarets of the mosque have ornate multi-tiered designs but, for reasons that remain unclear, these were encased shortly afterwards inside the massive square bastions still seen today.

Sayyidah Nafisah (also known as Nafisah bint al-Hasan) was a revered female saint and descendant of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). She is highly respected in Islamic tradition, particularly in Egypt, where she spent much of her life and where her shrine remains a place of visitation.

Lineage & Early Life
- She was born in **145 AH (762 CE)** in Mecca.
- Her full name was **Nafisah bint al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib**, making her a direct descendant of Imam Hasan, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
- Her family was part of the **Ahl al-Bayt** (the Prophet's household), known for their piety and scholarship

Travels & Knowledge
- Nafisah was known for her deep knowledge of Islam, including **Quranic exegesis (Tafsir)**, Hadith, and Fiqh.
- She traveled from Mecca to **Madinah**, where she studied and taught religious sciences.
- Later, she moved to **Egypt** with her husband, **Ishaq al-Mu’tamin** (a scholar and descendant of Imam Ja’far al-Sadiq).

Life in Egypt
- In Egypt, she became famous for her **piety, worship, and miracles (karamat)**.
- She was known for fasting during the day and praying at night, often completing the entire Quran in one night of worship.
- Many scholars and students sought her knowledge, including **Imam al-Shafi’i** (founder of the Shafi’i school of Islamic jurisprudence), who held her in high regard.
- When Imam al-Shafi’i was near death, he requested that Sayyidah Nafisah lead his funeral prayer, but she declined due to modesty. Instead, she prayed for him from her home.

Death & Shrine
- She passed away in **208 AH (824 CE)** in Egypt.
- Initially, her husband planned to bury her in Madinah, but the people of Egypt begged to keep her remains there due to her spiritual status.
- Her **shrine in Cairo** (near the Mosque of Sayyidah Zaynab) remains a major site of visitation (ziyarah) for Muslims seeking blessings.
- Her tomb is known as **"Masjid al-Sayyidah Nafisah"** and is a place of prayer and reflection.

Legacy
- Sayyidah Nafisah is remembered for her **asceticism, knowledge, and devotion**.
- She played a key role in spreading Islamic teachings in Egypt.
- Many miracles and answered prayers are attributed to her, making her one of the most revered female saints in Islam.

Diamond Mall offers a decent shopping experience, but it needs better organization and advertisement to attract more visitors. The layout can be confusing, making it easy to get lost. Clearer signage and a more structured design would improve the experience.

One of the mall’s highlights is its play area. The prices are reasonable, making it a great spot for families with children. It provides good entertainment options, ensuring kids have a fun time while parents shop.

Food options are limited. There aren’t many restaurants or cafes, so visitors looking for a meal might be disappointed. However, there are a few notable spots, such as Al-Abd and Tifidbas, which offer sweets and desserts. Expanding the food court would make the mall more appealing.

The mall has a strong focus on jewelry and accessories. There are many shops selling a variety of designs, catering to different tastes and budgets. This makes it a good destination for those looking to buy gifts or personal accessories. Additionally, the mall features stores selling computers and computer accessories. Tech enthusiasts can find useful gadgets, but they might need to navigate carefully to locate specific stores.

Clothing stores are also available, providing options for different styles and preferences. However, the variety is not as extensive as in larger malls. Shoppers might find what they need, but more well-known brands would enhance the mall’s appeal.

Overall, Diamond Mall is a good place to shop, but it could be improved with better organization and clearer directions. More advertising would help attract a larger crowd. If you plan to visit, be prepared to explore and ask for directions if needed.

This a beautiful and historic mosque that adjoins another beautiful and historic mosque. Both can be visited with the same shared ticket which is priced very reasonably. Both are beautiful on the inside as well as the outside. Though I liked the inside of the other mosque better, I found the architecture of this mosque to be more impressive from the outside.

For those that come here, know that you will have to remove your shoes like you would at any mosque, and that the counter where you can leave your shoes isn't intended to be free! I saw a few tourists who, when picking up their shoes, didn't give any money to the attendant. One said they didn't have cash, the others just ignored the attendants. It was hard to watch.

I know that tipping culture can be strange and off-putting to some people from certain cultures, but in some places (and situations) like this one, it is important to give a small token of appreciation for the person who watched your belongings. Please bring a little cash here or carry your shoes in your bag.

name: Bab al-Futuh
description: Bab al-Futuh (lit. 'Conquest Gate') is one of three remaining gates in the city wall of the old city of Cairo, Egypt. It is located at the northern end of al-Mu'izz Street. The other two remaining gates are Bab al-Nasr (Victory Gate) in the north and Bab Zuwayla (Gate of Zuwayla) in the south. The gate was built during the Fatimid period, originally in the 10th century, then rebuilt in its current form in the late 11th century.
address: 1 Darb Al Keshta, El-Gamaleya, El Gamaliya, Cairo Governorate 4334111
reviews:
Walking through Bab-ul-Fath and Al-Husayni along Al-Mu‘izzi Street feels like stepping into a living museum of Egyptian heritage. These historic streets are alive with centuries of culture, where every arch, lantern, and stone whispers stories of Cairo’s glorious past. The area is rich in authentic Egyptian culture, making it one of the best places to truly feel the heartbeat of the city.

The best time to visit is at night, when the streets glow under warm lights and the atmosphere transforms into something magical. Traditional music fills the air, performers and street sounds blend together, and the nightlife feels vibrant yet deeply rooted in history. The energy is unmatched.

As you walk—because this experience must be enjoyed on foot—you’ll find countless shops selling handcrafted souvenirs, perfect for taking a piece of Egypt back to your loved ones. From brass lamps to scarves, perfumes, and traditional artifacts, every corner offers something special.

Food lovers will feel at home here. The area is packed with restaurants and street vendors serving classic Egyptian dishes, rich in flavor and tradition. Eating here is not just a meal; it’s part of the cultural experience.

The streets are usually crowded and lively, so stay aware of your belongings and be cautious of scammers or snatchers—but don’t let that take away from the experience. Embrace the chaos, enjoy the rhythm of the crowd, and soak in the authentic vibe.

This is not just a place to visit—it’s a place to feel Egypt.

Families and children can enjoy dedicated entertainment areas, including indoor playgrounds, electronic games, and a modern cinema complex.

The mall provides numerous facilities, including ample parking spaces, 24/7 security, customer service desks, free Wi-Fi, and accessible facilities for people with disabilities. Seasonal events and special promotions are regularly organized to enhance the shopping and entertainment experience for visitors.

Personal Experience:
During my visit to Cairo Mall, I was impressed by its spacious and clean environment. Walking through the corridors was easy, and the stores were well-organized, making shopping convenient. I enjoyed dining at an Italian restaurant inside the mall, where the food was delicious and the service efficient. My children loved the entertainment areas, especially the indoor playground and arcade games. Recommendation:
I highly recommend visiting Cairo Mall for a full-day experience combining shopping, dining, and entertainment. Arriving earlier during weekends can help avoid crowds. Overall, Cairo Mall offers a modern, comfortable, and family-friendly environment that makes every visit enjoyable.

I recently stayed at Concorde El Salam Hotel and wanted to share my honest review.

I stayed in Room 119 from February 5th to February 7th.

First, cleanliness was acceptable, which is still a positive point for the hotel. Also, the staff were polite and cooperative throughout the stay.

However, there are a few points that need improvement:

- The food needs more variety. The options were somewhat limited and repetitive.
- The room telephone was not working, which made it inconvenient to contact services.
- On the last day before check-out, we faced an unpleasant situation:
The hotel provided one card that is used both to access the room and operate the elevator. The card stopped working while we were going up to get our luggage, even though there was still time before check-out. Because the same card operates the elevator and opens the room, we were unable to reach the room or access our luggage until we went back to reception to reactivate it, which caused delay and inconvenience during departure.

Overall, the stay was acceptable, but small details like these make a big difference in the guest experience. I hope management works on improving them, as the hotel has the potential to offer a much better stay.

name: Hanging Church
description: Coptic Orthodox church with a wooden roof in the shape of Noah's ark, a 5th-century pulpit & icons.
address: Mar Grgs, Station Mtrou El Anfaq(Margrgs, Ibrahim Ali, Kom Ghorab, Old Cairo, Cairo Governorate 4244001
reviews:
THE HANGING CHURCH - A SERENE JEWEL OF COPTIC CAIRO

We visited the famed Hanging Church in January 2026 as part of a large group exploring the historic Coptic area of Cairo. Most monuments in this area date from the 3rd to 12th centuries CE, though many were rebuilt or restored later. The district represents early Christianity in Egypt, the monastic tradition, and the development of Coptic art and architecture. Tucked within the ancient precincts of Old Cairo and built above the old Roman fortress of Babylon, this remarkable church instantly conveys a deep sense of antiquity and spiritual continuity.

Approaching the church through narrow, historic lanes adds to the experience. As one climbs the steps and enters, the atmosphere becomes calm and contemplative despite the steady flow of visitors. The beautifully crafted wooden ceiling, said to resemble Noah’s Ark, the elegant marble pulpit, and the remarkable collection of icons create an ambience that is both sacred and artistically rich. Every corner of the church reflects centuries of devotion and preservation.

Though we were part of a large group, the visit felt unhurried and meaningful. The church stands not merely as a monument but as a living place of worship and heritage for Egypt’s Coptic Christian community. Our stop here formed a memorable highlight of our visit to Coptic Cairo, offering a gentle yet powerful glimpse into one of the oldest Christian traditions in the world. We hope to come back here soon.

The panel contains a bilingual religious inscription - typical of monuments in Coptic quarter of old Cairo, containing both coptic and Greek Christian text on the top and the Arabian below. The upper section with crosses is writen in Coptic, the lithurgical language and the lower section is in Arabic, probably from the medieval or Ottoman period. Here, Coptic remained the sacred language and Arabic became the public or administrative language. All this reflects the Church's continuous use across centuries. It is a historical record of Church's reconstruction and dedication preserved on the wall.

A nice church built without usual foundations but perched on palm tree trunks that u can see thru the glass at one of the room. That’s why it’s called hanging church. The oldest church in Egypt built in 4AD. The tiles with stories of Jesus … More

Visiting the Hanging Church (Saint Virgin Mary's Coptic Orthodox Church) was one of the most memorable experiences of my trip to Cairo. Located in the heart of Old Cairo, this historic church beautifully reflects Egypt’s deep Christian heritage and timeless architecture. As soon as you enter, you can feel the serenity and sacred atmosphere that has surrounded this place for over a thousand years.

The church’s name, “Hanging,” comes from the fact that it was built above an ancient Roman gatehouse — and you can actually see parts of the old structure beneath it, which is truly fascinating. Inside, the wooden ceiling, designed to resemble Noah’s Ark, and the intricate icons depicting the life of Jesus and the Virgin Mary are absolutely stunning. The craftsmanship and attention to detail are remarkable.

The site is well-maintained and free to enter, though donations are appreciated. The surrounding area, known as Coptic Cairo, is also worth exploring — with other nearby attractions like the Coptic Museum, the Church of St. Sergius and Bacchus, and the Ben Ezra Synagogue.

I recommend visiting in the morning to avoid the crowds and to take your time appreciating the calm, spiritual environment. Whether you’re religious, interested in history, or simply looking for a peaceful escape from Cairo’s hustle and bustle, the Hanging Church is an unmissable landmark. A truly inspiring place that connects you to Egypt’s diverse cultural and religious history.

24/1/26 Saturday early evening meal

We three middle aged guys from London had toured the Coptic centre of Cairo, headed back to our hotel near Taria Square and needed a meal before heading our back to the Opera House later.

We had passed this restaurant the previous evening much too late after the Opera had finished. The kitchens had closed by 11. The boards promised vegetarian dishes and we voted to come back earlier to sample them.

This time we arrived around 5:30 to find a quite busy courtyard with locals and groups of Chinese students.

We had a look at the menus better entering and found the vegetarian options limited. We decided to stay and try it out.

A waiter showed us a table in the far right corner by the stairs leading to the internal dining room. We hoped no-one would smoke near us.

We were presented with more menus and separate drinks menus. Prices seemed reasonable. We chose two mains - Moussaka without meat (110), Penne Arrabiata (130), Lentil Soup (60), Beet & Yoghurt Salad (95), Caesar Salad (92), Banana with Milk (90), Lemon & Mint Juice (71) and a Sahlab (88). The menu started a 14%VAT would be added. There was no mention of Service at all.

The drinks came in good time and were tasty and generous. The Sahlab looked like a cross between. A babychino and zabaione topped with sliced nuts, interesting and hot. My lemon and mint was good as was the banana and milk.

A team of waiters then dressed the tables and presented the lentil soup which included half a lemon and croutons. My friend liked it.

A selection of salt, pepper, mustard and two spicy sauces were provided.

The salads came and were generous. My other friend is an expert on Caesar Salad (traditionally NEVER had chicken in it!) and found it tasty but lacking in real parmesan (that might have increased the price a lot!) and anchovies. It did have a quartered on it which is a no-no.

We shared the salads as the main courses arrived.

My Penne Arrabiata was also generous and with a lot of sauce. It was mildly spicy though. I could have spiced it up with a hot sauce but did not get round to it. The single slice of garlic bread helped.

Our friend's meatless Moussaka was tasty but not a proper moussaka as there was no layer of béchamel sauce. The aubergines were good though.

We enjoyed our meal and as we needed to get changed for the concert at our hotel nearby we could not hang around.

I added up the bill on my phone, asked the waiter for the 'cheque' as they say and it arrived at the correct amount of Eg 841.32 inc the tax. The waiter explained service was not included. We paid that by card and left a 100 tip hopefully to be shared between the many waiters who served us.

The large Chinese group nearby seemed to have a few issues with the bill. I hope they resolved it. The larger the group the more complex the bills.

reviews:
Ibn Hamido – Seafood Restaurant Review
I recently visited Ibn Hamido for dinner, encouraged by its relatively high Google rating. Overall, the experience was good but not exceptional, and here’s why:
Positives
• Extensive Menu: The restaurant offers a wide variety of seafood options, which is great for those who enjoy exploring different dishes.
• Availability: Most items on the menu were in stock, which is not always the case in seafood restaurants.
• Reasonable Pricing: Considering the location and the quality of the food, the prices are fair and offer decent value for money.
Areas for Improvement
• Menu Clarity: The menu could be more organized and easier to navigate. Some dishes were not clearly described, which made ordering a bit confusing.
• Service Speed: The restaurant was very busy, and it took quite a while to place our order. Even after ordering, the wait time for food was longer than expected, especially since we only ordered a few simple dishes.
• Crowded Atmosphere: While the popularity of the place is understandable, the high level of activity made the dining experience feel rushed and less comfortable.
Overall Impression
Ibn Hamido is a solid choice if you’re looking for a wide range of seafood at reasonable prices. However, if you value quick service and a more relaxed dining experience, you might find it slightly disappointing. In short, a good experience, but not the best seafood restaurant I’ve tried.

name: Mosque of Muhammad Ali
description: Grand, 19th-century mosque in Cairo's iconic Citadel, lavishly decorated with Islamic motifs.
address: Salah al-Din, al-Ayyubi, Saladin, Cairo Governorate 4252360
reviews:
The Mosque of Muhammad Ali is one of the most iconic spots in Cairo, and honestly, it’s impressive from the moment you see it. Sitting high inside the Citadel, the views alone already make the visit worth it. You can see a big part of the city from up there, and on a clear day it’s beautiful.
The mosque itself is elegant, grand, and very harmonious. The interior feels calm and spacious, with soft light, big chandeliers, and a peaceful atmosphere despite how popular it is. It has a very different vibe from older mosques, clean, balanced, and almost regal.
If you are visiting remember to dress modestly (covered shoulders and legs). If you’re not dressed appropriately, there are coverings available at the entrance. It is better if you go earlier in the day or near sunset for better light and fewer crowds.
Take your time in the courtyard, the views from there are underrated and perfect for photos.
A guide isn’t mandatory, but having some context helps you appreciate the history and why this mosque is so important. Also be mindful of people offering “extra help” or photo services—nothing inside requires it.
Overall, it’s a must-visit in Cairo. Beautiful, well maintained, and very symbolic. A place where history, architecture, and views come together perfectly. Calm, powerful, and absolutely worth your time.

This is an absolute MUST-VISIT! Don't miss it! The entry fee is around 450-550 EGP, but it's totally worth every penny. The site is massive, and you can easily spend half a day exploring the museums and the stunning mosque. The main hall of … More

The Muhammad Ali Mosque is a monument of truly inspiring grandeur. Dominating the Citadel of Saladin, its Ottoman architecture is majestic and imposing. The exterior, with its towering minarets, is emblematic of Cairo's skyline. The interior is even more dazzling: the vast dome, impressive chandeliers, and alabaster details are magnificent. A symbolic and touching detail are the 365 candles arranged inside, representing each day of the year, adding a layer of spiritual meaning to the visual beauty. It is a place of profound cultural importance. I recommend that anyone visiting Cairo, should not miss the opportunity to visit this monument.

reviews:
We recently visited this local shawarma restaurant in Giza, Egypt, and it was an absolutely delightful experience from start to finish. The place had a lively and authentic vibe — bustling with energy, filled with the aroma of freshly grilled shawarma, and clearly a favorite among locals.

We started with their fresh cocktail and mango juices, both of which were outstanding. The juices were pulpy, refreshing, and naturally sweet, a perfect start to the meal on a warm Giza evening. For our main course, we ordered the chicken shawarma with fries, and it turned out to be one of the best shawarmas we’ve ever had. The chicken was tender, juicy, and bursting with flavor, complemented perfectly by the crisp, golden fries.

One of the highlights of our visit was watching the chef prepare fresh kunafa right in front of us. The smell alone was irresistible, and when we finally tasted it, the kunafa was simply divine — soft, rich, and perfectly balanced in sweetness. It was the ideal ending to a wonderful meal.

Despite the restaurant being incredibly busy and overloaded with orders, the staff managed everything efficiently. Our server, Basel, was particularly friendly and attentive, ensuring we had everything we needed with a smile.

Overall, this restaurant captures the essence of great Egyptian street food — flavorful, fresh, and full of life. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Giza and craving authentic shawarma and an unforgettable kunafa experience.

Kasr El Kababgi: The Ultimate Royal Dining Experience for Authentic Egyptian Grills! 🥩👑
When it comes to authentic oriental food and premium grills, Kasr El Kababgi stands undefeated. The name says it all—it is truly a "Palace." From the grand entrance to the luxurious, spacious interior, the atmosphere exudes elegance and high-end Egyptian hospitality. The restaurant is beautifully designed with grand seating areas, making it the perfect destination for massive family gatherings, business lunches, or celebrating special occasions where you want to impress your guests.
The Food & Grills: 🥩🔥
The culinary experience here is absolute perfection. Their grills—including Kabab, Kofta, Tarb, and Lamb Chops—are expertly prepared using high-quality local meats. The meat is incredibly tender, juicy, and perfectly seasoned, carrying that irresistible smoky charcoal flavor without losing its natural richness. Apart from the grills, their traditional Egyptian tagines, stuffed pigeon (Hamam), and vine leaves are legendary. Everything, from the rich soups to the freshly baked, piping hot bread, is served with flawless execution. And you definitely cannot leave without trying their oriental desserts like "Om Ali" or Basbousa with cream, which provide the perfect sweet ending.
Service & Ambiance: 🤝🌟
Despite the restaurant being consistently busy, the management and staff operate with incredible efficiency. The greeting at the door is warm, and the waiters are extremely professional, attentive, and quick on their feet. The food arrives surprisingly fast, well-organized, and beautifully presented. Cleanliness is maintained at a strict 5-star standard across the entire venue. The overall vibe is lively, vibrant, and deeply rooted in generous Egyptian culture.
Final Verdict: 🌟
Kasr El Kababgi perfectly balances premium food quality, impeccable luxury service, and an unforgettable cultural atmosphere. It offers fantastic value for money given the top-tier dining experience you receive. It is easily one of the best oriental restaurants in the country, and a place you will find yourself returning to again and again! 🏆❤️

You must not be in a hurry when you come here. There is a vast space to visit and it is better to do it calmly; you have to walk between one historical monument and the other.
This place starts your imagination when you try to frame what you see in a scenario of what and how things were done in those ancient times. Death was more important than life because life was temporary, but death instead brought eternity to those who knew what things to do and how to do them in the right way, to guarantee the passage into the afterlife and the possibility of a return.
On the site, excavations are still continuing today; who knows what else we will discover soon? Some constructions are made of stone, others of mud bricks that have wonderfully arrived until our days.
On the walls and on the steles, there are representations of daily life with all its actions of fishing, agriculture, and even punishment for failure to pay taxes. Furthermore, various rites of worship and offerings to the gods are represented. Also, the relationships of sweet affection between some royal characters are very clearly highlighted.
Naturally, everything that could be taken away has been removed and transported to various museums (statues, sarcophagi, objects), but the place makes you feel the atmosphere; it shows you the general image of a complex so large and ancient. There are also many places to take beautiful photos. Many professional photographers are there.
Attention to the workers!!! They ask for money in an incredible way without any shame! If they open a door for you or show you with a finger which direction to go, that's it, you are in debt! Simply answer: "I paid for the ticket."
With us, one of the workers (without having helped or explained anything to us) was very insistent. When my husband refused the tip, he continued to grumble behind us: "Ok no problem, no money, no money yes? Ok no money".
Then I turned around and told him everything I thought: "I worked hard for the money I have and I paid a price for this ticket that is not small, so what money do I owe you now?". Then the worker apologized and disappeared.
Be careful, give tips when you feel like doing it, do not allow others to manipulate you — you are already paying for tickets, you owe them nothing extra!

reviews: It was such a great stay, the room was good the place is quite, but it's so difficult to get a transportation or Uber there unfortunately, but I would like to thank norhan from the front desk team for her genuine care and assistance she helped me to get Uber which made my stay much easier each time

⭐ 1/5 – Very Disappointing Experience

I stayed at Helnan Landmark Hotel for two nights because we had an event inside the hotel.

When I arrived around 4:00 PM, the reception staff were polite and respectful, and the check-in process was smooth. The room itself was clean and acceptable, although it did not have a view.

However, the real issue happened on the second day.

On the first day, food delivery was allowed without any problem. On the second day, I ordered food again, but the delivery person called me and said that security refused to let him enter. I went downstairs to understand the situation, and everything was still being discussed politely.

Suddenly, a man who claimed to be the Events / Halls Booking Manager arrived and spoke to me in a very rude and aggressive manner. He raised his voice, behaved in a completely unprofessional way, and even pushed me physically to stop me from entering, which is absolutely unacceptable in any hotel, especially a hotel of this level.

This kind of behavior is shocking and reflects very poorly on the hotel management. Regardless of any internal policies, there is no excuse for disrespect, shouting, or physical contact with a guest.

Unfortunately, because of this incident, I will not stay at this hotel again, and I do not recommend it to anyone who expects basic respect and professional treatment.

name: Mosque of Ibn Tulun
description: Sprawling 9th-century mosque featuring a spiral minaret & a courtyard lined with stucco arcades.
address: Ahmed Ibn Tolon Sq., Tolon, El Sayeda Zeinab, Cairo Governorate 4261342
reviews:
Considered one of the most magnificent mosques in Egypt and the wider Islamic world, this historic monument preserves its original architectural character despite the many centuries that have passed since its construction. What truly sets this mosque apart is its groundbreaking design, as it was the first mosque ever built without the use of standalone columns. Instead, its builders relied on thick brick walls and carefully engineered arches to support the structure. This innovative method not only gave the mosque exceptional strength, but also made it remarkably resistant to natural elements. Thanks to this construction style, the mosque is fireproof and highly resilient against flooding, ensuring its survival through numerous historical challenges and environmental conditions.

Another distinctive feature of this mosque is its unique minaret, which is unlike any other in Egypt. Its design closely resembles the famous spiral minaret found in Samarra, Iraq, making it an architectural rarity within the country and a fascinating example of cross-cultural Islamic influence. This uncommon structure adds to the mosque’s visual identity and historical significance.

In addition to its architectural and historical importance, the mosque is open to visitors free of charge, allowing people from all backgrounds to experience its beauty and spiritual atmosphere. Visiting this mosque is not merely a sightseeing activity, but a journey through history, faith, and innovation. It is truly a must-visit landmark that everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime.

name: Panoramic View of the Pyramids
description: Panoramic View of the Pyramids, located in the Al Omraneyah area of Cairo, is a well-regarded landmark. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.7-star rating from 5,220 reviews and standing as a firm favorite that draws steady crowds. Visitors frequently note views over the Nile and pleasant views. address: Al Omraneyah, Giza Governorate 3512201
reviews:
It is the only surviving wonder of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Built over 4,500 years ago, it remains a a monumental testament to ancient engineering, located on the west bank of the Nile in Egypt.
The pyramids of Giza and the Great Sphinx are among the most popular tourist destinations in the world, and indeed already were even in Roman times. Each of these spectacular structures served as the final resting place of a king of the 4th Dynasty (c.2613–2494 BC). The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for king Khufu (c.2589–2566 BC), and the other two for Khafre and Menkaure, his son and grandson. Khufu’s pyramid is both the oldest and largest of the three, and the first building to exceed it in height would not be built for another 3,800 years!

Although the three pyramids dominate the plateau, they are in fact surrounded by many other monuments. Every king’s pyramid was just one element albeit the most important of a larger complex that included smaller, subsidiary, queens’ pyramids; an additional one that acted as a second, symbolic, tomb for the king, called a satellite pyramid; mastaba tombs for nobility and other family members; burials of actual and/or symbolic boats; and a pair of temples linked by a richly decorated causeway. One of these temples, called the valley temple, led into the pyramid complex, and was located on or near a body of water where boats could dock. The other, the funerary (or upper) temple, stood near the base of the pyramid. Priests maintained the mortuary cult of the deceased king in these temples, where his divine aspect was worshiped, and where rich and diverse offerings were presented to his soul so he could have a peaceful and luxurious afterlife.

I stayed at The St. Regis in December 2025 and overall had a very pleasant experience. The room was spotlessly clean, beautifully designed, and offered a lovely view overlooking the pool, which made the stay even more enjoyable. I truly appreciated the welcome note and chocolates upon arrival, as well as the thoughtful complimentary attentions throughout my stay. Small gestures such as fresh juice served in the room and ginger-honey tea when I had a slight cold made a real difference and reflected a genuine sense of care. The breakfast buffet was one of the highlights of my stay. It offered a wide variety of options, catering to different tastes, and the quality was consistently very good.
That said, there were a few aspects that could be improved. It was unfortunate that the reception is located on the 5th floor and this was not clearly communicated upon arrival, as no one informed us. In addition, while the staff was professional, I felt that the welcoming attitude could have been warmer overall. The dining room service was good but not particularly memorable; I have experienced much better in Egypt. Finally, housekeeping was acceptable but not always done to the level of perfection one might expect from a hotel of this standing. Overall, it was a comfortable and enjoyable stay, with many positive elements.

reviews: I visited on a Friday and noticed that much of the crowds that bused through the citadel did not stop for or look at this museum. The palace which houses the collection is vast and highly decorated with hand painted walls, and many ornate features and decorations and beautiful wooden floors. There are many fine paintings detailing the battles of the pharaohs and kings and leaders through the ages. So many things to see and look at and then there are the fighter jets tanks, statues of leaders, guns, etc in the outside spaces....the collection is massive indeed. 1/5 – Deceptive, unfair, and unacceptable experience

I wish I could give it 0 stars.

This hotel operates in a deceptive and unfair manner.

Rehana Plaza Hotel is split into two very different sections: Classic and Standard. The Classic rooms are clearly better and match the photos shown online. The Standard rooms are in old buildings with worn carpets and outdated interiors and look nothing like what is advertised.

Guests who book through Booking.com are given Classic rooms. Guests who book through agencies are automatically downgraded to the old Standard building, even if the online booking shows the Classic accommodation.

Despite our booking reflecting the Classic room, we were placed in the Standard building. Staff admitted Classic rooms are better but claimed none were available for 1–2 days, even though availability was confirmed when we booked.

Management then tried to charge $15 per night extra, later reducing it to $5 per night, on top of what we already paid. The explanations kept changing and contradicted each other.

Two relatives with us were allowed to stay in the Classic rooms for free after making excuses, while others were pressured to pay. When we pointed this out, the manager said she could call them and force them to pay — despite already letting them stay for free. This shows arbitrary decision-making and intimidation.

The room and facilities were poor:

Dirty bedsheets

Old carpets

Exposed boiler and plumbing

Only one toilet paper roll

Weak Wi-Fi that constantly disconnects

Security and organisation were also lacking:

Basic key locks

No wristbands

Security asking for room numbers in lifts

Poorly managed swimming pool

The environment was unpleasant, with loud music every day, smoking in reception, and no enforcement of basic standards.

Overall, this stay felt misleading and exploitative. I would strongly advise others to avoid this hotel.

name: Mustafa Mahmoud Mosque
description:
Mustafa Kamal Mahmoud Hussein (27 December 1921 – 31 October 2009) was an Egyptian doctor, philosopher, and author. Mustafa was born in Shibin el-Kom, Monufia province. He was trained as a doctor, but later chose a career as a journalist and author, traveling and writing on many subjects. He wrote 89 books on science, philosophy, religion, politics, and society as well as plays, tales, and travelogues.
He was known for his popular program Science and Faith. Mustafa founded a mosque, a medical clinic, and a charitable organization which were all named after him.

This place has become a regular family spot. I first tried it about 5 months ago. It was recommended to my family by a Yemeni acquaintance .

The great thing about this spot is that it's always full of Yemenis, which is a great indicator of its authenticity.

I have tried a variety of dishes, chicken, goat, and fish .

My favourite so far has been lahm mandi / lahm madfoun / lahm heneiz as well as shrimp sauce and salmon

Portions : Overall, most of the dishes come in great portions. Yet I would not recommend the singular portion (Nfr) dishes in the meat / goat dishes as the meat ends up in a minute portion when they divide it up . I would recommend the "quarter" (Rba) at least, and it can be shared but still better value for money.

Staff: Are extremely patient and accommodating to non-yemeni clients who have a list of questions trying things for the first time

Ambience:
very lively, and they have a family section for more privacy . And it's very clean.

Recommended dishes:
I have tried these dishes several times;
Lahm mandi Lhm Mndi
Lahm madfoun Lhm Mdfoun
Lahm heneiz Lhm Hniz
- salmon in sauce (not on the menu, but a special order that's available)
- shrimp sauce ( Gmbri Sous)
- grilled fish ( Fish Arbi Moufi)

- I have also tried the chicken(Dgag Shouaia) but I didn't find it flavourful compared to everything else I tried. So if you're going for flavour, I wouldn't recommend it. Most of the other chicken options are boiled in a stew ( I haven't tried them)

- All bread is baked fresh on order, and it comes in a variety of.sizes according to the guests number

- I would recommend trying the tea and desserts section

Parking : I would highly recommend coming with uber, parking here is not always available

reviews:
This is a tricky one. Sizzler is my dear friend’s favourite restaurant. He was excited to bring us there but I was a tad disappointed.

First, we had to wait for our table outside the restaurant. I cannot remember ever having to do that before. I have waited at the bar in the restaurant, I have been given a pager and asked to return when the pager goes off but I have never stood outside on the street waiting for a table.
The first table we sat at was for four people but two men sitting side by side would barely have fitted. It was too small.
The waiter was lacked any charm or professionalism. I asked him (in arabic) to wait for a minute while I chose my food expecting him to leave and come back but instead he hovered over me impatiently.
The restaurant was busy and they just wanted to get us in and out so they could take the next diners. Again, I have never experienced that before. I have eaten at restaurants that have set a time limit for the table which they did when I booked, which was fine. I’ve just never been rushed like that before by the waiters. It was unpleasant.
The food was good but overpriced. Fifteen US dollars for a 180 gram steak, in Egypt, is a tad absurd.
The decor was dated. Rather like a Beefeater restaurant in England in the 1970’s.
I wouldn’t go again.

reviews:
Honestly, the food is excellent and the overall atmosphere is wonderful, but what made me decide to write this review today was the classy and professional service I received from Captain Mariam.

Why is Mariam so special?

Welcome and Greeting: As soon as we entered, she greeted us with a cheerful smile and a very pleasant demeanor, making us feel at home, not just as customers.

Ordering Intelligence: She has an excellent ability to explain the menu and recommend dishes that perfectly suited our tastes, and the choices were absolutely perfect.

Speed ​​and Attention to Detail: Even though the place was busy, she kept an eye on every detail of the table, ensuring we didn't need to order twice.

Professionalism: It's rare to find someone who understands the "principles of hospitality" so well—eloquent, quick-witted, and attentive to the smallest details. Summary:

Bistro Nasr City is always a great choice, but having staff like Mariam is what makes us want to come back again and again. She's a wonderful representative of the restaurant and a perfect example of a successful manager who truly knows how to win over customers.

Thank you, Mariam, for this lovely experience, and thank you to Bistro for their excellent staff selection! 👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻

Amazing Italian food with authentic flavors that truly reminded me of my trip to Italy. The taste was excellent, well-prepared, and clearly made with quality ingredients.

Unfortunately, the service experience did not match the quality of the food. When we first arrived, we were seated at a table, then shortly after the manager asked us to leave it and wait inside, saying we would be given another table. After a long wait, we were finally seated, but at a much worse table. What made this more frustrating is that the original table was later taken by two girls who only pretended to order, took a few photos for social media (including with the restaurant’s famous mirror), and then left.

The situation got worse after we finished our food. We had ordered coffee afterward and were still drinking it, my cup was half full yet the manager told us, “Oh, your coffee is finished, we need the table.”

We understand that the restaurant gets very crowded because of its great reputation, but guests should be treated with more respect and allowed to enjoy what they ordered without feeling rushed. The food is fantastic, but the service and management approach definitely need improvement.

Visiting the Aisha Fahmy Palace was such a unique and memorable experience. The palace itself is stunning, and what makes it even more special is that it houses the belongings and original furniture of the legendary singer Umm Kulthum. Walking through the rooms feels like stepping back in time and getting a glimpse of her life and legacy.

The best part is that entry is completely free, which makes it even more worth visiting. There’s parking nearby, so it’s easy to get to, but keep in mind that the palace closes early—so it’s a good idea to plan your visit earlier in the day.

Its location right on the Nile River makes the experience even better. After exploring the palace, you can enjoy a peaceful walk by the river and take in the beautiful view. Overall, it’s a lovely spot for anyone interested in history, culture, or just spending a calm and enriching day out in Cairo.

description: Ayadina, located in the Nasr City area of Cairo, is a popular restaurant specializing in Lebanese and Levantine fare. reviews:
I had a wonderful dining experience at Adaina today. It was a calm, enjoyable dinner that truly reflected the quality and authenticity of Lebanese cuisine.

We were two guests and started with soups: lentil soup and cream of chicken soup. Both were flavorful, well-balanced, and clearly prepared with care.

For cold appetizers, we ordered Muhammara and Moutabbal. The presentation was very artistic and impressive, but even more importantly, the taste was outstanding—rich, fresh, and genuinely delicious.

The hot appetizer was fried kibbeh, served as five pieces with a garlic-style sauce on the side. While the sauce was not my personal favorite, the kibbeh itself was exceptional. The flavor was deep and comforting, truly transporting you to another place.

For the main courses, we chose:
•	Lebanese Ouzzi parcels stuffed with meat and nuts
•	Mixed grill

The Ouzzi was excellent: tender meat that melted in the mouth, paired with fragrant, well-cooked rice.
The mixed grill included lamb kebab, shish tawook, and shish meat. All were good, but the shish meat stood out the most—perfectly grilled with great texture and flavor.

I would also like to sincerely thank the staff for their warm hospitality and professional service, especially Thomas, our waiter, who paid close attention to our comfort and followed up on every detail throughout the meal.
