reviews:
Compliments to Neama did a wonderful job keeping our room clean and tidy, she spoke a little English and was nice to chat to. Ditto all the staff who were lovely, helpful and organised, especially the head of breakfast service who made sure the vast array of tasty fresh foods never ran out.

We stayed good 7 nights at the Azal.

What we didn't like was the lack of cooling function in the room- we learned that all the rooms were like ours, i.e. with only fan working in the air conditioner unit. We managed fairly OK in February cool-ish weather (21C), but this would be a problem in the heat of summer.

If you like a swim, better bring a wetsuit in winter! Ok, I exaggerate slightly, but to explain: the unheated pool is at basement level in the open air. The height of the hotel building all around it meant that the sun in February never falls on the pool, and so doesn't warm it. Not a great design.

The location outside, is shabby and traffic- choked sometimes, but might improve when the metro extension has finished construction. There was no noise from the works, fortunately.

All in all a good stay, room size large and balcony nice ( ask for a pool view room on a high floor). Thank you again to the kind staff, including the in-house sewing lady who reception put me onto, and she made a repair to my skirt.

This restaurant is the perfect example of why I don't trust online reviews in Egypt. A 4.9 rating? Seriously?!

​The Food:
We ordered 2 seafood soups. They arrived cold. We informed the waiter, who apologized and took them back to be heated. When they returned, guess what? They were still cold. My friend and I gave up and sent them back entirely.
​The butterfly shrimp and the fish were not bad, but definitely below average. You can find much better quality and tastier seafood in many low-key places in Cairo for a fraction of the price.

​The Service:
Unprofessional and inattentive. The restaurant wasn't busy, yet everything we needed arrived late. Meanwhile, groups of 3 or 4 staff members were standing in corners chatting and having fun rather than attending to tables.

​Overall:
A deeply disappointing experience that raises serious questions about their high ratings. There is no way a restaurant like this should be rated above a 3.

It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.7-star rating from 3,101 reviews and standing as a firm favorite that draws steady crowds. Visitors frequently note pleasant views and garden seating. reviews:
It would be desirable to read a bit of history of the monastery and its links to the area it is located in prior to visiting. Perhaps then there would be fewer vile reviews about the people who made this place, and their hard life. We walked through the settlement inhabited by people whose income comes from recycling our garbage. I wish there never existed people forced to do this work. But they do. So, at least show them some respect when passing through the area in which they live and work. The area is very lively, with people walking, working, children playing in the streets. But mostly they are very busy sorting out the recyclables from other garbage, precisely thanks to those among us who do not even care to sort out their trash before dumping it. We never felt any bad smell, possibly this being winter, and the area is actually cleaner than I expected.
The monastery itself is free to visit, but they do have an office for tourism and donations, and they provide a certificate to donors. In Coptic churches it is also customary to give a tip to the person who cleans the church, but most tourists seem disinterested in the actual people there and are just busy posing for photos.
The monastery has a zip line, which is a unique way to visit a monastery. The place is quiet and nice.

Beautiful church inside of a cave there are actually two different churches present in the area. You have to drive through garbage city to get to the church which is an experience itself. I highly recommend getting a private driver to get … More

A very interesting Christian church that is built down into the side of the natural cliffs. Please do not use flash photography inside the church or sit on the metal guardrails (act as if your in a church). No guide is required although one could make your visit more informative and interesting. It is FREE to visit this site. We had no problem getting a taxi when leaving, a driver simply approached us as we were about to look for an Uber and he gave amusement a good price for the ride.

reviews: The hotel overall is pretty good. Very good location, readily accessible to restaurants nearby. Staffs are friendly, and Goog breakfast. The only thing I don’t like is no in-room WiFi. They should improve

Om Kalthoum Hotel – Two Stays, Two Perspectives
Having stayed at Om Kalthoum Hotel on two separate occasions, I was able to get a good sense of what the hotel does well and where expectations should be managed.
During our first stay, we were on the 16th floor in a room without a view, but it was surprisingly spacious and better furnished than expected. The room included a microwave, hairdryer, and a TV on a rotating mount, which made the space feel practical and comfortable. Our second stay was on the 2nd floor with a view. While both rooms clearly showed their age, they were in line with what we’ve come to expect from mid-range hotels in Egypt.
On our late January 2026 visit, it was clear that renovations were actively underway. Several rooms were completely stripped down and being rebuilt, which is a very positive sign. Future guests will likely benefit greatly once this work is completed.
Cleanliness was good overall. One small observation is that the softer, fluffier towels seemed to be reserved for the gym rather than the rooms.
Noise levels were interestingly inconsistent. Street noise was actually worse on the 16th floor. Either we adjusted over time, or the windows on the lower floors offered better insulation.
Wi-Fi was slow and unreliable, making it unsuitable for work or streaming. We relied on mobile data tethering for anything important.
Breakfast was a standout. The selection changed regularly, and the variety was impressive — including items like blue cheese on one morning. This was easily one of the strongest aspects of the stay.
Most of the staff spoke good English, with only one or two exceptions, and everyone was polite and helpful. Pricing, however, felt uneven: the 2nd-floor room with a view didn’t quite justify the higher cost in its current condition.
As with many hotels in Egypt, the hot water was extremely hot, bordering on scalding.
Tips for future guests:
Don’t rely on the Wi-Fi; mobile data works far better.
Lower floors may be quieter than higher ones.
Renovations are ongoing, so conditions should improve.
Ask staff to turn on the power in the gym if needed.
Be cautious with the hot water.
Overall, Om Kalthoum Hotel offers generous room sizes, excellent breakfast, and helpful staff, with clear signs of improvement on the way.

Bab Zuwayla is one of Cairo’s most iconic medieval gates and a remarkable example of Islamic architecture and urban history. Built in the 11th century during the Fatimid period, it originally served as a fortified entrance to the city and part of Cairo’s defensive walls. Today, it stands as a symbol of the city’s rich history and is one of the few remaining gates from the original Fatimid fortifications.

The gate’s architecture is imposing and elegant. Its massive stone towers flank a central passage, and the walls are adorned with decorative crenellations and pointed arches, typical of Fatimid military design. A steep staircase leads to the upper levels, where visitors (or historically, city guards) would have had a panoramic view of the surrounding streets and desert approaches. The elevated terraces were crucial for defense, surveillance, and controlling access to the city.

Bab Zuwayla is also historically significant beyond its defensive role. In medieval times, it served as a site for public executions, making it an important and sometimes grim part of the city’s social history. Nearby markets, mosques, and historic neighborhoods grew around the gate, creating a vibrant urban area that continues to retain much of its old-world charm.

Today, Bab Zuwayla is not just a relic of Cairo’s past but a cultural landmark. It offers insight into medieval Islamic architecture, city planning, and social life. Climbing the gate provides an impressive view of old Cairo, including nearby mosques, bustling streets, and traditional marketplaces. Bab Zuwayla stands as a testament to Cairo’s layered history, blending defensive ingenuity with cultural and urban significance.

everything was beautifully presented on rustic plates. We washed it down with hot tea and coffee, served in simple glassware that complemented the casual elegance.

Reservations are required, especially for peak times, and it’s suitable for all group sizes, from intimate gatherings to larger parties. There’s plenty of parking available in a paid lot, with a fee of 50 EGP.
If you’re looking for a spot where gourmet flavors meet stunning Nile views, Cavo Island is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

We had an absolutely wonderful experience dining here as a party of three my wife, my sister, and I. Everything from the food to the service was exceptional.

Our server Regina was fantastic, friendly, attentive, and genuinely kind. She made great recommendations, checked in at the perfect moments, and ensured our table had everything we needed without ever feeling rushed. Her positive energy really added to the experience!

We ordered vegetable kimbap, steamed and fried beef dumplings, and tteok-bokki, all of which were delicious and beautifully presented. We also had miso soup, wonton soup, and seafood soup, each flavorful and comforting.

For mains, we tried stir-fried chicken noodles, stir-fried mixed noodles, stir-fried beef noodles, and sweet and sour chicken. Every dish was packed with flavor, fresh ingredients, and perfectly cooked noodles. To top it off, the iced peach tea and iced blueberry tea were refreshing and a great balance to the meal.

The portions were generous, the presentation was clean, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. We could tell the kitchen and staff really care about quality and customer satisfaction.

Overall: an excellent dining experience from start to finish. Regina’s service and the consistently great food made this a memorable visit. Highly recommended and we’ll definitely be back en sha’a allah.

We stayed for 3 nights from 7 to 10 December 2025. I gave 3 stars because, for me, cleanliness is the main reason people choose a hotel. Of course, friendliness is important too, but cleanliness is my number one priority.

As a cancer survivor, I have allergies when it comes to reusing sheets. Even in my own home, I must change the pillowcases and bed sheets every day. So when a guest requests a cleaning, it means there is an important reason—even if they cannot explain it fully.

We requested our room to be cleaned, which includes changing the sheets as part of standard procedure. However, the housekeeping staff did not do this. They simply rearranged the sheets and added an extra tissue box and soap, but they did not actually clean the room.

I kept all my belongings inside the cabinet so they would not be disturbed during cleaning, but the staff opened the cabinet even though my private clothing was hanging inside. They were not supposed to open it, and if they needed to, they should have closed it properly afterward.

I gave 3 stars because I do not appreciate being treated as if I am stupid. I left a tip on the first day for the cleaner, what they did is just add tissue box,soap and changed the towels but they didn't clean the room and another tip the next day, the tips were taken, but did not clean the room or even do anything so we had to inform reception to clean the room but also they didn't change the sheets, which was disappointing. On the third day, we had planned to leave a tip again, but due to what happened, we chose not to.

My advice to housekeeping is: do not treat your guests as if they don’t know what is going on. Guests notice everything. We did, however, appreciate the friendly staff at reception and in the breakfast restaurant.

If the housekeeping had taken proper care of our room, I would have given 5 stars. But because cleanliness is my top priority, I rated the hotel 3 stars.

name: Saints Sergius and Bacchus Church
description: 4th-century church believed to be built on the spot where Joseph, Mary & baby Jesus once rested.
address: 264J+G77, Mari Gerges, Kom Ghorab, Old Cairo, Cairo Governorate 4244001
reviews:
ABU SERGA CHURCH - FAITH, HISTORY AND TRADITION CONVERGE HERE

We visited the beautiful Abu Serga Church (also known as the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus) on a weekday evening in January 2026 as part of a large group, and the experience was both peaceful, deeply meaningful and profoundly moving. Located within the historic Coptic Cairo complex, the church immediately conveyed a sense of antiquity and reverence. I learned that it is among the oldest and most sacred Christian sites in Cairo and continues to function as an active place of worship.

Its proximity to other important landmarks—the Hanging Church, Ben Ezra Synagogue, and the Coptic Museum—makes one feel that the entire area is a living tapestry of religious history. What impressed us most was the strong connection to biblical tradition. The belief that this site is associated with the Holy Family’s flight into Egypt, and that they sought refuge here with the infant Jesus, lends the church an extraordinary spiritual depth and meaning. The Church is believed to date back to 4th or 5th century CE, although alterations and changes are believed to have occurred in subsequent times.

Architecturally, Abu Serga reflects the early basilican style typical of Coptic churches. It features a central nave flanked by aisles, marble columns, and a wooden roof resembling the inverted hull of Noah’s Ark—symbolizing salvation. The interiors are simple yet evocative, encouraging quiet reflection. Even during a group visit, the atmosphere remained calm and contemplative. One could sense centuries of devotion embedded in the space. The crypt, situated below the main sanctuary, remains the most sacred part of the church and is a focal point for pilgrims and visitors.
Overall, it was a profoundly enriching visit—one that connected history, faith, and architecture in a way that lingers in memory long after leaving the site. A must visit site when you visit Cairo.

Stepping into Coptic Cairo feels like passing through a portal to the earliest centuries of Christendom. Nestled within the towering stone walls of the Roman Babylon Fortress, the district is a maze of narrow alleyways and quiet courtyards that immediately slow the pulse.

Beyond the stones and mortar, Coptic Cairo is a living testament to Egypt’s role as the "Second Holy Land." To the Coptic faithful, this isn't just a historical site; it is a landscape sanctified by the presence of the Holy Family.
Escaping the decree of King Herod, Jesus, Mary, and Joseph found refuge here. Just steps from St. George’s lies the Church of St. Sergius and Bacchus, which houses the crypt where the Family is said to have rested for three months. This history of hospitality and protection gives the entire district a profound "old world" gravity—it remains a place where the biblical past feels remarkably close to the surface.

Beware: The Bill Doesn’t Match the Menu Prices.

I ordered three dishes:
• Spicy potatoes ($5): so unbearably spicy that they were simply inedible. Truly a terrible dish.
• Salmon carpaccio ($9): at first glance it looked beautiful on a large plate, but the moment I lifted a slice with my fork, I realized the salmon was sliced nearly transparent. The portions were so thin that one piece of salmon on a simple sushi roll would contain more fish than the entire plate.
• Mushroom risotto ($15): the only dish that was acceptable, but still nothing special — very mediocre.

The total for all three items was $29, and the menu showed prices both in local currency and in USD. I received the bill in local currency, paid without double-checking, and left. Only a few days later, when I checked my mobile banking, I discovered that the transaction had been processed as $42.

How $29 turned into $42 remains unclear — whether they added items I didn’t order or included unauthorized charges or tips, I cannot know since I did not take the receipt. What I do know is that this should never happen in a restaurant that respects its customers.

On top of this, the place leaves a very poor impression: dated early-2000s interior, cheap plastic flowers, thick rain plastic sheets, and old-fashioned heavy leather menus that have been considered outdated in the restaurant world for the past twenty years.

Very disappointed. Shameful experience.

Visited in February 2026.
Egypt 🇪🇬, Cairo.

A stylish restaurant located on a boat with beautiful views over Cairo. The interior is designed in a dark, moody tone with an open kitchen, giving it more of an evening lounge or bar atmosphere rather than a traditional restaurant setting.

FOOD:

The cuisine is primarily Italian, offering appetizers, pasta, and main courses. The open kitchen adds a nice visual element to the dining experience.

We started with beef tartare, which was outstanding — delicate, melt-in-the-mouth texture, perfectly balanced seasoning, and excellent meat quality. Easily the highlight of the meal.

The octopus in oil was also very good. It had a slightly spicy sauce, tender tentacles cut into small pieces, and a pleasant grilled aroma and flavor. It was close to being slightly oversalted, but still delivered a bold and enjoyable taste.

The pasta, however, was average. While the dough was smooth and silky, it could have been rolled thinner, and the overall composition felt heavy and somewhat bland.

The shrimp tacos also felt unfinished — essentially just a breaded shrimp inside a tortilla, lacking sauces or brighter flavor elements to elevate the dish.

SERVICE:

Service was good but slightly slow. The restaurant was very busy, and while the staff moved quickly, they didn’t have much time to give personalized attention.

VERDICT:

The restaurant left mixed impressions. It feels more like a lively bar with loud music and decent food rather than a refined dining destination. We were expecting a different atmosphere — it was smoky and noisy inside. For a bar setting, the food quality is good, but for a proper dinner experience, we would likely choose another place.

name: Al Emam El Hussein Mosque
description: Al Emam El Hussein Mosque, located in the El Gamaliya area of Cairo, is an inviting mosque. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.8-star rating from 2,571 reviews and standing as a firm favorite that draws steady crowds. Visitors frequently note outdoor seating and a modern interior. It is typically open 05:00–21:00. It remains a worthwhile stop for both locals and visitors to Cairo.
address: next to Khan El Khlili, Hussein Hgazi, District, El Gamaliya, Cairo Governorate 4331330
reviews:
This mosque and shrine is held by some to house the blessed head of Imam Hussain (as), the grandson of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). He was martyred and beheaded by the Ummayad tyrant Yazid in the battle of Karbala and his head was taken to Damascus.

While most believe that his head is buried with him in Karbala, some local traditions hold that eventually it made its way to Palestine from where it was eventually moved to Cairo to protect it from the Crusader advance. This mosque and shrine was built to house it by the Fatamids. Successive dynasties added their own touches to the structure including the Mamelukes, Ismail Pasha and recent Egyptian governments in collaboration with the Bohras of India who've built a Zarih in the traditional Shia style and outdoor umbrellas similar to those in Madinah.

Regardless of the historicity of the location, the spiritual aura of the place is undeniable and many Egyptians visit the shrine on Fridays. It is an enduring symbol of the attachment of the Egyptians to the Ahl ul Bayt (as).

Mosque of al-Imam al-Husayn is a mosque and mausoleum of Husayn ibn Ali, originally built in 1154, and then later reconstructed in 1874.

It is considered to be one of the holiest Islamic sites in Egypt. Some Shias believe that Husayn's head is buried on the grounds of the mosque where a shrine currently stands.

According to Fatimid tradition, in the year 985, the fifth Fatimid caliph, al-Aziz Billah, located the site of his great-grandfather's head through the office of a contemporary in Baghdad. It remained buried in the Shrine of Husayn's Head in Palestine for approximately 250 years, until 1153. It was "rediscovered" in 1091 at a time when Badr al-Jamali, the vizier and de facto regent under Caliph al-Mustansir, had just reconquered the region for the Fatimid Caliphate. Upon his order, the construction of a new Friday mosque and mashhad (memorial shrine) was initiated at the site.

The building was reconstructed under the Ayyubids in 1237 and was burned down 11 years later. The Ayyubid minaret above the Bal al-Akhdar gate is the only part of the Ayyubid mosque that survives today.

To mark the site of burial, or Mashhad Ra's al-Husayn, Taher Saifuddin had a zarih built in Mumbai, which was later installed at the mosque in 1965 just before his death. It was subsequently inaugurated by his son, Mohammed Burhanuddin.

in 1874, Isma'il Pasha (Khedive Isma'il) reconstructed Al-Hussein mosque inspired by the Gothic Revival Architecture. Wanting to modernize Cairo, Isma'il Pasha created a mosque with Italian Gothic style and Ottoman style minarets. This mixture of various architectural styles famous in Islamic architecture during the khedival time period is called Islamic eclecticism.

Visiting the Al-Hussein Mosque in Cairo was an emotional and profoundly spiritual experience. Nestled in the heart of Islamic Cairo, the mosque holds a special place for Muslims around the world, as it is believed to house the head of Imam … More

reviews:
Brunch & Cake – unfortunately a disappointment

A weekend Friday around 3:00 PM, I spontaneously decided to visit Brunch & Cake with a simple expectation: coffee and cake!

I chose a lemon tartlet and a Cappuccino – a combination that generally works beautifully, as the fresh acidity of lemon can harmonize perfectly with a strong espresso under an airy milk foam.

The lemon tartlet impressed with its bright, citrusy freshness and pleasantly balanced acidity. Unfortunately, the tartlet base could not keep up: it lacked buttery flavor, structure, and depth. With a crisper, more flavorful base, this dessert could have been significantly a highlight.

The cappuccino, however, was the biggest disappointment. It lacked any character of a strong espresso – no depth, no roasted notes, and not even the distinctive aroma one expects from a proper cappuccino. The milk foam was very thin and unstable, almost as if the espresso had simply been topped up with a generous amount of hot milk. There was no sign of creamy- airy microfoam blending harmoniously with a strong espresso.

The ambience is generally a positive aspect: bright, friendly, and inviting, with a modern and understated design. All the more puzzling was the music selection. In the early afternoon, around 3:00 PM, the soundscape felt more like entering a bar than a café meant for a relaxed starting in the weekend with a coffee and cake enjoyment.

Conclusion:
Visually appealing, – but the overall experience, was below my expectations.

The Qasr Al-Nil statues, also known as the beautiful lion statue at the entrance of the bridge over the River Nile in Cairo, are iconic symbols of Egyptian civilization and history. description: Bebo restaurant, located at 24 Ghrnath Egypt New in the Nazih Khalifa area of Cairo, is a well-regarded restaurant. address: 24 Ghrnath Egypt New, intersection of Street Dmshq with, Nazih Khalifa, Cairo Governorate 11737
reviews:
Bebo: A Pricey Lesson in Patience
If you find yourself wandering through the neighborhood looking for a new dining spot, you’ll likely notice Bebo. With its inviting exterior and buzzy atmosphere, it promises an elevated experience. However, after spending an evening there, I found that the reality doesn’t quite match the price tag.
The Food: Reliably Average
Let’s start with the plate. The menu at Bebo reads like a "greatest hits" of modern bistro fare. I opted for the signature pasta and a side of roasted vegetables. While the presentation was Instagram-ready, the flavors were—to put it simply—fine.
There was nothing inherently wrong with the meal, but there was nothing memorable about it either. In a city where culinary competition is fierce, "just okay" usually isn't enough to bring people back for a second visit.
The Service: A Test of Character
The biggest hurdle of the night was the pace. We waited nearly twenty minutes for initial drinks and a significant amount of time between courses. While the staff was polite when they did arrive, the long stretches of empty glasses and uncleared plates made the evening feel much longer than intended. If you’re planning a quick pre-theater meal or have a low threshold for waiting, Bebo might not be the place for you.
The Value Proposition
The most difficult pill to swallow was the bill. Bebo positions itself in a premium price bracket, but the experience felt more like a standard mid-tier eatery.
• Price: Above Average
• Quality: Average
• Efficiency: Below Average
When you’re paying a premium, you aren't just paying for the ingredients; you’re paying for the expertise in the kitchen and the seamlessness of the service. Unfortunately, Bebo is currently missing those marks.

The Yard – El Rehab is honestly one of the best hangout spots in the area and a place I always enjoy visiting. It has a very nice balance between being lively and comfortable, which makes it suitable for all ages. Whether you’re going with family, friends, or even just for a quiet coffee, it works perfectly.
What really makes The Yard special is the variety of restaurants and cafés. You’ll find many different options, from coffee shops and dessert places to restaurants serving full meals. The quality is generally very good, and most places maintain a high standard of food and service. It’s also great that you can easily walk around and choose where to sit without feeling rushed.
The outdoor area is a big plus. The open space, greenery, and clean layout create a relaxing atmosphere, especially in the evening when the weather is nice. It feels safe, well-organized, and family-friendly. Many people come just to enjoy the vibe, not only to eat.
Service in most places is friendly and professional, and the overall management of the area is clearly well done. Parking is available and much more convenient compared to many other crowded places in Cairo, which makes the visit stress-free.
Overall, The Yard El Rehab is a great destination for dining, meeting up, or just spending a pleasant time outside. Highly recommended if you’re in or near El Rehab.

reviews:
**A Masterpiece of Faith and Architecture – Salah Al-Din Mosque**

From the moment I approached the **Salah Al-Din Mosque**, I was struck by its majestic presence. Nestled in the mountain this mosque is not just a place of worship but a breathtaking symbol of Islamic art and serenity.

#### **Architectural Grandeur**
The mosque’s design is a harmonious blend of traditional Islamic architecture and modern elegance. The towering minarets seem to touch the sky, while the intricate calligraphy and geometric patterns adorning the walls are a testament to meticulous craftsmanship. The grand dome, illuminated softly under the sunlight, creates a mesmerizing silhouette against the horizon.

#### **A Sanctuary of Peace**
Stepping inside, I was enveloped by an overwhelming sense of tranquility. The spacious prayer hall, with its soft carpets and elegant chandeliers, invites worshippers to reflect and connect with the Divine. The natural light filtering through the stained-glass windows casts a serene glow, enhancing the spiritual atmosphere.

#### **Impeccable Hospitality**
What truly stood out was the warmth of the community. The staff and volunteers were incredibly welcoming, offering guidance to visitors with smiles and kindness. Whether you’re a local or a traveler, you’ll feel at home here.

#### **A Must-Visit Landmark**
Whether for prayer, contemplation, or simply to admire its beauty, **Salah Al-Din Mosque** is a treasure that leaves a lasting impression. It’s more than a mosque—it’s a haven for the soul and a jewel of Islamic heritage.

A nice touch at the end was the complimentary dessert, where each person received three pieces of sweet treats—a great way to finish the meal!

Overall, I’d rate my experience 9/10, and I will definitely be coming back!

From the moment I walked in, this place immediately stood out as one of the best sushi experiences I’ve had. Everything—from the atmosphere to the food to the service—was absolutely exceptional and made the entire visit memorable.

Atmosphere:
The ambiance is incredible. The restaurant manages to create a perfect balance between being elegant and comfortable. The lighting is warm and inviting, the decor is modern yet tasteful, and everything feels clean and thoughtfully designed. It’s the kind of place where you can relax and truly enjoy your meal without feeling rushed. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, or even for a date night, the environment makes the experience feel special. The layout is also great because it doesn’t feel crowded or chaotic even when the restaurant is busy.

Food:
The sushi itself was outstanding. The quality and freshness of the fish were immediately noticeable, which is obviously the most important part of any sushi restaurant. Every roll was beautifully presented and packed with flavor. The balance between the rice, fish, and toppings was perfect, and nothing felt overwhelming or poorly made. You can tell the chefs really know what they’re doing and take pride in their craft. There was also a great variety of options, which made it easy to try multiple different rolls and flavors. Everything tasted incredibly fresh and well-prepared, and every bite was enjoyable. It’s rare to find a place where every single item you try is consistently delicious, but that was definitely the case here.

Service:
The service was just as impressive as the food. The staff were extremely friendly, attentive, and professional from start to finish. They were quick to help, answer questions, and make sure everything was going well throughout the meal. At the same time, they never felt intrusive or overwhelming. It’s clear that the team here really cares about creating a positive experience for their customers. Little details—like checking in at the right times and being genuinely welcoming—made a big difference.

Overall:
This restaurant truly delivers a complete dining experience. Excellent food, a welcoming atmosphere, and top-tier service all come together to make it a place I would happily return to again and again. If you’re a sushi lover or even just someone looking for a great place to eat, this spot is definitely worth visiting.

Highly recommended. I’ll definitely be coming back!

reviews: There's a ticket to go inside, you can get student discount. Its a small place but holds a big part of history, there are 3 trees, all in one place and the well where the holy family stayed. There's a small parking area right infront of the building, no queues,no crowd.
It was a very peaceful and spiritual experience

The Holy Family spends the most of their travels in Egypt... It embraced the Virgin Mary and her child while soldiers of Herod, King of the Jews (Roman), pursued her with the intention of beheading her child. During their journey, they … More

We visited on a quiet weekday at around 11am, and we were the only group in the site for most of our visit. It was a very peaceful and spiritual experience. The government-managed site is very clean, and has nice restroom facilities. There were no refreshment vendors operating on the day we visited.

Mary’s Tree in al-Matereyyah is an easy 10 minute walk from Cairo Metro (train/subway) station "El-Matarya" on the Green Line (AKA Line #3).

The ticket window and entry gate is at the northwest corner of the facility. As of August 2023, the entry fee for Egyptians is 10 L.E., 60 L.E. for foreigners.

As identified by religious historians, this historical site is one of the 15 locations accommodating the Holy Family in their flight to Egypt – escaping the terrors of Herod -- as mentioned in the second chapter of St. Matthew’s Gospel. A pdf brochure explaining further details regarding the site and the Holy Family’s journey can be downloaded via a QR posted on-site, or by searching for the following terms online: “marytree” and “egymonuments” (via the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism & Antiquities).

If you’re in Cairo and looking for a place that truly captures the magic of the Nile, Garden Cafe is not just a café — it’s an experience.
From the moment you walk in, you feel it. The breeze from the Nile, the soft golden light at sunset reflecting on the water, and the peaceful atmosphere that makes you forget you’re in the middle of a busy city. The location alone deserves five stars — sitting right on the Nile, offering one of the most calming and beautiful views you can find in Cairo.
🍽️ Food – Fresh, Flavorful, and Beautifully Presented
Every dish we ordered was outstanding. The flavors were rich yet balanced, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the presentation was elegant without being overcomplicated. Whether you’re going for a full meal or just light bites, the quality is consistently impressive. You can tell the kitchen takes pride in what they serve.
☕ Drinks – Perfectly Crafted
The drinks were just as memorable. Fresh juices tasted truly natural, coffee was smooth and perfectly brewed, and the mocktails were refreshing and creative. Everything arrived beautifully presented and at the perfect temperature.
🤍 Service – The Real Highlight
What truly made this visit unforgettable was the people.
Nour and Abdullah were exceptionally kind, professional, and welcoming. Their positive energy, attention to detail, and genuine care elevated the entire experience. They were attentive without being intrusive, friendly without being overwhelming — the perfect balance. It’s rare to find service that feels so sincere.
They made us feel valued, comfortable, and genuinely happy to be there.

name: Darb 1718
description: Darb 1718 is an Egyptian contemporary art and culture center located in the Fustat area of Old Cairo. As a registered non-profit, charity organization Darb 1718 seeks to encourage experimentation by supporting new works by emerging artists with particular attention to artistic merit, diversity of media and aesthetic traditions, along with originality of cultural influences. It thereby acts as “a trampoline to advance the burgeoning contemporary art movement in Egypt.” It also aims at presenting local and international contemporary art, archiving artwork and maintaining a comprehensive database of art in Egypt, as well as acting as an educational front through providing workshops, projects and film screenings. The center also aims to engage the local Fustat community through community service and outreach programs.

name: Gayer-Anderson Museum
description: The Gayer-Anderson Museum is an art museum located in Cairo, Egypt. It is situated adjacent to the Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun in the Sayyida Zeinab neighborhood. The building takes its name from Major Robert Grenville Gayer-Anderson Pasha, who resided in the house between 1935 and 1942 with special permission from the Egyptian Government. The museum is noted for being one of examples of 17th-century domestic architecture left in Cairo, and also for its collection of furniture, carpets, curio, and other objects.

Willy's Kitchen is a well-known burger spot in Cairo, with a reputation for serving up some of the city's most satisfying and hearty burgers. It has established itself as a go-to for those who appreciate a classic, no-fuss burger made with quality ingredients.
​The main highlight is, without a doubt, the burgers themselves. They are praised for using high-quality beef that is cooked well, often retaining a nice, juicy texture. Many customers appreciate the generous portion sizes and the variety of options on the menu, which range from classic cheeseburgers to more inventive creations. The toppings are generally fresh, and the buns are soft, holding everything together nicely.
​While the burgers get a lot of positive attention, other aspects of the experience can be mixed. Some reviews mention that the service can be slow during peak hours, and the atmosphere in some branches is simple, geared more towards a quick and casual meal than a sit-down dining experience. The pricing is considered a bit high by some, but most people feel that the quality of the food justifies the cost.
​Overall, Willy's Kitchen is a strong contender in Cairo's burger scene. If you're looking for a solid, flavorful burger that won't disappoint, this place is a great choice. It's a reliable spot for a satisfying meal, especially for those who prioritize a good patty and fresh ingredients.

reviews:
If you are visiting Cairo for the first time and want to stay at a place that is near famous landmarks, look no further. The hotel is situated in downtown Cairo, close to Al Tahrir Square and the old museum. Money exchanger is also at walkable distance. You can see the River Nile from your room window, which looks amazing at night. The Pyramids of Giza are also not very far. It took us around 20–30 minutes and cost about LE 170 via Uber.

Language can be an issue in Egypt, and you may occasionally get scammed by drivers. To avoid this, we preferred to use the hotel’s transportation services. We were provided with affordable transportation for the airport, local tours, and Alexandria. We also had an early checkout, and they were kind enough to allow us extended hours without any extra charge.

description: Hotel Beirut, located at 56 Beirut in the Heliopolis area of Cairo, is an inviting hotel. reviews:
I would have loved to give this place five stars for service and rooms but unfortunately I cannot.

Firstly, I will say all the staff we dealt with were very helpful, friendly and professional. Our floor housekeeper - Tahra - was excellent. Our room was always well done, clean and tidy.

However, there were some issues with the room.
1) three nights in a row the power in our room cut off and my mum and I were waiting 5-10 minutes before someone would come. We asked why this would happen and got several excuses from the switch is just old to it could just be using a blowdryer, which we never did.
2) over two - three nights the tv reception was terrible, constantly cutting off. Once this was resolved the channels were all jumbled and my mum could barely find something she liked to watch.
3) the wifi was very poor and even if you had signal it would be very slow.
4) my mum inspected six rooms before she was able to select one that was clean and liveable. The first room we were in was just dated and had no upgrades. We switched rooms because when my mum checked the bed it was dirty and the sheets were stained.

When we raised these issues on checkout, all we got was an apology no offer for compensation or asking how the hotel could improve.

How can this hotel improve? Invest in upgrading infrastructure like internet, electrical and air conditioning. The air con was very loud and dated. Properly renovating rooms. We had a room that only had the bathroom renovated but the carpet was old and looked worn out. The hotel is very mismatched and it’s as if management does not want to invest in essential upgrades that would make this hotel worthy of 3 stars.

Otherwise, this location is fantastic and in the heart of Heliopolis. Easy access to Roxy and El Korba. 15-20 minute uber to most places within New Cairo. I would consider staying here again if management committed to improvements.

I’d like to share my experience during my stay at the Beirut Hotel in Cairo.

Being originally from Heliopolis, this hotel was my first choice because of its location—and it did not disappoint. It’s within walking distance of everything I needed, and public transportation is close by for getting around the city. It’s truly an excellent spot for anyone wanting to spend quality time in the heart of Heliopolis.

I had the pleasure of meeting the owner, Nadya, who was incredibly kind, sweet, and compassionate. She made me feel completely at home, almost like family. The service throughout my stay was wonderful. Aya, the housekeeper, made sure everything was always clean and tidy. The front desk team was consistently polite and helpful, especially Rames and Laura, who even helped by arranging Uber rides for me. Breakfast each morning was a joy thanks to Hebba, Michael, and Marwen they made me feel like I was dining in my own home. They even surprised me with a special cake on my last day as a birthday gift. Special Thank you to the manager Naveen who is doing an excellent job running and is making sure thing are going smoothly.

The rooms do have some areas that could be improved. The bathrooms are a bit outdated and could benefit from newer towels. However, the room itself was spacious and included a pleasant outdoor patio area.

Overall, I give the hotel 4 out of 5 stars for its location, service, and room. The staff’s warmth and hospitality truly made my 25-day stay enjoyable.

The hospitality when we first entered the restaurant was excellent, and the place itself was very comfortable with attractive décor. Everything was going smoothly until our interaction with the waiter Habashi, and that’s where the problems began.

His greeting was weak, and it was obvious he was in a hurry to take the order and walk away without explaining anything or helping us choose. When we asked him for recommendations, he suggested extremely overpriced dishes, to the point that he recommended a dish for me that cost around 100 dollars. The issue wasn’t the price as much as the fact that it was a 600-gram meat dish… which is an unrealistic portion for one person. The same thing happened with my friend: he asked for a meat recommendation, and the waiter suggested something very expensive that wasn’t even meat.

More mistakes followed: we ordered 8 pieces of sushi, but they brought us 16 and charged us for them. I also received rice that was cold and stale, and when I pointed it out, the waiter tried to convince me it was “normal,” until we insisted on changing it.

After all this, the supervisor came over. He was very respectful, cheerful, and clearly understood what proper hospitality means. His attitude softened a lot of the negative experience.

Unfortunately, after the poor service, the waiter gave us a feedback card and directly asked us to write something positive about him, which felt very inappropriate.

The prices at the restaurant are reasonable, and the upper floor is clean and comfortable. The food itself was good. However, the bathrooms downstairs had a very unpleasant smell.

Overall:
The food and atmosphere were good, and the supervisor was excellent, but the waiter’s service was very poor.
Rating: two stars out of five.

description: Galaxy Cineplex El Maadi, located in the Maadi area of Cairo, is a celebrated entertainment venue. reviews: Worst cinema at all. Chairs are not clean or even comfortable. Even the popcorn from the rest room is not good at all. A new rule must be sit for children to NOT ENTER the cinema as they will make noises. CHILDREN ARE NOT SUPPPOSED TO ENTER THE CINEMA AT ALL.

I had high expectations walking into the VIP cinema experience, but honestly, it didn’t live up to the hype or the price tag. For a ticket that costs significantly more, you expect something truly elevated — but that just wasn’t the case here.

Seating & Screen Position:
The biggest issue? The seats are placed way too far from the screen. You don’t get that immersive feel that makes cinema worth it. It feels more like watching a screen from your living room, not a premium theater. If you’re going to label something VIP, screen placement should be ideal — not distant and disconnected.

VIP “Experience”:
There’s really no actual VIP service. No special treatment, no staff catering to your seat, no exclusive menu, nothing that justifies the word “premium.” It honestly felt like they just slapped a “VIP” label on a regular theater hall and hiked up the price. The whole thing screams money grab.

Comfort:
The chairs were decent — spacious and more comfortable than standard ones — but still not on par with real VIP theaters I’ve been to. No blankets, no pillow, no reclining footrests with adjustable angles. Just big chairs. It’s giving bare minimum.

Final Verdict:
If you’re expecting a luxury cinema experience, this ain’t it. You’re better off picking a regular seat with a better view and saving your money. Unless they seriously upgrade the service and viewing angles, I wouldn’t bother with their VIP option again.

Willow's has been my favourite spot in Arkan for years however I've been visiting Willow's regularly over the past three months, and it has consistently exceeded my expectations. Whether it's breakfast, lunch, dinner, or just a coffee break, Willow’s has quickly become one of my favorite spots in town.

The menu is thoughtfully curated and everything I’ve tried has been nothing short of excellent. Personal favorites include the cheese platter, salmon gravlax sandwich, eggs Benedict with Salmon gravlax, shrimp pasta, and their delicious pizza. The potato cheddar soup is pure comfort in a bowl, and for dessert, the tiramisu is a must-try. Coffee lovers will appreciate their rich brews, Cappucino and the pistachio latte is a unique standout I keep craving.

The service is warm and attentive. The waitstaff are friendly and welcoming, and on occasions when it’s been hard to flag someone down, the manager himself has stepped in with genuine care and efficiency — a rare and appreciated gesture. Even their takeaway packaging reflects the same attention to detail you get when dining in.
Willow’s offers not just great food and drinks, but a consistently pleasant experience that keeps drawing me back. Highly recommended for any time of day.

We went during peak tourist season. Our guide was very knowledgeable and patient. We saw the church that the Holy Family escaped to. We saw the synagogue where the supposed Torah is kept. The Coptic Museum is one of the most important museums in Egypt for those who are deeply interested in exploring the history of the Coptic community and their role in Egyptian civilization throughout the centuries. It is a highly … More

This museum was extremely impressive and well organized. It did a fabulous job of telling the history of the Coptic Christians in Egypt, with tons of information and perspective. The actual artifacts were very impressive, from statutes to textiles to woodworks to manuscripts, some of which were nearly 1500 years old. They did a very good job on this museum, and the ticket price was fair considering what you get. Would definitely recommend
Wait time
Up to 10 min

Visiting here feels less like a museum and more like stepping into a traditional mansion that has been carefully preserved for centuries. The artifacts and the intricate glasswork are truly impressive. Simply breathing in the atmosphere of this place was a pleasure in itself. More

The Coptic Museum provides a thoughtful flow of displays of artifacts that are well lit, clearly marked, and accompanied by helpful information. The facility is clean and cool. There is also an outdoor cantine for refreshments, and restrooms are available. The woodwork and architecture are truly beautiful. There are exquisite textiles, paintings, woodwork, carved stones, scriptural texts, and more.

As non-Egyptian visitors, we paid 280 EP each, which was well worth it. They only received payment by card on the day we visited. We spent about two hours exploring the Museum. We’ve been to Coptic Cairo before, but we’re so glad we included the Coptic Museum this time.

reviews:
The food was okay — nothing too special but decent for a river cruise.
The music and belly dance were fun and lively, though a bit loud at times. It added energy to the night, but if you prefer a quiet dinner, it might feel a little much.

Overall, it was a pleasant evening on the water with great views of the city — especially in October when the weather is cool and the breeze feels just right. The open deck was definitely the best spot to enjoy the skyline and take photos.

If you sit on the second floor, though, be prepared — the smell of gasoline can be quite strong throughout the ride, which takes away from the otherwise relaxing experience.

Still, it’s a nice cruise if you just want to unwind, take in the view, and enjoy a fun, easy dinner by the river. 🌇🚤

The food was pretty average, and the show was entertaining. It's not for everyone. If you're looking to have a good time and don't have an issue with being in a paradoxical situation (women in niqab on the one hand, and dancers clad in … More

I do not recommend the Golden Pharaoh Nile cruise. The experience was far below acceptable standards for any tourist activity.

The food was very poor in quality, badly prepared, and lacked variety. It did not meet even basic expectations, especially for a cruise that markets itself as a premium Nile experience.

Seating was extremely crowded, uncomfortable, and poorly organized. Guests were packed too closely together, which ruined any chance of enjoying the view or relaxing during the cruise.

The staff were cheap in attitude, unfriendly, and unprofessional. There was no sense of hospitality or customer care, and requests were met with indifference rather than assistance.

The entertainment was very low quality and felt cheap and poorly performed. The show lacked energy, professionalism, and authenticity, making it feel more like a rushed afterthought than a proper cultural experience.

Overall, this cruise does not offer good value for money and falls far short of what visitors expect when cruising the Nile. I strongly advise travelers to look for better-managed alternatives with higher standards of service, food, and entertainment.

address: X4GJ+99V, Al Haram, Giza Governorate 3512201
reviews:
WHERE STONE TOUCHES ETERNITY - AN AFTERNOON WITH THE PYRAMID OF KHAFRE

We visited the Pyramid of Khafre on a weekday noon in January 2026 as part of a large group touring Egypt for over a week. Although the interiors were not open to visitors on the day of our visit, the experience of observing this magnificent structure from the outside was deeply memorable and humbling. We spent time sitting in a nearby café, quietly admiring the monument and silently absorbing its timeless presence.

Built around 2550 BCE for Pharaoh Khafre of Egypt’s Fourth Dynasty, this pyramid takes one back more than 4,500 years. While technically shorter than the Great Pyramid of Khufu, it appears taller because it stands on higher ground, giving it an even more commanding visual presence. From a distance, one cannot help but feel dwarfed by its scale and by the weight of history it carries.

The Pyramid of Khafre is among the best-preserved structures on the Giza Plateau. At its summit, remnants of the original smooth limestone casing are still visible. Interestingly, several stones near the top appear dislodged, lending the upper cone a slightly different colour and texture that makes the pyramid instantly recognisable even from afar.

Behind this imposing monument lies the Great Sphinx, believed by many scholars to be associated with Khafre’s funerary complex. Together, they create one of the most iconic archaeological landscapes in the world. Even without entering its interior chambers, the Pyramid of Khafre offers a profound and humbling encounter with ancient engineering brilliance and enduring legacy.

reviews:
We dropped in right around noon. Orangette, at 2 Hassan Sabry Street, just in front of Gezira Sporting Club, is the kind of café that wakes up slowly but stylishly. The sunshine filters through large windows, orange decor glowing, and shaded patio feeling calm yet alive.

We only sampled what we came for: a cappuccino, a café mocha, shisha, and their crème brûlée — and every single one was excellent. The cappuccino was smooth, the mocha rich and balanced, with chocolate and coffee working in harmony. The crème brûlée? Gorgeous: perfect caramel top, creamy custard underneath, exactly the sort of dessert that makes a stop worth it. Shisha added a relaxing layer — well prepared, nice ambiance.

Everything else was secondary to those highlights. The food options felt average in comparison (we didn’t try many), but honestly, with treats like these, and drinks done this well, the experience leaned strongly positive. The service was gracious and unobtrusive, letting us linger without rushing.

If you want a spot in Zamalek for a calm midday escape — great dessert, excellent coffee or mocha, a nice shisha side, and atmosphere that’s relaxing but polished — Orangette still delivers beautifully.

Extremely Poor Service and Dishonest Check-In Experience

This was one of the worst hotel check-in experiences I have had.

The hotel itself is difficult to find, as it is hidden down a narrow alleyway and there are two hotels in the area with almost identical names, which already makes arrival confusing.

When we arrived, the receptionist named Mahmoud was assisting other guests. That in itself was fine, but the way he addressed us when he noticed our group waiting was extremely rude. Instead of a simple greeting or acknowledgment, he told us to go and sit down because he was busy, in a very irritated and dismissive tone. There was no welcome, no politeness, and absolutely no sense of hospitality.

After waiting around 20 minutes, the situation only got worse. Mahmoud initially claimed he could not find our booking. When he finally located it, he insisted that we had only booked one twin room for two people, despite the fact that our reservation clearly showed two twin rooms. We showed the confirmation email, receipts, and booking documentation multiple times. He repeatedly dismissed the evidence and ignored what was right in front of him. His own system screen appeared to show a multi-room booking, yet he continued insisting that only one room existed.

The entire interaction felt incredibly dishonest, almost as if he was trying to pressure us into paying for an additional room that we had already booked and paid for. It was extremely uncomfortable and unprofessional.

Customer service here is essentially non-existent. No greeting, no apology, no attempt to resolve the situation properly—just dismissive behaviour and rudeness.

The building itself also reflects the poor standard of the service. It is old, worn down, and dusty, and feels very neglected. The room was large but extremely barebones, with almost no amenities considering the advertised star rating.

The bathroom is a wet-room style which is fine in theory, but the boiler only produces enough hot water for one shower. If one person takes a normal length shower, the next person will likely be left with cold water.

Another strange rule is that the hotel does not allow visitors in guest rooms, which is unnecessarily restrictive and not something that was clearly communicated beforehand.

Overall, I would strongly recommend avoiding this hotel unless you have absolutely no other option. Between the rude and dismissive reception staff, the suspicious handling of bookings, and the worn-down condition of the building, this stay was a very disappointing experience.

reviews: Super busy place in the heart of Cairo City Centre. Buzzing with services around with access to alot of other interesting places nearby

Lazoughly square is not so interesting by itself. However it's importance may be crucial for some people. It is the location of the Egyptian ministry of justice. Especially, there is an entire floor dedicated to marriage registration of foreign citizens. Those foreign nationals who want to get legally married in Egypt must have their marriage concluded right there, on the fourth floor. The building even has a separate entrance for this purpose. The officers is very friendly and forthcoming. English spoken and very helpful. At times it can be overcrowded. Let's not forget that Egypt is a very populous country of over 100 million inhabitants. Marriage is a pre-condition to cohabitation culturally. To comply with the requirements, applicants must present super-legalised birth certificate, residence permit and in certain cases an exception to marriage with a foreigner obtained at Ramses street 57. Bring also 5 passport-size photos and copies of these documents to be on the safe side.

name: St.Mark Coptic Orthodox Cathedral
description: St.Mark Coptic Orthodox Cathedral, located in the Al Azbakeya area of Cairo, is a celebrated church. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.7-star rating from 1,471 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. Visitors frequently note a calm, quiet setting and an authentic experience. It is typically open 06:00–21:00. It remains a worthwhile stop for both locals and visitors to Cairo.
address: 364X+QGW, El-Qady Path, Al Qebleyah, Al Azbakeya, Cairo Governorate 4320252
reviews:
Saint Mark’s Coptic Orthodox Cathedral in Azbakeya, Cairo, is one of the most important spiritual and historical landmarks of the Coptic Orthodox Church. This cathedral is not just a church, but a living witness to a long history of faith and prayer. It served as the official Papal seat of the Coptic Orthodox Church from 1800 until 1971 ⛪🕊️.
The cathedral was established at the beginning of the 19th century during a crucial period in Coptic history. For more than a century and a half, it was the spiritual and administrative heart of the Church, where patriarchs led the faithful and major ecclesiastical events took place ✝️🙏.
Architecturally and spiritually, the cathedral reflects the authentic Coptic tradition. Its icons, altars, and sacred spaces carry a deep sense of holiness. When you enter, you immediately feel a unique spiritual atmosphere, as if decades of prayers still fill every corner of the church 🌿🔥.
This holy place witnessed countless liturgies, feasts, and major church celebrations led by great patriarchs, priests, and bishops. Because of this rich spiritual heritage, the cathedral holds a special place in the hearts of Copts, not only as a historical site, but as a true house of prayer 💒❤️.
Visiting Saint Mark’s Cathedral in Azbakeya is a spiritual journey through the history of the Church, offering inner peace, reflection, and a deep connection to the roots of the Coptic Orthodox faith ✝️🕊️.

Ok it’s not your Coptic hanging church in the old quarter but as a cathedral church it is beautiful - the quiet reverence of the side prayer chapel with the resting place for the past leaders of the Coptic church is very powerful.

It’s been a while since a restaurant checked every single box for the perfect dining experience, but Tamara did just that—twice! 🌟 My first visit was at their Madinaty branch, and this time, I had the pleasure of trying their Fifth Settlement location. Honestly, this place is *criminally* underrated. From start to finish, both experiences were nothing short of amazing.

Let’s start with the ambiance—cozy, elegant, and inviting. The seating is comfortable, and the interior gives off that warm Lebanese charm. Despite our big, chaotic family group (with lots of kids!), the staff handled everything with such professionalism and grace. 👏

Now, the food—where do I even begin? The mixed appetizers are an absolute must. Skipping them would be a crime because they’re the heart of Lebanese cuisine. A standout? The **4-way hummus**—original, truffle, pesto, and… wait for it… *blueberry*! 🫐 Sounds wild, but it was *divine*. The manaqesh was another winner—soft, fluffy dough with just the right amount of flavor.

For drinks, we tried the **sugarcane smoothie** (qasab 😂) with a twist of vanilla—refreshing and fun! The **mixed grill family platter** was a showstopper—succulent meats, perfectly seasoned, with smoky charred edges and juicy tenderness in every bite. Every dish was generous in portion, making it great for sharing.

Now, the prices—let’s be real, dining out in Egypt has become *expensive*, and Tamara is no exception. Our big group (with kids) ended up paying around 11k, which is steep, but the quality and portions somewhat justify it. Still… ouch. 💸

Overall, Tamara delivers a **truly unique Lebanese experience**—one I can’t wait to relive. Final score? As a tough grader, I rarely give high marks, but this deserves… 🥁🥁🥁

**9.3/10!** ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

name: Catchy Fish & More
description: Catchy Fish & More, located in the Zamalek area of Cairo, is a popular restaurant specializing in fresh seafood and fish dishes. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.8-star rating from 1,461 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. address: Nile Maxim Boat, Omar Al Khayam, Zamalek, Cairo Governorate 11561
reviews:
Visited in February 2026.
Egypt 🇪🇬, Cairo.

A large and spacious restaurant located on a boat with beautiful views over the Nile. The interior is elegant, featuring a large seafood display and a salad bar. The atmosphere feels refined yet relaxed, with a scenic setting that makes the experience even more enjoyable.

FOOD:

There is a wide selection of seafood, including a large display of freshly caught fish, prawns, and other seafood that can be prepared in various ways upon request. In addition to the menu dishes, there is a salad bar included with main orders — offering fresh vegetables, spreads, and sides, all of good quality.

We selected fish and prawns directly from the display and had them grilled. We also ordered several items from the menu. The bisque soup was rich and flavorful, with a pronounced shrimp taste. They add roe, which may not appeal to everyone but adds depth to the dish.

The seafood kofta was not exactly what we expected — rather than grilled patties, they were breaded and slightly oily. Still tasty, but heavier than anticipated. The seafood tagine was more like a stew and didn’t stand out in terms of flavor.

On the other hand, the dynamite shrimp and gyoza were very good, especially the shrimp — the coating was light and crispy. Presentation across all dishes was beautiful and creative. While not every plate was executed perfectly, everything cooked on the grill was flawless.

SERVICE:

Service was excellent. Our waiter, Abdallah, was knowledgeable, attentive, and made us feel truly welcome. He guided us confidently through the menu and ensured everything ran smoothly.

VERDICT:

One of the best seafood restaurants in Cairo. Delicious food, excellent service, and a pleasant atmosphere without unnecessary pretension. Prices are surprisingly reasonable for the quality and location. Highly recommended for seafood lovers visiting Cairo.

description: Arabesque Mall Madinaty, located in the Second New Cairo area of Cairo, is an inviting shopping mall. It is highly rated, holding a 4.4-star rating from 1,428 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. reviews:
The Open Air Mall in Madinaty is a breath of fresh air—literally and figuratively. From the moment you step inside, you’re welcomed by an atmosphere that blends modern retail sophistication with the serenity of open, green spaces. It’s a true lifestyle destination rather than just a place to shop.

What sets this mall apart is its unique design. The open-air concept gives you the feeling of walking through a charming, upscale neighborhood rather than a typical shopping center. The landscaping is beautifully maintained, with wide walkways, fountains, and plenty of shaded seating areas that make it perfect for leisurely strolls or a relaxed day out with family and friends.

The variety of stores is impressive, ranging from global fashion brands and electronics to stylish local boutiques. Dining options are abundant too, offering everything from quick bites to elegant sit-down meals with outdoor seating—ideal for enjoying Egypt’s sunny weather.

It’s also a very family-friendly spot. There’s a vibrant kids’ area, clean facilities, and a strong sense of security, which adds to the peace of mind while shopping or dining.

Whether you’re looking to run errands, catch a movie, sip coffee under the sun, or simply unwind, the Open Air Mall delivers an enjoyable, upscale experience. It’s a standout addition to Madinaty and definitely worth the visit.

Highly recommended! 🌿🛍️

name: Al-Aqmar Mosque
description: The Aqmar Mosque or al-Aqmar Mosque (al-jāmiʿ al-aqmar, lit. 'Moonlit Mosque'), is a mosque located in Cairo, Egypt. Built as a neighborhood mosque by the Fatimid vizier al-Ma'mun al-Bata'ihi in 1125, the mosque is situated on what was once the main avenue and ceremonial heart of Cairo, known today as al-Mu'izz Street, in the immediate neighborhood of the former Fatimid caliphal palaces. The mosque is an important monument of Fatimid architecture and of historic Cairo due to the exceptional decoration of its exterior façade and the innovative design of its floor plan.
address: Al Moez Ldin Allah Al Fatmi, El-Gamaleya, El Gamaliya, Cairo Governorate 4331404
reviews:
Al-Aqmar Mosque is one of Cairo’s most iconic examples of Fatimid-era architecture. Built in the 12th century, the mosque is renowned for its stunning façade, featuring intricate stone carvings, decorative inscriptions, and unique geometric patterns that exemplify Fatimid design.

Inside, the mosque offers a serene and contemplative atmosphere, with beautifully proportioned prayer halls and elegant details that reflect the artistic sophistication of the period. Its central location in historic Cairo makes it accessible for visitors exploring the old city.

Al-Aqmar Mosque is a must-visit for architecture enthusiasts, history buffs, and anyone interested in Islamic art and Cairo’s rich cultural heritage. Its combination of historical significance, craftsmanship, and charm makes it a standout landmark in the city.

reviews:
Went there for a birthday party and it also happened to be their valentines night. Honestly the food is good and service is alright especially if you go with someone they know. We got there at 10 pm and nothing happened before midnight. Then they had a live singer and a belly dancer. Both were good, however the crowd was just not it. Everyone was basically 55+ and there were a lot of much older men with younger women who looked like they were their sugar daddies. No kidding like men in their 70s or 80s with women in their 50s maybe and they definitely didn’t look like they were couples. I was even taking a video of the belly dancer and one woman noticed she might be in the video so she ducked real fast to hide. That only tells me one thing. Also when I got home I had to throw everything in the laundry due to the unbelievable amount of cigarettes that were being smoked in what is basically a basement. The stench was terrible.
Anyway so it’s definitely catered to an older crowd and not the crowd that you would expect at a high end restaurant, especially with their prices.

We were a group of 11 people visiting Coco Restaurant at Alamaza City Center and the experience was excellent.
We ordered a wide variety of items including drinks desserts and main dishes. For desserts we had cookie dough chocolate lava cake and strawberry and raspberry cheesecake. Drinks included peach iced tea orange juice lemon mint blueberry milkshake lotus milkshake and mango peach. For main courses we tried chicken teriyaki pineapple chicken Italiano old style cordon bleu butter Colorado steak and rigatoni stroganoff chicken.
The food was delicious and the portions were more than enough. There is a wide variety on the menu which made it easy for everyone to find something they enjoyed. The drinks were superb and the peach iced tea is highly recommended though all the drinks were very good. Desserts were tasty and high quality and while the selection is small the flavors and presentation were great.
The staff were extremely friendly and professional. Special thanks to Asmaa who managed our large group smoothly and efficiently without any mistakes or delays.
I highly recommend this place for work lunches or dinners group outings and friendly meetups. Definitely worth visiting.

Me and my partner went on the boat cruise over the river Nile with Dahabiya Cairo and what a beautiful experience from start to end. It was our last night and we wanted something special, it was a last minute booking and it was so easy getting it all organized due to the quick response from the Company on the same day, even when we had to advise them on our slight delay arriving at the activity due to the traffic in Cairo we were reassured by them that we would get to the boat somehow with great communication throughout.
The boat is elegant with great design all around that makes it very welcoming. Although there's the option to have drinks only, we opted for the full meal with appetizers, soup and the Surf &Turf as a main as well as dessert. The meal was delicious and cooked perfectly we even gave compliments to the cheff on board. There was a live saxo and drum show that made the cruise more dynamic but we even enjoyed the background music playing throughout. What put the cherry on top was the great service on board, all the crew was friendly, they all help with the delux vibe that characterizes this experience, we loved that the waiter picked on the fact we enjoyed the mango smoothie so much he offered us some more at the end without us asking. This is perfect for a romantic night but I'm sure groups would love it too, it's a 10/10 activity and great value for money, we didn't get any names as it was a bit rushed for us at first but thank you all for treating is so well :) We recommend it 100%!

reviews:
I visited El Borg restaurant recently, and honestly the experience was very disappointing, especially compared to how El Borg used to be in the past.
The fish soup was extremely light, poor, and almost empty, with no real flavor or substance. The seafood pasta was literally empty, containing only three small pieces of shrimp, and it was served without cheese. Overall, the food quality was very bad and not up to the restaurant’s old standards.
We ordered lemonade, but we honestly couldn’t drink it and didn’t even finish it. It didn’t taste like lemonade at all. It’s supposed to be a simple drink, not an invention. Later, we were surprised to find it priced at 150 EGP. Despite that, we paid the bill.
To be fair, the staff were polite and tried their best to satisfy us. After we complained, they took the pasta back and added more cheese and some seafood. They also offered us orange juice instead of the lemonade as a gesture of goodwill.
I’m not saying El Borg is bad compared to other restaurants. I’m saying it’s bad compared to El Borg itself in the past. Unfortunately, we won’t be visiting again.

reviews:
My stay at Egypt Pyramids Inn was truly unforgettable. From the moment I arrived, the staff made me feel like family — warm, welcoming, and always ready to help with anything I needed. They offered great local tips, helped organize my tours, and even arranged an airport pickup that made my arrival stress-free.

The absolute highlight of the stay was the rooftop terrace. Watching the sunrise and sunset over the Pyramids and the Sphinx from the comfort of the hotel was an experience I’ll never forget. It’s hard to imagine a better view anywhere in Giza. Breakfast on the rooftop was also excellent — fresh, delicious, and served with genuine hospitality.

The rooms were clean, comfortable, and air-conditioned, with everything you’d expect for a relaxing stay. The Wi-Fi worked well in most areas, and the location couldn’t be better — just a short walk to the Giza Plateau entrance.

If I had to mention one downside, it would be a bit of street noise at night, which is quite common in Cairo. However, the overall experience more than made up for it.

Egypt Pyramids Inn offers outstanding value for money and a level of personal attention you won’t find in larger hotels. Whether you’re visiting for a night or a week, this place combines comfort, culture, and one of the best views in the world. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Cairo or Giza!

I contacted the hotel in advance via Booking.com chat and WhatsApp to explain that I was unable to travel as planned and asked whether an exceptional cancellation could be considered due to unforeseen circumstances. Communication was limited and unclear, with occasional replies such as “don’t worry my friend,” but without any concrete confirmation.

When my friend called the property on my behalf, the hotel stated verbally that if the room were rebooked, a full refund would be provided; otherwise, a partial refund would be given, which we accepted. However, after the reservation date passed, I received no further response from the hotel.

I then contacted Booking.com customer service and was informed that the property had reported that I behaved offensively toward staff during my stay as we as repeatedly complained about the New Year’s fireworks which was impossible as I never checked in. After I raised this issue, Booking.com confirmed that the hotel had reported the wrong guest. Unfortunately, no apology or clarification was provided by the hotel.

Despite this, the hotel refused to approve the cancellation and did not follow their stated no-show policy regarding a partial refund. Booking.com ultimately had to intervene multiple times to resolve the situation.

An excellent location cannot compensate for misleading communication and failure to honor stated policies. The hotel’s actions demonstrated a lack of accountability and sincerity, making it difficult to trust any assurances provided by their staff.

I am happy to share any relevant messages and records if further clarification is needed.

Step right up, dear reader, and let us whisk you away to a Cairo gem, a venerable stage echoing with laughter: El Rihany Stage. Nestled in the heart of once-glittering Emad El-Deen Street, a testament to Egyptian entertainment's "Golden Age," this theater invokes Naguib el-Rihani, the "Charlie Chaplin of the East."
El Rihany Stage's story is intertwined with Naguib el-Rihani, a comedic genius born in 1889. He built a laughter empire, establishing his troupe here in the late 1910s, collaborating with Badeih Khairy to bring French theatre, tailored with local flavor, to Egyptian audiences. El-Rihani, the "Father of Comedy," created the unforgettable "Kesh Kesh Bey." Though initially drawn to tragedy, fate led him to comedy, gifting Egyptian cinema timeless classics. His genius connected with everyday Egyptians, grounding universal themes in local contexts with humor. He even ventured into musical theatre with Sayed Darweesh.
El Rihany Stage's bricks whisper tales of transformation. Initially the Radio cinema (1932), boasting Cairo's largest screen, it was reimagined as a playhouse in 1922 by Youssef Wahbi. Briefly the Ritz Theater under el-Rihani, he took over in 1934 due to Wahbi's financial woes. This highlights the dynamic entertainment world. The area was a bustling hub with venues like El Dorado café chantant. In 1952, the government fittingly renamed it El Rihany Stage, honoring his legacy.
Today, at 17 Emad El-Deen, El Rihany Stage stands as a charming, if timeworn, testament to its past. Despite time and a post-2011 lull, it hosts performances, proving its enduring appeal with recent productions. While some Cairo theaters faded, El Rihany's survival suggests a dedicated audience and a vital cultural role. Cairo's growing independent theatre scene offers an environment where El Rihany could truly shine.
Imagine grand evenings within its walls. Authenticity clings to the velvet curtains. This is where potential lies. Emad El-Deen Street is reviving, with historical buildings undergoing restoration. El Rihany Stage's structure is an iconic piece of Downtown Cairo's heritage. With thoughtful refurbishment, it could reclaim its position as a premium entertainment destination, aligning with Cairo's historical landmark revival.
El Rihany Stage carries a legacy, forever linked to the "Father of Comedy" in a historic district. Its continued operation is promising. By honoring its charm and embracing modern standards, El Rihany Stage has the potential to once again draw enthusiastic crowds, eager to experience live theatre in a historical setting. The final curtain hasn't fallen; it awaits a new act, ready to rise and shine once more.

reviews:
We are an American couple who were staying in New Cairo for a conference. On our last night in Egypt (a Friday night) we stumbled into Marzipan and our experience couldn't have been better. We were there at a very busy time and the place was packed but we only waited about 10-15 minutes for a nonsmoking table (the least popular)! The waitstaff was very helpful and friendly in spite of being insanely busy. We ordered way too much food because we wanted to try it all! We had been to several dinners (and breakfasts) featuring classic Egyptian food because of the conference, but Marzipan was on an entirely different level. We got the Keshk with chicken and hazelnuts, liver Alex. style, hot vine (grape) leaves, cheese cigars, baked rice with pigeon, and chicken sharkasiya. I also wanted Koshari, but they had run out. Everything was fabulous, and very different from the grilled meats and dips (hummus, etc) we had elsewhere on this trip. We had an interesting dessert, the Marzipan Konafa, which was konafa filled with a melted, mild cheese. Unique and not too sweet. We didn't get the feteer because we had eaten it several times elsewhere, but it was great fun watching the pastry chef stretch the dough. We could not have asked more of our last night in Egypt.

name: Mosque of Sultan al-Muayyad Shaykh
description: The Mosque of Sultan al-Mu'ayyad, is a mosque on al-Mu'izz Street, adjacent to Bab Zuwayla, in Islamic Cairo, Egypt. The complex was built between 1415 and 1421, under the rule of the Mamluk sultan al-Mu'ayyad Shaykh, from whom it takes its name. The complex includes a Friday mosque and two mausoleums, which contained the tomb of al-Mu'ayyad and his family members. The monument replaced a prison which originally stood next to Bab Zuwayla. When originally completed, it also included a madrasa that taught the four madhhabs. The mosque's two minarets are built on top of the older Fatimid-era towers of Bab Zuwayla, a choice unique to this mosque.
