The Mosque of Sultan al-Mu'ayyad is a Mosque in Cairo, Egypt next to Bab Zuwayla built under the rule of sultan Al-Mu'ayyad Sayf ad-Din Shaykh and it’s often described as the pride of the Mamluk architecture during the Circassian Mamluks’ … More

Sultan al-Muayyad Shaykh was a Burgi or Circassian Mamluk who served as sultan between 1412 and 1421. Al-Maqrizi relates that during the reign of Farag ibn Barquq, al-Mu'ayyad, a great intriguer during a time of great intrigues, was captured and thrown into the prison on this site. He suffered terribly from the lice and the fleas, and vowed then that if he ever came to power he would transform the infested prison into a "saintly place for the education of scholars." Once he became sultan, he soon fulfilled his promise, spending some 40,000 dinars on its construction. "Marble was taken from everywhere", relates the 15th century historian al-Taghribirdi, "even from (private) houses and palaces ... The prize of marble in Egypt soon rose to astronomical height for the vast demand and the big dimensions of the mosque. Thus, what regards decoration and the use of marbles, this mosque became the most beautiful ever to be built in Cairo".
Numerous donkeys were occupied for days carrying away loads of bones of the dead found in the prison. Due to the Sultan's lavish endowments, the madrasa became one of the most prominent academic institutions of the 15th century. A large library was collected, and the most eminent scholars of the day filled professorial chairs. the most famous specialist in Quranic exegesis in Egypt, Ibn Hagar al-'Asqalani, was installed as lecturer in Shafi'i jurisprudence.
Finally, there was a great ceremony for its opening, when al-Mu'ayyad and his Mamluk entourage came down from the Citadel. According to reports, the water basin in the middle of the vast courtyard was filled with liquefied sugar and sweets were offered, along with lectures and much ceremony.

name: Qalawun Complex
description:
The Qalawun complex, also known as the Funerary complex of Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun, is a historic religious complex located at Bayn al-Qasrayn on al-Mu'izz street, in Islamic Cairo, Egypt. Built by Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun between 1284 and 1285, the complex is like many other pious complexes and includes a hospital (bimaristan), a madrasa, mausoleum, and mosque.
Despite controversy surrounding its construction, the complex is widely regarded as one of the major monuments of Islamic Cairo and of Mamluk architecture, notable for the size and scope of its contributions to legal scholarship, its charitable operations, and for the richness of its architecture.
address: 27X6+R9P, El-Gamaleya, El Gamaliya, Cairo Governorate 4331154
reviews:
The Qalawun Complex, located on Al-Muizz Street, is one of the most stunning and historically significant landmarks in Islamic Cairo. It represents a remarkable example of Mamluk architecture, with its intricate decorations, elegant design, and powerful sense of history that immediately captures the attention of every visitor.

The place is truly impressive the moment you step inside. You can feel the grandeur of the past in every corner, and the atmosphere carries a deep sense of heritage and reverence. It is one of those sites that naturally makes you pause and admire the craftsmanship and beauty of Islamic art.

However, visiting the complex without a guide or explanation can change the experience significantly. While you will certainly appreciate the visual beauty and feel the historical atmosphere, you may not fully understand the stories behind what you are seeing. Without context, it can feel like just a beautiful monument rather than a deeply meaningful historical site.

That’s why having a guide or even a brief explanation can completely transform the visit. It helps you understand the purpose of each part of the complex, the history behind its construction, and the lives of the people connected to it.

In short, the Qalawun Complex is not just a place to see — it is a place to understand and experience.

I didn’t really enjoy that part — their pushy behavior made it hard to relax and enjoy the stunning architecture at my own pace. You might also be approached by guides outside. Seriously, guys, if I ever need a guide, I’ll just ask ChatGPT.

reviews:
With high expectations based on the many positive reviews, I decided to try this restaurant today. Unfortunately, my experience was quite disappointing.
On the positive side, the restaurant is spacious, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It is nicely furnished and generally clean, which creates a pleasant first impression.
However, the negatives outweighed the positives. The food was served cold, and the portion sizes were only average, not as generous as some reviews suggested. More importantly, the quality of the ingredients was quite poor. The cheese and butter tasted artificial and low-grade, and the beef lacked flavor and had an unpleasant aftertaste. Despite what the menu promised, there were no distinctive spices or anything particularly memorable about the dishes.
Even the French fries were disappointing, dry, clearly reheated, cold, and overly oily, making them inedible.
While the prices are not particularly high, similar or better quality meals can easily be found elsewhere for the same cost. The staff were numerous and generally helpful, but the service felt unorganized, and the uniforms of several staff members did not appear clean, which affected the overall impression.
Overall, the experience was underwhelming. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this place, and I do not plan to return.

Going out Thursday night was a huge mistake. The entire Sodic area was pure chaos. The garage queue was insane. It took me almost 30 minutes just to park.

Then I met my friends and we walked around looking for a place to sit and almost every restaurant was packed.

Finally found a table at Izmir Saray. First time here for me but my friends had been before and liked it. Getting an outdoor table seemed impossible so they seated us indoors until something opened up. The table wasn't clean. We had to ask them to clean it.

One of my friends decided we should follow the waiting strategy. We refused to order anything until we got an outdoor table. Smart pressure tactic. Getting a table for 6 people isn't easy but his strategy worked perfectly. Less than 20 minutes later, we got moved to the upstairs terrace.

Note to self: next time call ahead and book if it's Thursday or weekend.

The outdoor table upstairs also wasn't clean. Had to ask twice for them to clean it properly.

Our server Othman tried really hard to please everyone. He put in huge effort and actually recommended my main dish to me.
I ordered Dana Saslik for 950 EGP. Thin sliced beef with grilled onions, roasted potatoes, and a side dish of your choice: rice, burgul, or fries. I'm on a diet so I complained about the sides. Othman offered to replace it with sautéed vegetables. Great idea right? I asked what's in the sautéed vegetables. Potatoes and beetroots😳 Seriously, which genius designed this menu? Kiss your diet goodbye. Othman saved the day by suggesting mushrooms instead. Thank you Othman.

I didn't like the meat sauce at all. Preferred eating the saslik plain. It was well seasoned, tender, and juicy. Rating it 7/10 because the complete dish together was disappointing.

Here's what really bothered me. Every single salad had loads of sugar. Fruits, raisins, and sweet dressings everywhere. What are you doing to salads? Why?

Looking at the bill, we also ordered Izmir Festive 330 EGP (6/10), looked better than it tasted. Pera Salad 330 EGP (6/10), way too sweet and loaded with raisins and fruit. Sigara Boregi 195 EGP. Mutabel 145 EGP (10/10), the best thing I ate that night, smooth and rich flavor. Karisik Tabagi 145 EGP. Urfa Lahmacun 995 EGP. Tavuk Sis Kebap 275 EGP. Kasarli Kofte 575 EGP (8/10), juicy, filling, and the cheese was oozing out of it.

One friend wasn't hungry and just ordered tea with milk 115 EGP. It took over 40 minutes to arrive. The drinks were nothing to write home about and the juices and water are overpriced.

My friends loved the food. I wasn't impressed. Maybe I was spoiled by better Turkish restaurants, maybe it was the crowd. I don't know.

Trying to leave around midnight was another disaster. There was a super long queue to get out of the garage. The parking attendants were just collecting tokens without charging customers so cars could keep circulating. Despite their efforts, there was horrible congestion. It took me at least 30 minutes to get out of this Sodic garage.

Will I go again? Probably not. There are many other restaurants in Sodic Park I'd like to try first. But after this parking nightmare, I'm not sure if I ever want to go to Sodic Eastown again.

I stayed at Dahab Hostel for several nights and had a great experience overall. The place was very clean, and the staff constantly made sure the bathrooms were well maintained, which I really appreciated. The outdoor area was cozy and had a nice atmosphere, making it a great spot to relax. For the price, it was absolutely worth it.

The rooms were very simple, just a bed and a table, but that was perfectly fine for me since I was only there to sleep. The hostel also tried to organize small activities, like group dinners and outings to different places, which was a nice touch and made it easy to meet other travelers.

The location couldn’t be better, right in the heart of downtown Cairo. The only minor issue was that the elevator didn’t always work, so sometimes I had to walk up and down seven floors.

Another thing to mention is that during the night, people would sometimes sit at the tables right outside the room doors and talk very loudly. I woke up a few times because of the noise. I think it would be helpful for the hostel to introduce a quiet time and for the staff to be stricter about enforcing it.

Despite that, I would definitely stay at Dahab again if I ever return to Cairo. Highly recommend!

We had a wonderful dining experience at Namaste Indian Restaurant in Cairo. From the moment we walked in, the warm hospitality and inviting ambiance set the tone for a great evening. Special shoutout to Mustafa, who took excellent care of us – his service was attentive, friendly, and made the meal all the more enjoyable.

We tried a wide selection of dishes: Chicken Biryani, Bhajias, Mulligatawny Soup, Murgh Tikka, Tarka Dal, Murgh Tikka Masala, Jeera Chawal, Lasooni Naan, and Paneer Kulcha. The flavors were rich, authentic, and beautifully balanced, especially the Murgh Tikka Masala and Lasooni Naan, which stood out as favorites. The bhajias were crispy and flavorful, and the Murgh Tikka was perfectly grilled and well-marinated.

A couple of areas for improvement: the Mulligatawny Soup could have been seasoned a bit more to bring out its full depth of flavor. Also, the rice in both the Chicken Biryani and Jeera Chawal was slightly undercooked, which affected the texture of otherwise well-spiced dishes.

Overall, we had a great experience, and would definitely return for another delicious meal. Namaste offers a lovely taste of India in the heart of Cairo – highly recommended for Indian food lovers!

The Imam Husayn Mausoleum in Cairo is a site of immense religious and historical significance, especially for Shia Muslims. Believed to house the head of Imam Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, this mausoleum is a masterpiece of Islamic art and architecture. Its intricate design features a stunning facade, detailed minarets, and a richly decorated interior, with latticework and Arabic calligraphy that evoke a deep sense of reverence and awe. The atmosphere inside is one of solemnity and devotion, often bustling with pilgrims and visitors who come to pay their respects. This mausoleum is not just a religious landmark but also a cultural treasure, representing the rich history and spiritual depth of Islamic Cairo.

This might be a bit long, but it’s an honest review of our experience. We were really excited to try this place, but the service didn’t meet our expectations.

We didn’t have a reservation, and they told us the wait would be around 1.5 hours — we agreed. But then, people who came after us were being let in before us. We even checked the list to be sure.

At one point, I joked with my friends, saying, “I am not Egyptian,” and suddenly the staff’s behavior changed — but only towards me, not my friends. They apologized and let us in right away.

As for the food, the raw dishes were fresh and clean, especially the salmon tartare — it was amazing! But anything with sauce, Philly cheese, or fried was too heavy, and you could barely taste the seafood. The shrimp dynamite, for example, was just okay — honestly, Bahary does it better in terms of taste and portion.

Overall, I’d rate the food 6.5/10. We sat in the back indoor area, which had very loud music and felt stuffy — I needed some air.

Final score: 7.5/10. I don’t regret going, but I probably wouldn’t rush back.

Tajori is a wonderful spot for anyone looking to experience authentic Egyptian cuisine, The restaurant offers a beautiful oriental atmosphere, with tasteful traditional décor and soft music that perfectly matches the experience.

One of its biggest highlights is the view overlooking the Nile ..

As for the food, the experience was excellent overall. The chicken yogurt fatta was outstanding .. honestly the best fatta I’ve ever had, and highly recommended.

The mixed appetizers platter was generous and very enjoyable; the crispy roqaak was delicious, the mombar was excellent, and the stuffed vegetables " mahshy " were very good. However waraq enab was average.

The eggplant with meat "messakaa " was rich and flavorful, the lentil soup (Adas) was very well prepared,

A special mention goes to the freshly baked bread made in-house with butter warm, flavorful, and absolutely delicious.

Service was another strong point. Mr Saleh, the restaurant manager, is extremely kind, welcoming, and professional, which adds a very personal and pleasant touch to the whole experience.

Overall, I highly recommend Tajori for anyone looking for Egyptian oriental food & peaceful atmosphere .

reviews:
The vibe felt pretty dull, even though the place itself has unique décor and a hidden-gem aesthetic. Unfortunately, the DJs are always the same and play identical sets every event, so you’ll likely want to leave after about 30 minutes. The crowd is mostly underage, which makes it feel more like a high-school event than an adult venue.

On the positive side, the staff and bartenders are friendly and welcoming. However, the food menu is basically just overpriced appetizers. Overall, it’s probably a “go once for the Instagram stories” kind of place, and I don’t see myself returning.. I gave it one star for aesthetic and friendly bartenders nothing more .
I really like this place — the music is always great and the venue itself is super cute. I genuinely enjoy spending time there. … More

The Rec Room: A Speakeasy with Potential but Needs Polishing

Our visit to The Rec Room delivered a mix of memorable moments and room for improvement. The speakeasy concept is well-executed, with an intimate dinner vibe at 8:30 PM, transitioning into a lively party atmosphere by 10:30 PM. It’s a versatile space, though the location is not parking-friendly and isn’t in the nicest part of Maadi.

Food Highlights:
- Royal Shumai: Unfortunately, this dish didn’t impress. The low-grade caviar was unnecessary and messy as the dumplings stuck to the bamboo steamer, with caviar pearls falling off. However, the sauce was a redeeming feature.
- Duck Money Bag: A dish with a nice gingery aftertaste but a strong, overpowering duck flavor that could benefit from better seasoning. The sauce, again, was a standout.
- Shrimp Gyozas: Delicious, though the crimp was too thick, making them overly doughy. A thinner wrapper would elevate the dish.
- Tuna Truffle Roll: The star of the night—so good we ordered it twice. A must-try for sushi lovers.
- Spicy Salmon Roll: Equally enjoyable but very spicy, so best avoided if you have a low spice tolerance.
- Chicken Miso Potstickers: A delightful surprise, with a fantastic miso sauce that complemented the potstickers perfectly.

Drinks:
While the champagne paired well with the food, the sparkling wine was disappointingly flat, leaving us with a less-than-pleasant hangover the next morning. Next time, we’ll explore their cocktail menu.

Service and Management:
The staff was polite but inexperienced, which is understandable for a restaurant that had just opened (we visited two days after its launch). Management was attentive, but several issues stood out: mislabeled menu items (e.g., a truffle Angus ribeye that turned out to be duck), unavailable dishes like the repeated "Chicken Xiao Long Bao," and general disorganization.

Pricing:
The pricing is reasonable for the quality and concept, but the execution of some dishes and the menu itself needs refinement.

Final Thoughts:
Despite the hiccups, we’d return for the atmosphere, the exceptional tuna truffle roll, and to try the cocktails. The Rec Room shows promise, but it needs better staff training, more attention to detail, and improvements in food consistency to become a standout dining destination. For now, it’s a great place to visit early for dinner or later for a lively night out.

reviews:
While the mosque’s architecture is modern, it is thoughtfully designed to accommodate large congregations, particularly for funeral services. The mosque features spacious prayer halls and dedicated areas for both men and women to host condolence gatherings. Its strategic location near the city’s cemeteries makes it a convenient venue for such events.

The mosque is named after the Abu al-Makarem al-Zaghl family, notable figures in Egypt’s textile industry. This naming reflects the family’s contributions to the country’s industrial development and their philanthropic efforts in establishing the mosque.

The Abu al-Makarem al-Zaghl Mosque stands as a testament to modern Islamic architecture serving the community’s needs. Its primary role in hosting funeral prayers and condolence gatherings highlights its importance in Cairo’s social and religious fabric. Whether attending a service or visiting to appreciate its community role, the mosque offers a serene and respectful environment for all.

description: Tree Lounge Pyramids Branch, located at in front of Gate El Sout and El Dou, 9 Abou Al Hool Al Seiahi in the Al Haram area of Cairo, is a celebrated restaurant. reviews:
Service:
I honestly don’t know whether to laugh or cry. Since it was my first day in Egypt, I only had large bills and simply asked the front desk to break them so I could pay for small things. I handed over five 200-EGP bills—basic math: that’s 1000 EGP.
The guy vanished long enough for me to wonder if he went to print the money himself. When he finally returned, he clutched the bills like he was performing a magic trick. Then came the punchline: he claimed he could only exchange one 200-EGP bill into two 100-EGP bills and had to return the rest.But here’s where the “magic” gets impressive:
2×100 + 4×200 magically became 5 bills instead of 6.
And suddenly, according to him, I had only given 800 EGP, not 1000. Truly amazing—David Copperfield would be proud.
If this is their idea of customer service, then yes, I got an unforgettable experience.

Environment:
Sure, you can “see” the pyramids—if you can see through the layers of dust, sand, and whatever else is floating in the air. The surroundings are so dirty that I genuinely wondered if cleanliness is optional here. At night, the place turns into complete darkness, which might be a blessing because at least you can’t see how filthy everything is.

Food:
The food? Let’s just say the highlight was that it was edible. What I ordered and what I got had absolutely nothing in common. Maybe they’re running a guessing-game kitchen. I was starving, so I just gave up and ate it. But wow… what a “culinary adventure.”

Value for Money:
None. Zero. Absolutely no value. Unless you count the life lesson.

Disclaimer: I have not yet tried the one in Paris so therefore I cannot compare it.

It is located in a pretty open mall. We did not make a reservation and got a table immediately (at the same time, my cousin in Paris had to wait for half an hour for the same restaurant before they even opened), this of course made me very happy. The restaurant was decorated in a traditional french way and looked really pretty.

There is an extensive menu for alcohol if you're interested. Appetizers are salad and bread with butter. I disliked the salad a lot as it had a strong taste of vinegar and honey mustard (which I usually love but the taste was too overpowering). However, the bread and butter was delightful. Probably one of the best butter I had in a while, it was creamy and a bit salty. The bread itself was also very soft and light.

As for the steak frites, it was delicious 🥰. The sauce was nice with a bit of peppery taste and the steak was cooked the right way as I had requested. Vittorio’s is a nice little Italian restaurant that I like to go to every once in a while. It is never too crowded and provides a consistent quality of food every time I go. This time, we ordered the Filetto Diana and the Risotto Funghi. We ordered it Medium, and I have to say that Vittorio’s is one of those rare places here in Egypt that doesn’t usually overcook the meat and often serves it as a perfect pink. The meat was tender. The brown mushroom sauce complemented the meat, mashed potatoes, sautéed vegetables AND the risotto really well. The sauce was very rich. It 𝘸𝘢𝘴 a bit salty, but the creaminess of risotto really rounded things out. The risotto came out HOT! The saltiness of the grated parmesan cheese with the umami of the mushroom paired really well together. Finally, disaster struck. I had always wanted to try their Tiramisu, but I never did, so I was determined to try it this time. Big mistake. The tiramisu was, for the lack of a better word, bad. The lady fingers were cakey, the mascarpone cream was dry and it was topped off with what seemed like brown sugar. It lacked a strong coffee flavor, which was disappointing. Overall, I still love this place but I cannot vouch for their desserts.

name: Sapporo Japanese Restaurant
description: Fashionable destination offering Japanese specialties, sushi & cocktails, plus wine.
address: Galae Square, Ad Doqi A, Dokki, Giza Governorate 3750412
reviews:
Authentic Japanese for Traditionalists, but missed the mark for us

If you are looking for authentic Japanese sushi in Cairo, Sapporo is a unique find, though it might not be for everyone. We came here with high expectations, but ultimately left feeling a bit disappointed given the high price point and very “rich” taste.

The Food: For the Purists
This is not your typical "fusion" spot with mayo and fried crusts. The flavors are very traditional—which means the fish is the star of the show.
* Warning: The taste is very "fish-forward." If you aren't a fan of strong, natural seafood flavors, you might struggle here.
* Not Kid-Friendly: This isn't the place for children who love "American-style" sushi rolls. It’s strictly for sushi traditionalists who appreciate raw, simple ingredients.
The Atmosphere & Vibe
The decor is incredibly authentic and feels like a hidden spot in Tokyo. However, the dining room has no windows, which made the space feel a bit claustrophobic and dark for our taste. It lacked the "wow" factor we were hoping for in terms of ambiance.

While we appreciate the dedication to Japanese tradition, the overall experience didn't quite justify the expensive bill. It’s a solid choice if you want a quiet, windowless, and very traditional meal, but for the price, we were hoping for a bit more "spark."

A hidden gem in Cairo! The Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil Museum has an incredible collection of fine art, including works by Van Gogh, Monet, and Renoir. The place is beautifully restored, quiet, and well-organized. a perfect spot for art lovers who want to explore something truly special in the city. More

Very beautiful museum with a fantastic collection of art (primarily French) from the 19th and 20th centuries.

Located in a fine villa, the museum is especially a must visit for everyone who is into French impressionists.

To my understanding, all the pieces of art are coming from a personal collection of Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil and his wife, and it's amazing that they decided to present it to the state of Egypt and make it available for general public.

There's actually a hidden gem in there: apart from the main stairs there's a back one around a very nice vintage lift. Apparently it leads to the top floor — another level full of beautiful art. This wasn't obvious for me — I was just wondering whether I could go up (never seen any other visitors in that part of the museum).

All staff members working there are extremely nice. I would easily give five more stars if I could.

The Church in cairo is a truly remarkable place. Nestled amidst the bustling city, it offers a serene and spiritually uplifting atmosphere. The church's architecture is breathtaking, blending ancient Coptic elements with modern influences. The intricate carvings and vibrant frescoes are a testament to the rich history and artistic heritage of the Coptic Orthodox Church.
Visiting the Church was a deeply moving experience. The atmosphere inside is filled with a sense of peace and tranquility. The prayers and hymns create a harmonious backdrop, enhancing the spiritual experience. The church is well-maintained and clean, reflecting the reverence and care that the community has for this sacred site.
The staff at the Church are incredibly welcoming and helpful. They are knowledgeable about the church's history and traditions, and they are happy to share their insights with visitors. They create a warm and inclusive environment that makes everyone feel comfortable and respected.
Whether you are seeking spiritual solace, cultural enrichment, or simply a moment of quiet reflection, the Church in cairo is a must-visit destination. It is a place where you can connect with your faith, appreciate the beauty of ancient architecture, and experience the warmth of the Coptic Orthodox community.

Olivo is a small Pizza & Bar which I discovered years ago. It’s next to two hotels in the disttict Zamalek of Cairo.

Olivo has two spaces, a dimly lighted indoor space with bar, high tables and chairs sitting and an outdoor space with an outdoor bar, a long bench & chairs. The menu have small plates, salads, pizzas, cakes and dessert options. There is also a wide selection of alcoholic beverages besides soft drinks.

I usually prefer to order pizza and salad and I can attest that they are really successful with pizza. At the first bite you will instantly taste that quality and tasty ingredients are used at Olivo. The taste of the salad could be enhance by using a more delicious x-tra virgin olive oil.

My favorite pizza is '4 Stagioni' with mozzarella, olives, mushroom, artichokes, smoked turkey and olives, which I remove because personally I prefer olives soaked in olive oil to olives soaked in brine.

Judging by the price segment and location next to hotels with international audience the service leaves much to be desired.

Olivo did not leave the impression that customer dialogue, customer service and customer satisfaction were a priority. Yes, taste good, but is it done? I cannot say that there is the 'indispensable' customer communication which is common in the service sector. This approach is unfortunately not available at Olivo, which tells me personally a lot about Olivo's approach to its customers: Come-eat-pay-bye bye 👋🏻

The net prices are already in a higher price level, plus 14% taxes and 12% service,

It is a small, cozy place aimed mainly at international travelers and hotel guests. With this awareness, I recommend that you make your choice pro or contra Olivo.

The main issue with this restaurant is the meat. If you value tender, medium-rare meat with a nicely seared exterior, you will likely be disappointed.

If, however, you are looking for a romantic setting by the Nile, good wine, and a pleasant atmosphere to enjoy with a loved one, this place delivers. The view is excellent, and the staff are attentive and professional. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for the meat.

Despite being a French-origin, meat-focused restaurant (hence the name “Grill”), the meat was consistently overcooked. The waiter kindly replaced the first dish, but the second attempt produced the same result.

This may partly be a cultural preference, as meat in Egypt is often cooked more thoroughly, and the chef was Egyptian. That said, the cut was sliced too thin to achieve a proper medium-rare. Additionally, there were clear signs that the meat had not been brought to room temperature before grilling; it appeared to have been nearly frozen when cooked.

I would not be this critical if the restaurant were casual or moderately priced. However, this is an expensive establishment, and for someone who prioritizes meat quality and preparation, the experience was a disappointment.

If exceptional meat is your priority, this is not the right place. If ambiance, romance, and a beautiful Nile view matter more to you, then it may still be worth visiting.

name: Casa Talia
description: Casa Talia, located in the First Al Sheikh Zayed area of Cairo, is a go-to restaurant. It is highly rated, holding a 4.5-star rating from 865 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. Visitors frequently note outdoor seating, a clean, well-kept space, and friendly service. It is typically open 09:00–00:00. address: Arkan, First Al Sheikh Zayed, Giza Governorate 3242304
reviews:
Casa Talia is truly one of those places that never fails to impress 🤍

We started with the Truffle Fries — thick-cut, homemade potatoes tossed with parmesan, herbs, and just the right amount of truffle oil. Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and incredibly flavorful.

The Brie Garlic Knots were on another level: warm wood-fired garlic bread stuffed with creamy brie, melted mozzarella, and served with marinara sauce. Rich, cheesy, comforting, and absolutely addictive.

The Pepperoni Pizza was perfection — a beautifully baked crust topped with mozzarella and parmesan, generous slices of pepperoni, and fresh basil. Every bite was balanced and delicious.

For drinks, the Mint Lemonade was refreshing and light, the perfect palate cleanser alongside the food.

And then came the highlight: the Apple Crumble Pot, presented as a complimentary welcoming gift. A warm apple cinnamon crumble tart paired with vanilla ice cream and silky vanilla custard — comforting, indulgent, and honestly out of this world.

Beyond the food, the staff are truly the best — welcoming, attentive, and always smiling. The service is consistently amazing.

Casa Talia has been one of my favorite safe go-to places since my first visit in 2022, and to this day it continues to deliver the same high quality and great experience. Highly recommended — it’s a place I always come back to.

This is a review that captures the magic of the Mazhar Botanic Garden.
A Hidden Gem of Botanical Wonders: Mazhar Botanic Garden Exceeds All Expectations
Mazhar Botanic Garden isn't just a garden; it's a sanctuary for the world's most precious and endangered flora. From the moment you step onto the grounds, you're transported to a realm of botanical wonder, where rare and nearly extinct plants from across the globe thrive in meticulously curated spaces.
The garden itself is a masterpiece, a symphony of colors, textures, and scents. The glass gardens, housing a vibrant array of tropical plants, are a testament to the dedication and expertise of the staff. What truly sets Mazhar apart is the depth of knowledge shared. Each plant is accompanied by fascinating scientific facts and explanations, turning a simple stroll into an educational and enriching experience.
But the experience doesn't stop there. The hospitality at Mazhar Botanic Garden is truly exceptional. Guests are treated to a delightful break with delicious mini club sandwiches, delectable sweet desserts, and a choice of coffee, tea, or other hot beverages, along with refreshing mineral water—all provided free.
And if that wasn't enough, at the end of the tour, every visitor is gifted a plant of their choice, a living memento of this extraordinary place. This incredible generosity, coupled with free entrance, free parking, and a free guided tour, makes Mazhar Botanic Garden a truly unique and unparalleled experience.
The passion and dedication of the staff are evident in every detail. They’ve created a haven where conservation, education, and hospitality seamlessly blend. This is more than just a visit; it's an immersion into the beauty and importance of our planet's botanical heritage.
Mazhar Botanic Garden is a must-visit for anyone with a love for nature, a thirst for knowledge, or simply a desire for a truly exceptional experience. It's a testament to the power of passion and a shining example of how we can cherish and protect our natural world. I left feeling inspired, grateful, and with a newfound appreciation for the incredible diversity of plant life. Thank you, Mazhar Botanic Garden, for an unforgettable day!
Key points emphasized in this review:
* Rarity and Diversity: Highlights the rare and nearly extinct plants.
* Educational Value: Emphasizes the scientific facts and explanations.
* Exceptional Hospitality: Details the free food, drinks, and gifts.
* Overall Experience: Captures the feeling of being transported to a special place.
* Value for Money (or Lack Thereof): Stresses the free entrance, parking, and tour.
* Staff Dedication: Acknowledges the passion and expertise of the staff.

This place feels less like somewhere to enjoy a meal and more like a place you come specifically to see the pyramids from here.

Because the hotel is located very close to the pyramids, the grounds are spacious and well maintained, with clean gardens and surroundings.

Being able to sit in this calm setting while looking directly at the pyramids is a special experience that is hard to find anywhere else.

To be honest, it’s better not to have high expectations for the food.

Including the breakfast buffet, this is more about the experience of dining in this location rather than seeking outstanding flavors.

If you rate it purely on food quality, it might not score very high, but the time spent here with the pyramids right in front of you is truly one of a kind.

For that reason, if your main purpose is to enjoy the view and atmosphere, it’s a place that can be very satisfying.

As long as you visit with the mindset of enjoying the scenery rather than the cuisine, it becomes a memorable and unique dining experience.

description: NEV Spa & Wellness CFC, located at Ring Rd in the New Cairo 3 area of Cairo, is an inviting nightlife spot. reviews:
The spa has a convenient location in New Cairo and is easy to reach, but unfortunately, my overall experience didn’t live up to the high price point (over 3,000 EGP for one massage).

Massage experience:
My husband booked me with a masseuse named Daisy, but when I arrived, I was given another masseuse called Apple. No one informed me of the change, and when I asked Apple where Daisy was, she just said she didn’t know. Communication was very difficult as Apple spoke almost no English, which made it hard to explain my needs. Her technique felt very basic and generic—she didn’t adjust to my body or focus on trigger points. The leg and arm massage was okay, but the back massage was poor and felt inexperienced.

Facilities:
The jacuzzi before the massage was fine, but most of the water streams were very weak—only one was strong. There was also a complete lack of guidance or instructions (e.g., where to change, what to bring, where to leave personal items).

Customer service:
When I raised my concern at the reception about being booked with one masseuse and given another, the response was dismissive: “If you told me, I could have changed her.” But I did tell the masseuse, and nothing was done. That’s not the level of service I’d expect at this price.

Overall:
The spa itself shows some wear and tear, the service is not up to standard, and the massage quality didn’t justify the cost. I’ve had much better experiences in Cairo for less. Three stars only because of the convenient location and okay facilities. Otherwise, definitely overpriced.

Absolutely horrible and dirty!
At the end of what I was hoping was going to be a luxurious and rejuvenating experience, I was seriously disappointed and refused to pay the prices they were … More

I booked a last-minute prenatal massage & the booking through WhatsApp was quick and easy, which I appreciated. I payed a total of 2500 for 50 minutes.

The massage itself was pretty good not gonna lie. The therapist was Thai and strong. They provided a pregnancy pillow so i could lay on the side comfortably.

But overall, the experience didn’t feel relaxing the way a spa should. During the massage, the oil bottle kept making an empty pumping sound right next to my ears, which was really annoying. Also the lights were left on the whole time — even after I mentioned it — so I had to cover my eyes myself (usually spas place a small towel on your eyes or dim the lights completely).

The room also needs maintenance. The paint was peeling from humidity (probably from the hammam next door), and I could clearly hear two women chatting in the waiting/relaxation, which is weirdly placed right at the entrance of the massage room area, the entire time. It didn’t feel private or peaceful.

There were also no clear instructions from reception. No one explained the changing process or the robe situation — I had to figure it out myself. After the massage, I wasn’t offered water or tea and wasn’t told what to do next. It just felt unorganized and awkward.

The massage was good, but the overall management, cleanliness, privacy, and attention to detail need improvement.

Went to get a lymphatic drainage massage and Moroccan bath treatment.

The place was very clean and super professional staff. Someone explained the … More

I was really looking forward to a luxurious Moroccan bath experience at Nev Spa, but unfortunately, it was quite disappointing. The bath lacked proper steam, which is essential for softening the skin before exfoliation. Instead of addressing this, the staff insisted it was the “traditional way,” which felt more like an excuse for cutting corners rather than providing high-quality service.

As a result, the treatment felt rushed and ineffective because my skin wasn’t properly prepped. For a spa that markets itself as a luxury experience, I expected much better. On a positive note, the massage was excellent, but it wasn’t enough to make up for my overall disappointment.

If you’re looking for an authentic and well-executed Moroccan bath, this may not be the best place. I wouldn’t return for this service.

The ambiance was peaceful yet vibrant, with the lights of Cairo reflecting on the water and laughter echoing gently through the evening air.

I ordered the Kofta Kabab dish, which came with tender lamb rolls and perfectly cooked vegetables—hearty, flavorful, and authentically Lebanese. The oven-baked bread was fresh and addictive, especially paired with the tasty mini appetizers that kicked things off. We ended with the classic Om Ali dessert, warm and comforting.

Highly recommend for anyone looking to soak in Cairo’s magic while savoring top-tier Lebanese cuisine. Five stars all the way.

name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier
description: Monument to the Unknown Soldier, located in the Nasr City area of Cairo, is a standout landmark. It is highly rated, holding a 4.5-star rating from 818 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. Visitors frequently note a spacious setting and a modern interior. It is typically open Open 24 hours. It remains a worthwhile stop for both locals and visitors to Cairo.
address: 3887+5G4, El-Nasr Rd, Al Estad, Nasr City, Cairo Governorate 4436002
reviews:
The Monument to the Unknown Soldier in Cairo, Egypt, is a striking modern memorial located in Nasr City. Designed by Egyptian artist Sami Rafi and commissioned by former President Anwar Sadat, it was completed in 1975 to honor the Egyptian and Arab soldiers who lost their lives during the October War of 1973 (also known as the Yom Kippur War).
The monument takes the form of a hollow concrete pyramid, standing 25 meters (82 feet) tall with a base width of 14.3 meters. Its pyramid shape deliberately echoes ancient Egyptian architecture while symbolizing eternal remembrance. Four thick pillars support the structure, each inscribed with 71 symbolic names representing ordinary people from every province of Egypt, emphasizing national unity and the shared sacrifice of all citizens.
At the center of the base lies a solid black basalt cube, symbolizing the tomb of the “Unknown Soldier.” No specific remains are buried here; instead, it represents every unidentified hero who fell in battle. The design is simple yet powerful, conveying both strength and solemnity.
In 1981, President Anwar Sadat was assassinated during a military parade and, per his wishes, was laid to rest beneath the monument, making it also his final resting place. Every year on October 6th (Victory Day), Egyptian leaders, military officials, and citizens gather here for official ceremonies, wreath-laying, and guard-changing rituals.
Today, the Monument to the Unknown Soldier stands as a national symbol of courage, sacrifice, and unity. Surrounded by the busy modern city, it remains a quiet, dignified space guarded around the clock, reminding visitors of the high cost of freedom and the enduring memory of those who gave everything for their country.
Here are some powerful photos capturing the monument’s impressive scale and solemn atmosphere:
A perfect blend of ancient inspiration and modern meaning – truly one of Cairo’s most moving landmarks. 🇪🇬🕊️

reviews:
This historic mosque is dedicated to the shrine of Sayyida Sakina bint Hussain (ra), the daughter of Imam Hussain (as) and the great granddaughter of the Holy Prophet (saw). She was martyred in the captivity of Yazid in Damascus after he had the women and children of the Ahl ul Bayt (as) brought there as captives after the tragedy of Karbala.

This is why most traditions hold her as being buried in Damascus. Regardless, this is a very spiritual place that has been built and dedicated to her veneration by both locals and foreign visitors. It's been restored by the government with the help of the Bohra community just like the rest of the sites in Cairo associated with the Ahl ul Bayt (as).

reviews:
Dragon Island Park – Cairo’s Adventure Destination

[Dragon Island Park one of the newest and most exciting outdoor adventure parks in Cairo, located at Cairo Lake in the Fustat area near the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization. It combines adventure sports, family entertainment, and lakeside relaxation in one destination.

🌟 Main Attractions

🚡 Egypt’s Long Zipline

One of the park's biggest highlights is its 250-meter zipline, allowing visitors to fly above Cairo Lake while enjoying panoramic views of the surrounding area.

🧗 High Ropes Adventure Course

The park features 36 obstacle challenges spread across multiple difficulty levels, including suspended bridges, balance beams, cargo nets, and climbing elements suitable for children and adults.

🧱 Climbing Walls

Visitors can test their skills on several climbing walls designed for different experience levels, from beginners to more advanced climbers.

🌊 Floating Trampoline

Dragon Island Park is known for introducing one of Egypt's first floating trampoline experiences on the lake, creating a unique water-based adventure activity.

🚤 Boat Tours

For visitors seeking a calmer experience, the park offers scenic boat rides around Cairo Lake with views of the greenery and waterfront surroundings.

---

📍 Location

The park is located at:

Cairo Lake – Gate 2, Fustat, Cairo, next to the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization and Champions Club.

This makes it easy to combine a visit to the museum with an adventure-filled day at the park.

---

🎟️ Packages

Popular packages include:

Dragon Package – Includes most major activities.

Discover Package – Focused on climbing and high-adrenaline experiences.

VIP Heroes Package – Includes multiple adventure activities plus a boat tour.

---

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Who Is It For?

✅ Families with children
✅ Friends and groups
✅ School trips
✅ Corporate team-building events
✅ Adventure lovers
✅ Tourists looking for unique activities in Cairo

---

⭐ Visitor Experience

Many visitors praise the zipline, climbing activities, lake views, and safety procedures. Reviews frequently mention the friendly staff and enjoyable atmosphere, especially for families and young adventure seekers. Some visitors note that weekends can be crowded and recommend arriving earlier in the day.

Operating Hours:

Organized Trips: 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM

Walk-in Visitors: 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM

name: The Origins
description: The Origins, located in the New Cairo 1 area of Cairo, is a noteworthy restaurant. It is well rated, holding a 4.0-star rating from 701 reviews and standing as a well-established local favorite. Visitors frequently note outdoor seating, a clean, well-kept space, and friendly service. It is known for being affordable and offering good value, and it is typically open 10:00–00:00. All in all, The Origins has earned a loyal following for its food and welcoming setting.
address: Salah El Din Abdel Karim, New Cairo 1, Cairo Governorate 4740302
reviews:
⭐ Rating: -100 stars (if that were even possible)
I am genuinely shocked that a restaurant like The Origins can exist in its current state. If I could give -100 stars or even -10,000 stars, I absolutely would.
Let me start with the food, because that alone deserves a detailed breakdown.
🦆 OVEN-BAKED DUCK (560)
This dish was an absolute disappointment from the first glance to the last bite. The portion size was shockingly small, almost laughable for the price. What arrived on the plate reminded me of the worst kind of school cafeteria food — the kind cooked carelessly, scooped out by a tired lunch lady with zero attention to quality or flavor.
The duck meat tasted cheap, bland, and poorly prepared. The texture was loose and unpleasant, giving the strong impression that the meat was not fresh at all. There was no richness, no depth, no technique — just a sad, simplified version of what duck is supposed to be. For a dish priced at 560, this was frankly insulting.
🍗 SPICY HARISSA WINGS (260)
This dish was even more alarming. The wings were over-fried to the point of being burnt. The outer layer was literally black, not crispy — burnt. At first glance, it was genuinely scary. I honestly thought to myself that this looked like something that could qualify as a Grade 1 carcinogen.
Despite the appearance, I still forced myself to try them. The result? A strong bitter aftertaste, the unmistakable flavor of burnt oil. The sauce on top was beyond terrible — confusing, aggressive, and frankly disgusting. It felt like my taste buds were under attack, as if someone was deliberately trying to punish my tongue and stomach at the same time. Eating this was not enjoyable; it was unsettling.
🍝 DAWOOD PACHA MARINARA (480)
This dish did nothing to redeem the experience. It was bland, uninspired, and completely forgettable. At this point, it felt like a continuation of the same theme: high price, low effort, zero respect for the customer.
🍴 Tableware & Hygiene (Extremely Disturbing)
Now let’s talk about something that truly crossed the line: the cutlery.
Using the utensils at this restaurant was nauseating. The forks and knives had a strong metallic, rusty smell, as if they had not been properly cleaned for a very long time. The cutlery seemed to be left exposed on the tables, and the moment you picked them up, you could smell that unpleasant old metal odor.
It gave me the constant feeling that the utensils were dirty, unhygienic, and poorly maintained. This alone made the entire dining experience feel unsafe and disgusting. No matter how good the food might have been (which it absolutely was not), this level of hygiene failure is unacceptable.
☕ The Only Positive (Barely)
To be fair — and this is the only positive thing I can say — the café environment itself is quite nice if you only come for coffee or drinks. The space is large, relaxed, and visually pleasant. Sitting there with a coffee feels calm and leisurely.
That said, even the drink cups had a strange unpleasant smell, which again raises serious questions about cleanliness.
❌ Final Verdict
Do NOT come here for food. Just don’t.
If you absolutely must visit The Origins, limit yourself to coffee or basic drinks — and even then, be cautious.
Between the terrible food quality, burnt and bitter dishes, questionable hygiene, and the audacity to add 30% service and tax, this place feels like a complete scam. The more I think about it, the angrier I get.
I will never return, and I would never recommend this restaurant to anyone. This experience was not just disappointing — it was genuinely upsetting.

Hygiene Concerns: Cleanliness has been a concern for some visitors. A reviewer observed flies in the dining area and described the restrooms as unclean and unpleasant. Additionally, they reported unauthorized items added to their bill, raising questions about the establishment's integrity.

Portion Sizes and Pricing: Several patrons felt that the portion sizes were small relative to the prices charged. One diner commented that both the food and bread portions were insufficient, requiring additional orders to feel satisfied, which increased the overall cost.

These accounts suggest that while Maharaja Indian Restaurant has its strengths, there are areas that require attention to enhance the overall dining experience.

For such a global brand, this was a really frustrating and unprofessional experience. Definitely not what I would expect from Burger King.

They have lots of pizza, burger, sandwich, salad, and feteer options. I will have to try their dessert in the future. The burger had multiple types of meat in it and a pepper slice. The burger came with fries. It was really good. I wish they had mustard for the fries. They had ketchup, but I don't like ketchup very much. The smoothie was also good.

My meal cost £109 EGP, including VAT and service charge. Their credit card machine wasn't working, but I had cash. The manager, who was the only one who spoke English, apologized about the credit card machine and asked me how the food was.

The beanbags are comfortable, but the table is really low, making it awkward to eat at. It does, however, make it feel like a retro gaming den. So, maybe comfort can be sacrificed for the theme. At midday (in August) it's fairly hot, but I was in the shade.

Edit: the place has gone downhill since the launch. Service is slow. They recently started offering hookah, which I imagine is meant to increase business. I was in the elevator with a waiter and he was smoking in the elevator! I won't go there again.

Review for Booking.com
My stay at this hotel was nothing short of exceptional. Nestled in Cairo’s vibrant Dokki district, the location is a colorful blend of lively streets, colonial architecture, and embassies, just a 3-minute walk to Dokki Metro and a pleasant 10-minute stroll to Zamalek. The neighborhood buzzes with street food stalls, cozy restaurants, coffee shops, juice bars, and bakeries, making evening walks to the Nile River a delight. While Dokki’s main street can be noisy, as is typical in Cairo, the hotel’s soundproofing ensures a peaceful retreat.
My room was spacious (over 40 sqm), thoughtfully designed, and equipped with a fridge (a must in Cairo’s heat) and all essential amenities. For two weeks, it felt like a comfortable home away from home. The staff was warm, professional, and always ready to assist, adding a personal touch to the experience. Daily complimentary water, coffee, tea, and sugar were thoughtful gestures.
As a frequent global traveler, I value hotels that blend high standards with local charm, and this hotel delivers exactly that. Its convenient location (paired with Cairo’s efficient Uber service) and outstanding quality far exceeded expectations for the price. I’m already looking forward to returning to Cairo and staying here again—my perfect temporary home in the city.
Highly recommended!

City View Hotel, Cairo — Excellent Value for Solo Travellers

I stayed two nights at City View Hotel, after spending a few nights at a five-star property in the Nasr City area. Having experienced both, I can say City View offers far greater value for money — at nearly one-third the price.

The hotel’s location is unbeatable: right in the heart of downtown Cairo, directly opposite the Egyptian Museum, with the Sadat Metro Station just a short walk away. Coptic Cairo lies about 3 km to the south, and Khan el-Khalili Bazaar around 3 km to the northeast. It’s easy to explore during the day, return to rest, and head out again in the evening. The Nile is just across the road, and rooms on the west side offer a lovely view of it.

The rooms are modest but comfortable, with everything a tired traveller needs to rest and recover. The hot-water shower works perfectly, and the complimentary breakfast is a fixed set menu (see photo). Several cafés nearby serve excellent sandwiches and coffee.

Overall, City View Hotel is a clean, convenient, and well-run budget option that delivers more than it promises. I would happily stay here again on my next visit to Cairo.

description: Also called Aqsunqur, this 1300s structure features a mausoleum, courtyard & a blue-tiled interior.
address: 25 Abd El-Hameed Mahmoud, El-Darb El-Ahmar, Al-Darb Al-Ahmar, Cairo Governorate 4292401
reviews:
The Aqsunqur Mosque, also known as the Blue Mosque or the Mosque of Ibrahim Agha, is one of the nicest and most unique mosques of Cairo.

The mosque was completed in 1347 on the orders of the emir Shams ad-Din Aqsunqur during the reign of the Mamluk sultan, al-Muzaffar Hajji. Aqsunqur was the son-in-law of former sultan an-Nasir Muhammad and one of the more prominent emirs of the latter's court. Aqsunqur's influence in the affairs of the sultanate grew during the reign of an-Nasir's successors following his death in 1340.

Medieval Muslim historian al-Maqrizi noted Aqsunqur supervised the entire project and also participated in its actual construction. Being the former governor of Tripoli, he had the mosque built in a Syrian architectural style.

It was built around the late sultan al-Ashraf Kujuk's mausoleum which had been constructed previously in 1341. The mausoleum's incorporation within the mosque accounts for the irregularity of the building's structure. Aqsunqur's grave is also located in the mosque complex along with those of his sons.

By the 15th century the Aqsunqur Mosque was reportedly in poor shape due to the loss of waqf funds from Syria. In 1412 an ablution fountain was built in the center of the courtyard by the Mamluk emir Tughan. Because funding was low, the Aqsunqur Mosque was used only for Friday prayers and religious holidays.

Between 1652 and 1654, during Ottoman rule, the emir Ibrahim Agha al-Mustahfizan, who was a general of the Janissaries, began a major renovation project for the Aqsunqur Mosque, restoring its roof and arcades, and adding columns to support the mosque's southern prayer hall. Significantly, he decorated the building with blue and green tiles, hence the mosque's unofficial name as the "Blue Mosque". The tiles, which were imported from Constantinople and Damascus, were crafted in the Iznik style with floral motifs such as cypress trees and vases holding tulips.

The Aqsunqur Mosque, commonly called the Blue Mosque, is a historic mosque located in Cairo’s old district of Islamic Cairo. It was originally built in 1347 during the Mamluk era under Sultan Aqsunqur, a Circassian mamluk ruler. The mosque gained its nickname “Blue Mosque” because of the stunning blue Iznik-style tiles that decorate its interior walls and domes, which were added during Ottoman renovations in the 17th century.

The mosque’s architecture is a beautiful blend of Mamluk and Ottoman influences, featuring intricate tile work, carved wooden doors, and a peaceful courtyard. Despite periods of neglect and damage over centuries, recent restoration efforts have preserved much of its historic beauty. The Aqsunqur Mosque remains an active place of worship and a treasured cultural landmark, attracting visitors interested in Islamic art and history.

description: Valley Temple of Khafre, located in the Al Haram area of Cairo, is a standout landmark. reviews:
BEFORE THE GREAT SPHINX - A WALK THROUGH KHAFRE'S TIMELESS VALLEY TEMPLE

We visited the Valley Temple of Khafre while exploring the pyramids of Giza as part of a large group touring Egypt in January 2026. The experience was both humbling and intellectually enriching, offering a deeper understanding of ancient Egyptian funerary traditions and architectural mastery.
Dating back to around 2500 BCE, this temple forms an integral part of Pharaoh Khafre’s funerary complex. It is widely believed to have been used for purification and mummification rituals prior to burial, making the entire complex essentially a grand mortuary and ceremonial centre. Constructed with massive limestone blocks and lined with polished red granite, the temple stands as a remarkable testimony to the engineering skills and cultural traditions of ancient Egypt.

Inside, we walked through large halls supported by imposing pillars and simple yet majestic architectural lines. The temple once housed numerous statues of Khafre, including the famous diorite statues discovered here, some of which are now preserved in museums. Because the structure remained buried under desert sands for centuries, large parts of it have survived and are in a relatively intact condition.

The interiors can be crowded, and one may not always fully appreciate the wall surfaces and structural details unless sufficient time is spent. It ideally requires at least half an hour to walk through and absorb the atmosphere. Emerging from the temple and proceeding towards the Great Sphinx adds to the dramatic effect, making this visit an unforgettable journey into Egypt’s distant past.

The Valley Temple of Khafre is such an underrated part of the Giza Plateau - and absolutely worth visiting while you’re at the Pyramids. It’s incredible how well preserved it is, with the massive granite and limestone blocks still perfectly fitted together after thousands of years.

Standing inside the temple, knowing it was used for the mummification rituals of King Khafre, is such a surreal experience. Our guide explained how it connects directly to the Sphinx, which made everything come to life.

A short walk or shuttle ride from the main pyramid area - definitely add it to your visit if you want a more peaceful, less crowded glimpse of ancient Egyptian architecture.

Beyond its religious significance, St. Mary Church contributes to the neighborhood’s identity, serving as a focal point for social gatherings and cultural celebrations.

reviews:
Cairopolitan is a really nice store with a strong Cairo identity. They feature a great selection of Cairo-inspired, artist-designed posters, coasters, stickers, and T-shirts, with designs in both Arabic and English. The aesthetic is creative, modern, and clearly well thought out.

The quality of the products is excellent—especially the T-shirts—and the overall store experience is pleasant. Even the scent of the shop adds to the atmosphere.

The only downside is the pricing. The items are on the expensive side, and it adds up quickly. I bought two T-shirts and a few stickers, and it was definitely more than I expected to spend.

That said, if you appreciate original design, high-quality materials, and a contemporary Cairo vibe, it’s a great store and worth visiting.

Cool shop, very nice pieces, not your typical souvier shop. Well thought out. Bought some really nice cards, tshirt.and intend to buy some posters. Love the poster exhibition downstairs, they have an amazing collection, think this was their … More

A cute little place that sells post cards, and unique posters with Egyptian themes. They also a renal selection of t-shirts with unique Egyptian themes. Their posters are displayed in a gallery with the artist names. Prices are on the high side.

Very cute spot! The staff are angels!! They helped me out with an emergency without asking twice. The place itself is very clean and well-kempt, with some of the most unique pieces of egyptian culture and folklore enspired merchandise. My favorite has to be the dad slipper rug! Their apparel and prints are very unique and cute and their totes are sturdy and spacious. Definitely worth a visit! At first I was a bit shocked by prices but I learned all of the designs belong to real artists that get their commission for it so it makes sense. Overall a very cute shop with decent variety and very sweet staff! They also feed the strays which earned them a special place in my heart. If you're in garden city I highly recommend dropping by!

A Hidden Gem Beside the Giants! The Pyramids of the Queens may be smaller than the famous ones of the kings, but they’re just as fascinating in their own way. Tucked near the Great Pyramid, these elegant structures were built for the wives and mothers of pharaohs, offering a more intimate glimpse into ancient royal life.

The site is usually quieter, which makes it perfect for exploring without the crowds. You can really appreciate the craftsmanship and the sense of history, all while enjoying a peaceful moment in the shadow of the great pyramids. A must-visit for history lovers looking beyond the main attractions.

We visited Maze Roof Restaurant in Giza and it honestly became one of the highlights of our trip. The rooftop atmosphere is exactly what you want after a long day around the pyramids — relaxed, open air, and a perfect place to unwind at night.

We had shisha (hookah) and drinks, and both were excellent. The shisha was smooth, fresh, and lasted a long time without getting harsh, which tells you they actually prepare it properly and don’t rush guests. The drinks were also very good and reasonably priced for a rooftop spot in a tourist area.

Service really stood out. Saler took great care of us all evening — attentive without hovering and always making sure we were comfortable. Muhammad also checked on us and made sure everything came out right. They were friendly, patient, and welcoming, which made the experience feel genuine and not like a tourist trap.

If you’re visiting the pyramids or staying in Giza and want a relaxed night with a great view, good hookah, and welcoming service, I’d absolutely recommend Maze Roof Restaurant. We would come back again without hesitation.

description: City Palace Hotel, located in the Qadadar Street area of Cairo, is a well-regarded hotel. reviews:
We reserved a room via Agoda in this hotel (City Palace Hotel). When we arrived here, they told us that the hotel is overbooked and that they would transfer us to another hotel named „Tahrir View Hotel“ (owned by the same owner) just a few minutes walk away from this hotel. It turns out that they own four or five hotels in this area and, as far as I can tell from reading other reviews about this hotel, they seem to do this transfer thing on a regular basis. It is not that we would not have been willing to transfer to the other hotel, but it was the overall attitude and kind of communication that was infuriating and upsetting.
First of all, since we were not able to stay at the hotel we booked, we asked for some kind of compensation. When I asked them to lower the price, they answered that we would have to cancel the original reservation and make a new one (at the new hotel) in order to get a discount. Then when I tried to cancel the original reservation, obviously it was too late, as Agoda, or really any booking service for that matter, reasonably charges 50% of the price as a cancellation fee, when trying to cancel on the day of arrival. Accordingly, we were not able to cancel the reservation ourselves. The owner, who then was called and came to „help“ us, offered he contact someone to cancel the reservation with no fee. At that point, they have told us so many contradicting things that we could not believe that he would actually be able to cancel the reservation for free and so we tried further to get a discount on the original price, as that was the only appropriate compensation imaginable and realistic. However, the owner did not seem to be listening at all. He told us the same things over and over again, sometimes even contradicting himself, and foremost, he did not in the slightest appear to be sorry or even just apologize to us for the inconveniences. Again, this would not have been a big problem if they were actually offering to help us and be truly sorry about the overbooking. Clearly the overbooking is their fault. They do this on purpose and do not care about their guests. They even seemed to be enjoying themselves arguing with us, making stupid jokes from time to time. To tell the end of the story, we took the offer and stayed at the new hotel (for the same price!!) because it was already past 10 p.m. and we were tired, both of walking and arguing.

If you just want a cheap place to stay without caring much about the people there or the hospitality they bring towards you, I can recommend this hotel. However, if you expect the slightest bit of kindness (and not just the shallow one they show on the outside), then I would recommend not staying at any of the hotels owned by this owner, meaning the City Palace Hotel, the Tahrir View Hotel and Panorama New City Hotel (these are the hotels I know they own for sure).

The Al-Nasser Mohammed Ibn Kalawoun Mosque is an incredibly old and fascinating piece of history in Cairo. reviews: Sam is a legend. Great service and superb atmosphere. V gd red wine selection. Balcony at sunset superb.

Magra El Oyoun Aqueduct (Fum al-Khalig) is a historic waterway in Cairo, reflecting the city’s ancient engineering and urban planning. The aqueduct was designed to channel and manage water flow, showcasing the ingenuity and technical skill of its builders.

Visitors can appreciate the functional design, structural details, and the role of such waterways in supporting Cairo’s historical urban life. The aqueduct also offers insight into the city’s development and the importance of water management in Islamic architecture and urban planning.

Though less frequented by tourists, Magra El Oyoun Aqueduct is a fascinating site for history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and anyone interested in Cairo’s engineering heritage. Its combination of functionality and historical significance makes it a unique stop for those exploring the city’s hidden gems.
Huge history in Egypt, it was built to bring water from the river Nile to the cetedle of Mohamed Ali Basha More

The river of El-Oyoun.. One of the most important landmarks of Islamic Cairo, it was built with the aim of extending the Citadel of Salah al-Din with water by raising the waters of the Nile with streams to the course of the wall, so that the water flows until it reaches the citadel. The citadel was the seat of government in Egypt since the Ayyubid era Abdeen Palace The wall of Majri al-Ayoun is considered an ancient archaeological area and enjoys a great historical and geographical position. The wall consists of a tower called the “Al-Maqsad” tower, in which there are six driveways, and divided into contracts known as “the drives of the drivers,” and it bears the water canal above which is called “a stream.” El-Ayoun" The wall of the stream of El-Ayoun is known as "Water Aqueduct", and these aqueducts were built by Sultan Al-Nasir Salah El-Din Youssef Ibn Ayyub.

This was a disappointing and uncomfortable experience overall, and I strongly do not recommend it.

The most serious concern was the lack of staff training and professionalism when dealing with children. One employee touched my child without permission and removed her socks, which is completely unacceptable. This teaches children that it is okay for strangers to remove their clothing, a dangerous message. In another incident, my child fell and hit her head because a group of staff members were standing in a narrow hallway, chatting and blocking the way. Yes, it was an accident, but it happened due to carelessness and lack of awareness.

The staff also don’t seem to understand that the fun for kids is in the process, not just the outcome. For example, during the pizzamaking activity, the employee was clearly rushing to get it done and into the oven instead of letting the children enjoy making it at their own pace completely missing the point of hands on learning and play.

The space itself is much smaller than expected. There are only around seven small tables where kids can play with blocks, sand, and other materials but the quality and quantity of those materials are very poor. The blocks are very few, the sand-like substance (similar to kinetic sand or Play-Doh) is low quality and barely enough, and the tools to shape it are limited to around five or six. Kids get bored quickly because there’s just not enough to engage them.

The ball pit structure, the main play area, is also disappointing. The ball pit is very shallow—only two to three layers of balls. Unlike other play centers where children can safely jump and play in deeper pits, this one feels unsafe. If a child jumps in, there is a real risk of injury due to the lack of cushioning.

They do have another area for kids above 110 cm, but we weren’t allowed to try it, so my review focuses on the area for children under 110 cm.

Overall, this was a one-time visit for us. It was not fun, not safe, and definitely not worth the price. We paid around 400 EGP, and even if your child finishes early, there is no refund or flexibility; you are locked into a two-hour slot. For comparison, Kid's Station offers far more games, better quality, and a more enjoyable experience for only around 150 EGP.

To make matters worse, the toilets smelled very bad, unacceptable in a place meant for families and children.

I even tried to speak with someone in charge to share my feedback, but it was clear they weren’t interested. The staff made no effort to connect me with the owner or anyone with authority, which makes me feel like they’re already aware of these issues but simply choose to ignore them.

I would never visit again and I don't recommend it.

I would recommend Jewel Zamalek to anyone visiting Cairo who wants a spacious room, a great location, and warm Egyptian hospitality.

This experience was subpar and not reflective of the service the Ritz-Carlton is known for—or the standard that has been highlighted in countless case studies. I am highly disappointed, and management should address this with their staff.

At check-in, we informed the staff that we were celebrating our anniversary, requested a window seat, and planned to arrive at 7:00 PM. We were told that the window tables were reserved and that we could be seated elsewhere. We then spoke with the concierge and asked them to speak with the restaurant staff, as I am a Titanium and Lifetime Platinum member with Marriott. The concierge informed us that the restaurant does not reserve seats and that if we arrived first, we should be able to sit by the window.

Based on this information, we adjusted our plans and arrived at 6:00 PM. Despite this, the service we received was noticeably inferior compared to the gentleman seated alone nearby. His beer was refilled frequently, and staff regularly checked on him. We did not receive the same attention; my glass sat empty, and I had to ask for another drink.

At the end of our meal, we waited 10–15 minutes for the check to be brought to our table. At that time, there were still very few guests in the restaurant, and it was largely empty, so there was no apparent reason for the slow service.

Additionally, our anniversary was never acknowledged, despite us clearly stating the reason for our visit. You will not have another opportunity to make this right. For reasons that remain unclear, there was a clear difference in the level of service we received, which was disappointing and unacceptable at an establishment of this caliber.

Valencia Restaurant: A Downtown Gem for Burger Lovers
Valencia Restaurant in downtown Cairo is a true hidden gem for burger enthusiasts. From the moment I stepped inside, The service was incredibly friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.
But the real stars of the show are undoubtedly the burgers. I opted for the classic beef burger, and it was cooked to perfection – juicy, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The accompanying fries were crispy and golden brown, and the onion rings were perfectly battered and delightfully crunchy.
What truly sets Valencia apart is the quality of its ingredients. You can taste the freshness in every bite. The beef was high-quality, and the buns were soft and perfectly toasted.
Overall:
Valencia Restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving a delicious and satisfying burger experience in downtown Cairo. The friendly service and exceptional food quality make it a standout choice.
Highly recommended! And don't forget to order Hell Fries Sauce it's not that much it's very light spicy but it will add more delicious taste to your meal 😋

reviews:
All Saints' Cathedral, Cairo was consecrated in 1988 and is the home of the Episcopal/Anglican Diocese of Egypt with North Africa and the Horn of Africa.

The cathedral compound also houses the Diocesan and Bishop's offices and projects and services – including the Diocese NGO EpiscoCare and Refuge Egypt, which serves Cairo's refugee communities.

The church was designed in the shape of a cross at ground level and a crown at the top. Its roof is visible around Zamalek and was described by the Cairo Observer as reminiscent of a lotus flower.

It was designed by Egyptian architects Dr. Awad Kamel and Selim Kamel, who also created the design for Cairo's Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral (Cathedral of Abbasiya).

Zooba is a truly unique dining experience that takes you on a nostalgic journey back to Egypt in the 1950s and 60s. The restaurant’s traditional design captures the essence of that golden era, with vintage décor, classic signage, and an atmosphere that feels warm and authentic.

The presentation of the food is charmingly old-fashioned, just like the setting. The dishes are served with great attention to detail, reflecting both heritage and creativity. The food itself is absolutely delicious — rich in flavor, freshly prepared, and full of traditional Egyptian taste.

The service is excellent. The waiters are friendly, professional, and always ready to assist with a smile. Their way of serving matches the restaurant’s theme perfectly, making the whole experience feel even more immersive and enjoyable.

Whether you’re visiting for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, Zooba in Open Air Mall is a must-try for anyone who loves good food served with a touch of culture and history.

One evening, my wife and I were walking around looking for a place with a hookah and came across Mokhito. The manager convinced us to look at the menu, and even though we weren’t very hungry, the dishes sounded so good that we decided to stay.

My wife ordered shrimp soup with coconut milk and a shrimp salad, while I tried the beef with caramelized onions and sheep cheese. While we waited, we enjoyed a hookah, which helped pass the time. When the food arrived, it was amazing – very tasty and perfectly cooked.

The only downside was that the drinks took a long time to arrive. Both the first round and the refills were slow. For example, my second non-alcoholic beer came after I had already finished eating, which was disappointing.

Overall, Mokhito is a great place. The food was delicious, the prices were reasonable, and I’d happily come back again.

I booked three days early to make sure the room I reserved was available. I received a confirmation email, and I even messaged them that I would arrive around 8 PM. I got there at 8:30 and was surprised when the reception said they had no reservation under my name. They asked me to contact the owner, Dr. Madhat, via WhatsApp. He didn't respond to customers, they said; it was just him. The reception rudely suggested I find another place.

I insisted on speaking with the owner and they finally contacted him using the landline. He answered and bluntly stated I was late for my booking, so he gave the room to someone else. He told me in a disrespectful tone to find somewhere else nearby. I got angry and demanded they contact him again. They did, and they arranged another room for me.

This room turned out to be on the fifth floor with no elevator. I accepted it for one night and regretted it immediately. The mattresses were worn out, the sheets were yellowed, the bathroom was old and dirty with no tissues, and the air conditioner was noisy and barely worked. The lighting was poor, and overall cleanliness was severely lacking.

I wasn't expecting luxury for the price, but I at least expected basic human usability. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone, not even for an hour.
