A Night at Food Fish: Fish, Fancy Vibes, and a Few Extra Fees!

So, let me set the scene: I walk up to Food Fish, a place that screams high-end from the outside. It’s clear they spent some serious cash and time making it look this fancy, and I’m already excited. But before I even step foot inside, I get hit with an unexpected twist – no self-parking allowed. You’re forced to valet, like, “No sir, you may not park your own car.” I think, fine, I’ll roll with it. Until the end of the night, when that “small detail” turned into a not-so-small 40 EGP valet fee. Yep, an expensive restaurant charging extra just to park my own wheels. Wild, right?

So, I walk in, and immediately, there’s this interesting mix in the air – a blend of fish and what I’m guessing is an industrial-grade air freshener. Like, they’re really trying to mask that fishy aroma, and it almost works, but you can still tell. It’s a bold move, and I respect it… mostly.

Then comes the army of staff. And when I say army, I mean an army. It felt like they had more staff than diners! Over 15 employees just hanging around, standing like statues, keeping an eagle-eye on every single move. And look, I get it, great service is amazing, but there’s a fine line between attentive and intense, and we had definitely crossed it. I’d raise a fork, and I’d have five waiters ready to leap into action. It was both hilarious and kind of nerve-wracking to have them practically watching us chew.

But here’s the redeeming part – the food! Oh man, the food was the kind that makes you forget everything else. We ordered Singary-style fish, some fried fish, butterfly shrimp, and fried calamari. It was all fresh, delicious, and clearly prepared with love. Not a single complaint, just pure satisfaction with every bite.

Now, just when I thought I’d seen it all, the bill arrives, and there’s a 20 EGP “cover charge.” A cover charge? For a restaurant? Not a nightclub, not a shisha lounge – a restaurant! The nerve, right? Between that and the valet, it felt a bit greedy, like they’d figured out every little way to tack on fees.

In summary, Food Fish offers fancy décor, great food, and, well… a few interesting “extras” that you probably won’t see coming. Would I recommend it? Sure – just go in prepared for valet, cover charges, and a team of watchful waiters ready to cater to your every blink.

reviews:
I saw that other reviews rated Dai Pescatori as either absolutely stellar or completely abysmal, so I really didn't know what to expect. Turns out, it was lovely! The music was Mexican and the art was a mix of Egyptian/Sufi mysticism, but the food was 100% Italian. The space was calm, clean, the servers seemed like naturally happy people, and the food was amazing. I highly recommend the lasagna! We'll be back for sure and try the desserts as well.

I do want to address the cost complaint that many seem to have, though. It's true that the dishes were probably the most expensive I've seen, particularly considering the portions. If they go any higher, it likely won't be worth it as a customer. However, I always try to consider operational costs. You cannot realistically compare a restaurant located in Sarayat to have the same prices as somewhere in, say, Hadayek; the rent (and space) for the building, the quality of staff (who I hope are getting paid a living wage), the quality of ingredients, maintenance, the education and skill of the chef and kitchen staff, etc...they're just not the same. When you go out to eat, you're paying for the location, convenience, experience, hygiene, and (God-willing) good food. Put simply, you get what you pay for. Enjoy!

My visit to Cafino left me thoroughly disappointed and frustrated. The lack of cleanliness and hygiene in the establishment was evident from the moment I stepped in. The unclean tables and floors were off-putting, and it was clear that proper cleaning protocols were not being followed. As if that wasn't enough, the absence of internet connectivity due to a supposed quota depletion added to my frustration. It's hard to understand how a business in this day and age could run out of internet quota, especially when customers rely on it for various purposes.

The menu, while attempting to offer a fusion of Arabic and English, ended up being a confusing mishmash of poorly translated items. You'll see choices like "polo bery chees" for Shizkik Baltout instead of the expected blueberry cheesecake. This shows that no effort has been put into compiling the menu.

Also a significant portion of the drink menu was unavailable. Almost 90% of the items listed were not being served, leaving me with limited options and a sense of false advertising.

The staff's unfriendly attitude only added to the negative experience. Their lack of courtesy and willingness to assist customers was evident. Everytime I called the waiter, he was annoyed.

To top it all off, the inadequate ventilation in the establishment left the air heavy and stifling. The lack of fresh air made it uncomfortable to stay for an extended period, and I found myself wanting to leave as soon as possible. This is also aggravated by the shisha they serve inside and outside. So get ready to drink and eat your food with Shisha smoke blowing at you from a directions.

In conclusion, my visit to Cafino was marked by filth, a lack of internet access, confusing menu translations, unavailable items, unfriendly staff, and poor ventilation.

It's like an upgrade from Qahwa Balady (but not really an upgrade). Avoid it like the plague.

During my stay in Cairo, I struggled to find meals that truly satisfied me, so I came here looking for Japanese food.

To be honest, my impression is that this is the kind of place you go to only when you really want Japanese food and have no other option.

The fried octopus, fried chicken, and pork ginger (although it had far too many onions) were all at a level that was simply “okay.”

Nothing special, but no major complaints either. On the other hand, the sashimi, cream croquettes, eel, and simmered tuna cutlet were quite disappointing.

If you eat them expecting proper Japanese cuisine, the gap between expectation and reality is noticeable.

I couldn’t really feel a good balance of flavor or quality ingredients, so these dishes are honestly hard to recommend.

There was also an issue with service.

The wine I first ordered was said to be unavailable, but later it turned out they actually had it.

Even then, the staff showed no sign of concern, which left a bad impression.

Overall, the service level was not very satisfying. This place feels like a last-resort option when you’re craving Japanese food in Cairo.

This was by far one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had. The property looked nothing like the description — the only positive was the view. Everything else was misleading and deeply disappointing.

The cleanliness was appalling. The bedsheets had visible stains, the common areas were dirty, and the entire place felt neglected. Security was practically nonexistent, and stray dogs were wandering freely inside the building. On top of that, the room service staff were unprofessional and frankly creepy, which only added to the sense of being unsafe.

What was advertised online and what I experienced were worlds apart. Instead of comfort and hospitality, I was left with discomfort, anxiety, and frustration. To make matters worse, the management refuses to issue a refund, holding onto the money simply because they think they can.

I would strongly recommend avoiding this property at all costs. It’s unsafe, unhygienic, and completely misleading. There are far better, safer, and more trustworthy options available

🔥 Absolutely the WORST hotel experience of my life. This place is a scam, especially targeting foreign travelers!
First of all, the photos online are a complete lie. The rooms look nothing like what’s advertised. Instead of a bright, cozy space, we got a dark, humid, disgusting box. The sheets were dirty, the walls moldy, the air smelled awful, and the bathroom looked like it hadn’t been cleaned in weeks. No towels, no water, no toilet paper — nothing. It felt less like a hotel and more like a trap.

Then there’s the staff attitude — unbelievably rude and careless. When we politely asked for help, the receptionist just said “wait a moment” and never came back. After an hour, still nothing. We asked again, and they gave us a death stare, as if we were annoying them. That’s not hospitality; that’s pure contempt.

The most suspicious part? I strongly believe this hotel deliberately overbooks rooms and scams guests. We paid for a “room with a view,” but got shoved into a windowless cell. When confronted, the front desk flat-out lied, saying it’s the same type. Other guests were also arguing about the same issue — clearly this is how they operate.

The whole place is dark, creepy, and unsafe. It honestly felt like they prey on tourists who can’t fight back.

⚠️ Do yourself a favor — don’t even think about booking here.
This isn’t a budget hotel; it’s a fraud in disguise.
Spend your money somewhere that respects you as a guest and as a human being.

Overview:

Nestled with a view that captures the heart of Corniche El Mokkatam, Soly’s presents a dining experience that is as refreshing as it is satisfying. This gem offers not just a meal but a journey through flavors, backed by a panorama that adds a visual feast to the already delightful experience. Friendly staff, exceptional service, and a diverse menu ensure that each visit is memorable.

The Positive:

•	The breathtaking view of the Corniche El Mokkatam elevates the dining experience, especially from the outdoor seating area complete with a swing and the second-floor panorama.
•	Soly’s staff are the epitome of friendliness and accommodation, making every visit feel personal and welcoming.
•	The menu’s variety is impressive, spanning pizzas, western pies, a range of beverages including coffee and fresh juices, along with main dishes that cater to all tastes.
•	The Oriental breakfast is a standout, offering traditional favorites like falafel, fool, omelette, and pie with molasses and tahini, providing a delightful start to the day.
•	Reasonable and affordable pricing makes Soly’s an accessible option for regular visits, offering great value for the quality and variety provided.
•	The Oriental sausage pie comes highly recommended, a must-try that promises to be a highlight of any meal.
•	For those cooler days or when outdoor seating isn’t preferable, the interior provides a cozy refuge with comfortable couches and chairs, ensuring comfort regardless of the weather.

The Negative:

•	The major downside to Soly’s location is the poor network reception across the main service providers, which can make it a challenge to stay connected or reachable during your visit. WE is the only network that works there.
•	While Wi-Fi is available, it tends to be unreliable and slow, which might inconvenience those needing a steady internet connection.

Final Verdict:
Soly’s stands out not just for its stunning location and view but for delivering a consistent, quality dining experience that resonates with both the heart and the palate. With its warm atmosphere, diverse menu, and reasonable pricing, it’s a place that beckons for repeat visits. The Oriental sausage pie alone is worth the journey, adding to a menu full of gems waiting to be discovered. While the connectivity issues might deter some, they also offer a chance to disconnect from the digital world and immerse fully in the moment, making Soly’s an ideal spot for those looking to enjoy good food and great company, away from the distractions of the outside world. A true jewel of Corniche El Mokkatam, Soly’s is a testament to what a dining experience should be—delicious, welcoming, and utterly unforgettable.

reviews: I've tried many Korean restaurants here in Cairo, and this place takes first place among all the others. The food is very authentic and incredibly tasty. A Korean family was sitting next to us, and they were very friendly—they didn’t … More

Nestled close to Maadi, this gem shines as the epitome of Korean culinary excellence. Delight in exquisite dishes that marry authenticity and affordability flawlessly.

Hailing from South Korea, the devoted family behind this culinary haven has graced Egypt's taste buds for almost three decades. Their homemade kimchi is a testament to tradition and craftsmanship.

Step inside to find a modest setting, devoid of ostentation but exuding a certain charm. The focus here is unequivocally on the gastronomic experience. Authenticity permeates every corner, drawing a predominantly Korean clientele seeking a taste of home.

Language barriers fade as the gracious owners communicate in Arabic with a touch of English. Their warm hospitality is unmatched, ensuring each guest feels like family in every visit.

Immerse yourself in the aromas of sizzling delights while savoring the rare treat of pork dishes and local beer alongside your meal. It's not just a dining experience; it's a culinary journey to Korea's heartland.

Dining at Arirang feels like being warmly welcomed into a cozy home in Seoul. From the very first bite, it’s clear this isn’t just a meal — it’s an experience. The noodles are silky and flavorful, the rice dishes perfectly seasoned, and the kimbap? An absolute delight — fresh, balanced, and packed with love.

Their tteokbokki offers that perfect kick of spice with the chewy rice cakes cooked to perfection, while the meats are juicy, and grilled just right. Don’t even get me started on the kimchi and salads — crisp, refreshing, and bursting with authentic Korean flavor.

What truly sets Arirang apart is not just the food, but the heart behind it. The owner is incredibly sweet and attentive, going above and beyond to make you feel comfortable. The staff are kind, professional, and attentive, making the whole experience feel like a warm family gathering. Honestly, everything was 10/10 — a true chef’s kiss.

If you're in Maadi and craving an unforgettable Korean meal, Arirang is a must-visit. You’ll leave full, happy, and already planning your next visit.

name: Giza Plateau
description: Iconic, ancient 4,500-year-old plateau featuring the Great Pyramids, the Sphinx & other sites.
address: Al Haram, Giza Governorate 3512201
reviews: The timeless Pyramids of Giza rise majestically against the horizon — silent witnesses to the boundless genius and eternal glory of the ancient Egyptian civilization.

This is one of the most beautiful places on earth. It’s very majestic and fascinating, it really speaks for itself. It’s truly jaw dropping eye popping. I’ve been here several times now and it never gets old. It’s one of the ancient wonders … More

What's the Giza Plateau you ask? Basically, its the huge, flat area in the desert where the ancient Egyptians decided to build giant pyramids to be their really fancy graves. That’s the Giza Plateau.

It home for the massive Great Pyramid, the Sphinx (aka the world’s most famous cat statue), and a bunch of smaller pyramids too. If you see giant stones and a lot of tourists, congratulations, you’ve arrived.

Actually, being at the pyramids was the best thing about being in Cairo. It felt like I walked into a history channel documentary. 10/10, would get sunburned again.

While the pyramids are worth more than five stars, the camel and horse riders make you feel unsafe. Furthermore, they are very insistent and some of them are very intimidating. Shame that the authorities do not step in and make the site more safe for tourists.

A must visit place when in Cairo. Plan enough time and take waterwith you. Comfortable shoes are important and wear light clothes as it's warm inside the pyramids. Free Shuttle bus from ticket office to the Pyramids/Sphinx Easy to buy tickets and the cleanest toilets I ever seen in Egypt.

reviews:
Had a pleasant stay with my wife here. The room looked great and was kept clean throughout our stay. The location is superb, and the staff has been nothing but super nice to us, especially Ali and Ahmed.

Now granted, this is an old building where the hotel is sharing space with. For the price, do not expect 4-star or 5-star hotel lobbies, etc. It's worth noting that the elevator may feel a bit unsafe due to not having wall on the front side while ascending (like I said, old building, and they probably don't have full control over the building structure itself). Might not be good for those with fear of heights. Otherwise, the elevator itself is pretty reliable.

The spaces that they do own, like the café and the rooms are amazing. The café has a balcony area where you can eat as well, although a bit cramped. Great for photo ops though! The included breakfast could be better, but was pretty satisfying overall. Their coffee tasted great.

The building entrance has a security guard at night, so we really weren't worried about safety. The other tenants in the building keep to themselves and don't bother hotel guests.

Overall, we had a great stay!

Runnnnnnnn! Don't come! It's a nightmare! We agreed at the front desk that I'd shower first, then get a massage. The masseuse didn't understand English, so she started with a massage and oil treatment before even letting me shower.
She started the oil massage from my feet upwards! I came here sweaty after playing golf, and my feet weren't even that clean! The massage was weak, and the pressure points were all wrong.

After getting covered in oil, I went to the Turkish bath, and it was the start of another nightmare.
She just steamed me without letting me shower, and the steam wasn't even hot enough; it would stop after a while. I was shivering in the bathroom. Finally, I was allowed to shower, but they made me lie on the cold, slippery shower platform. The platform wasn't heated! It was soaking wet, so scrubbing vigorously was dangerous. The water kept switching between scalding hot and freezing cold, making it impossible to adjust the temperature properly.
After rinsing off all the oil, without applying any black scrub or oil-removing products, how could I possibly get rid of any dirt from all that oil?

I finally finished lathering up, but there was full of foam. Applying it to both sides made it easy for the foam to slide off. After applying it, I lay down on the counter to rinse off, but then the water temperature got messed up again.
So, I had to put on a bathrobe and go to the massage room to shower, still covered in foam. It was the first time in my life I'd ever worn a bathrobe while covered in foam, and I was freezing! During the bath, people kept opening the door to check if I was done showering. Since there was only one shower room, it made me even colder.
Back in the massage room, another problem arose: the showerhead switch was broken, and there were bugs inside!

After washing, I started getting bumps on my back, probably from the oil. I also had an allergic reaction to the scrub on my face. My husband's arm got chafed from scrubbing it so much. That's what I got for today's 4,000 Egyptian pounds.

As a foreigner who has lived here for many years, I've never given a bad review. Even if it's slightly off, I wouldn't comment. This isn't my first time getting a massage and Turkish bath in Cairo; I've had very satisfying experiences before. A 2000 Egyptian pound package isn't expensive, but it shouldn't be this bad.

name: Silk Road Chinese Restaurant halal
description: Silk Road Chinese Restaurant halal, located in the Maadi area of Cairo, is an inviting restaurant specializing in Chinese cuisine. It is well rated, holding a 4.0-star rating from 365 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. Visitors frequently note pleasant views and a family-friendly environment. reviews:
“Silk Road used to be a hidden gem for me, my family, and friends a few years ago, so I went back expecting that same level… but it didn’t hit.
We ordered a few dishes and honestly, most of them lacked real flavor. The beef dumplings were bland no ginger, no garlic, no sesame oil, nothing. However wrapper was a bit thick and chewy, but the main issue was the filling had zero personality (4/10).

The chow mein noodles themselves were actually good they were fresh and nicely chewy, but the sauce was weak, barely any chicken, and again missing proper Chinese seasoning (5/10).

The rice cakes used to be my favorite, especially with that Sichuan kick, but this time they were overloaded with onions (some still raw), and the sauce just didn’t deliver. Texture wise was still great though (5/10).

Sweet and sour chicken had a nice crispy outside and juicy inside, but the sauce leaned too much into a ketchup vibe for me (5/10).

Also the chili oil was very disappointing tasted like burnt chili in oil, nothing else (2/10).

Beyond the food, the overall experience didn’t help. Service was slow, hygiene needs serious attention, and no card machine, which is just inconvenient at this point. Honestly, not sure I’d go back anytime soon.

Might just be nostalgia carrying it, but I wouldn’t confidently recommend it right now.

I had an awesome time staying at Bella Hostel! It’s right in the middle of Cairo, at Midan Talat Harb, so you’re super close to everything literally..restaurants, galleries, you name it. It’s perfect if you don’t want to spend ages in transportation.
The team there... Mirna, Sahar, and Om Mohamed were amazing. They made us feel so welcome and really went out of their way to help. The place was super clean, and the rooms and bathrooms were well kept. Yeah, the water pressure is a bit on the gentle side, but that just adds to the vintage charm of the place.
If you’re after something super luxurious, this might not be it, but if you want that authentic, vintage Cairo vibe, you’ll love it. It really feels like stepping into the heart of the city.
The kitchen’s got everything you need for a quick meal or breakfast, and the views are pretty awesome, as you can see in the pics.
All in all, I had a fantastic stay and would totally recommend Bella Hostel if you want to experience Cairo in a genuine way ❤️

Hotel staff helpful and responsive. Easy check in too. Must try their delicious falafel during the morning breakfast.

The location of this place is great, literally a one-minute walk from the pyramids site. There is a nice rooftop with a bar and restaurant with a perfect view of the site. And that's all the good things about this place. Everything else is very poor. First of all, most of the rooms do not have a window, which could be problematic for people suffering from claustrophobia (not my case), and this is not specified when booking the room (or at least, my understanding was that I had selected a room with a view). To me, this is a very minor issue, but I've heard people complain about it -- and for good reason. The biggest issue that I have with this place is the hygiene: the room was very dirty, and the bed sheets were not changed; we found hair (see screenshot) on the bed, probably from the previous guest -- I do not think it was from the cleaning ladies, since they were all covered. When I raised the issue, the receptionist proposed moving us to another room for the night, which I refused because I didn't trust it would be clean; I wanted a sheet change. What they did instead was to make me carry a blanket from the other room (myself), and after 30 minutes, they gave us only one pillowcase. Another issue was that we asked the hotel to book us a tour guide for the pyramids, and they scammed us with overcharging and with the laziest tour guide I've ever seen: he cut the tour short, mostly took the bus from one spot to another with no historical background (he did not even believe aliens made the pyramids! :) ), didn't do 70% of the things we were promised in the tour list of activities, and didn't want to bring us to places we asked for. The last point was about the restaurant: since the region is extremely unwelcoming to tourists, we did not dare to go out much in Giza, so we stayed at the rooftop hotel restaurant, since no other options seemed suitable. While we had to wait because a huge group had a reservation, we asked for some bread in the meantime, but this request was ignored by the waiters (it arrived after the main dish); then, we also received grilled meat that was completely burned and therefore inedible (see screenshot). At breakfast, if you only ask for coffee, they insist that you have something to eat even though you don’t want to, and this is — trust me — extremely irritating. My overall suggestion is to spend only half a day in Cairo/Giza, see the pyramids, then move on to Luxor or head back home. Do not pay these scammers. A real shame to go from the best civilization on Earth to this.

Easily one of the best places to get value for your money,

-Food is cuisine like quality and experience for much cheaper prices
Note: all the food tastes good, and i especially recommend the Polinari Pasta, it is a big bowl and it gets Two people stuffed, you can just get an appetizer beside it for variety, but it really is perfect and the portion like I said is for 2, I also the Chicken Mushroom Main dish, it is really good and tasty, just a heads up, make a reservation prior going as they take a lot of time preparing the main dishes because they serve them fresh, that is if you don't love waiting, but it is really worth the wait, Lasagna is good and the portion is also for 2, but after finishing the bowl, you'll end up hating the color red from the amount of tomatoe sauce you've eaten 😂.

Pizzas are good but they are not amazing, you'll not be wowed from it like the other plates, if you want to try it though, I really recommend the primavera with extra cheese (with no blue cheese, or olives because pizza is not the food to add those on), the one with pineapples is also good, it's just a bbq pizza with pineapples on it, they do not put a lot of pineapple on it so it is not overwhelming the other flavors, it just gives a kick of sweetness that tastes good, but again pizza will not wow you, it's just a good pizza.

Ask for their spicy sauce bottle if you love spicy, it is really really good and it'll leave you very satisfied.

-Service is great, and the people are lovely there, especially El Capitano, his hospitality and friendliness is what made us fsll in love with this hidden franchise, to the point that we sometimes ask prior going what branch is the Capitano at so we can meet him.

-Atmosphere is very beautiful and peaceful, it should resemble the local restaurants of Italy, of course, I do not know how much of resemblance there is because I've never been to Italy, but I guarantee you'll feel comfy there, they just need to buy AC for the summer as their portable water cooling fans do not do enough work to cool you in that hot weather, but you can spend everyday of your week there in Winter.

Overall I really with the deepst regret recommend the place as much as I hate to do it, as it's been a special spot for me, and in a selfish way you just want to keep it to yourself, but I really wish them all the best! ♥️

name: Taha Hussein Museum
description:
Taha Hussein Museum is a historic house museum and biographical museum in Giza, Egypt.
It is about the life, teaching, and residence of Taha Hussein, who was one of the most influential 20th-century Egyptian writers and intellectuals and a figurehead for the Al-Nahda—Arab Renaissance and the modernist movement in the Arab World.
The museum is located in Hussein's former home, where he lived from 1955 to 1973.

reviews:

As Taha Hussein's grandson I know the house well. While it has generally been well maintained, some aspects need attention and a budget. Floors have been allowed to become shabby, with haphazard coverings. Furniture has been reupholstered poorly. Shutters need a paint job.
Considering that in the two hours I was there there were no other visitors, it is perhaps understandable that there is no incentive to make the effort.
It is a pity that the garden, once the main attraction of the residence, is no more. I suppose visitors are naturally more interested in the house.

My experience at Bacardi Bar was absolutely disappointing. From the second I walked in, it was obvious the staff treat people based on personal preference, not respect. If you’re a regular male customer, don’t expect much attention — you’re practically invisible. The place itself is poorly managed and chaotic. Staff claim that “all tables are reserved” when the place is clearly half empty. You’re not allowed to choose where to sit — they’ll seat you wherever they want, based on their mood, not your comfort. It’s unprofessional and frankly, disrespectful.

This bar lacks the basics: organization, equal treatment, and customer respect. There are far better places where you’re treated fairly and professionally.

Bacardi Bar is not worth your time, money, or energy. Avoid it.

reviews:
This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in, especially considering the price. I paid over $300 for three nights, and the hotel is absolutely not worth this amount. Honestly, it does not even deserve a one-star rating.

I was completely misled by the 75+ reviews on Expedia, which give the impression that this is an excellent hotel, with a rating of 9/10. The hotel is also listed under two different names on Expedia, one of them being Cairo Plaza Prime Hotel. This raises serious concerns and makes me suspect that something unusual is going on with the property management.

During the same trip, I stayed at another hotel for three nights for only $220, including an open buffet breakfast, and the rooms and service were far superior.

The hotel is located in a very old building, and you have to climb large stairs just to reach the reception on the first floor. The reception office is extremely close to the rooms, so you can hear their noise throughout the night.

The bathroom setup is unacceptable. The toilet is placed inside a small cabinet within the room, right next to the beds. When someone uses it, it feels like you are inside the bathroom yourself, and any smell spreads immediately across the room.

Although I booked three nights under a non-refundable policy, I contacted the hotel to request staying only one night and refunding the remaining nights. They kept making excuses and asked me to contact Expedia instead. I spent a lot of time with Expedia customer service, and they made several attempts to reach the hotel by phone and email. All of these attempts were ignored. The hotel later claimed they never received any communication from Expedia, which I find very hard to believe. As a result, I was forced to stay all three nights, which completely ruined my trip.

I later switched to another room where the toilet was slightly farther from the beds (about one meter). However, there was a very strong and unpleasant smell outside the room, possibly coming from a laundry or utility area.

Finally, Expedia states that a “full breakfast” is included. In reality, this so-called full breakfast consists of only one boiled egg, a single piece of cheese, and a tiny jar of jam. Calling this a full breakfast is simply misleading.

I strongly do not recommend this hotel.

name: Dahabiya Nile Sailing
description: Dahabiya Nile Sailing, located in the Mohammed Roushdy area of Cairo, is a standout attraction. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.9-star rating from 331 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. Visitors frequently note views over the Nile, pleasant views, and friendly service. It remains a worthwhile stop for both locals and visitors to Cairo.
address: In front of Co-operation Gas station, 11 Gawad Hosny St, Off, Mohammed Roushdy, Cairo Governorate 11513
reviews:
Our 4 day/ 3 night dahabiya cruise from Aswan to Luxor with Dahabiya Nile Sailing was a truly remarkable experience, start to finish. From our highly attentive and communicative tour organiser, Omar, to the transportation, boat crew and tour guide; the level of customer service and care was impeccable. Not only was our flight delayed by several hours causing us to miss our scheduled check in but we also had our two little ones (aged 1 and 3) to consider in our travel plans. The crew accommodated our late arrival and seemlessly organised transportation to the next port, transferring us to a tug boat and welcoming us with smiles, cool towels and fresh drinks upon our arrival. The staff were wonderful and engaging with our children throughout our stay, ensuring a cot and small bed were available in our room and often taking time to play and interact with them which only added to their enjoyment on board. The meals were well timed with a beautiful assortment of traditional Egyptian cuisine and other delicious delicacies. The boat and rooms were clean and well serviced. Even with two young children, we found the itinerary manageable and rich with unique cultural experiences that you wouldn’t otherwise have on a larger cruise ship. The intimate and relaxed atmosphere was a perfect way to absorb the magic of the Nile.

We also went on to have a private tour organised through Dahabiya Nile Sailing while in Luxor. Our Tour guide, Reham, was exceptional. She was incredible knowledgeable and accommodating to our pace and needs.

Highly recommend this company. You will not be disappointed.
Visited on
Weekend

This might be the best way to see Egypt. The moment we boarded the dahabiya, we were greeted with smiles and immediately felt welcomed. The rooms are incredibly comfortable, and the views of the Nile River are nothing short of breathtaking. … More

This dahabiya tour was the highlight of our trip- it is not to be missed! The tour itinerary thoughtfully balances historical and archeological sites with cultural experiences highlighting modern-day life for Egyptians living on the Nile, and plans fun-filled days that also doesn’t overwhelm you with overactivity- you will want plenty of time to just enjoy the beautiful boat in the evening! The boat switches between being towed by tugboat or sailing. It doesn’t has an engine if its own so it is airways very quiet and clean. They deftly time the tours at the popular attractions around the schedules of the larger boats to avoid overcrowded experiences, and the smaller size of the dahabiya allows for docking at smaller locations and not just the larger tourist ports. Here, you meet and interact with locals in villages along the way for cultural exchanges that are invited by the welcoming residents in a way that was authentic and not exploitative. Our tour guide Shaima was attentive, thoughtful, highly informative and adaptable, helping us with any side-quests that we fancied along the way. We always felt safe, welcome and taken care of everywhere we went. The crew on the boat was amazing! Incredible hospitality from Imad, Hassan and Ali who were so friendly and helpful, and captain Yousef always made sure we were having fun. Younes, Ahmed, Haroun, Hussein and Hamdy made sure we had smooth sailing the whole trip. The daily 3 square meals (plus teatime) served up by chefs Sayed and Amr were always delicious, and our groups’ dietary restrictions were navigated with care. The tugboat operators Tamer and Fahed made sure we arrived everywhere on time, and even drove us around to see the Dahabiya from afar when it set sail. Really can’t recommend this tour enough! Sometimes on a trip, packing your bags every night to go experience a new location gets tiring, but on the Dahabiya, the sights come to you!

Absolutely magical experience, sailing the Nile on a dahabiya. It’s a smaller traditional boat and can reach areas which the. Offer cruise ships cannot. Only 10 cabins, so a smaller group of guests. A mix of learning about Egyptian … More

This is hands-down the best tour experience I've ever had., anywhere. I did a Nile cruise on one of the big boats two years ago and this is so much better! The dahabiya boat itself was comfortable and the crew fantastic. My compliments to the chef, and the music and dancing! Going on our own schedule -- such as visiting Edfu temple with only ourselves for company instead of the thousands that come on the big cruiser schedules, and getting to places like the stone quarry where the bigger boats can't go at all -- was AMAZING. The local experiences of fishing and tea on an island village where we could ask questions to those who lived there was so enlightening. The very best? Coming back each day to cool towels and fresh lemonade!

reviews:
The Egyptian Bazaar in Cairo is an absolute gem and a must-visit for anyone immersing themselves in the rich culture and history of Egypt. As soon as you step inside, you're greeted by a captivating array of colors, aromas, and sounds that embody the spirit of Cairo.

The selection of goods is truly remarkable. You'll find everything from exquisitely crafted handicrafts and beautiful textiles to stunning jewelry, aromatic spices, and traditional Egyptian delicacies. Each stall offers something special, making it an ideal location for discovering authentic souvenirs that reflect the area's rich heritage.

What truly distinguishes the Egyptian Bazaar is its vibrant atmosphere. The lively exchanges between vendors and customers create a welcoming environment. Many shopkeepers are eager to share the stories behind their crafts, adding a personal touch to your shopping experience.

Additionally, the bazaar's prime location near historical landmarks makes it even more appealing. Whether you're there to shop, indulge in local cuisine, or simply soak in the lively culture, the Egyptian Bazaar offers an unforgettable experience that you should not miss during your time in Cairo. Highly recommended!

Mohamed was the kindest soul, he met my sister and I on the street invited us for dinner during Ramadan. We ended up browsing the shop and walked away with a deal of paintings and perfumes along with a new friendship!

I bought some papyrus. The owner seems to be used to dealing with foreigners, so he also recommended perfume and desert tours. He wasn't pushy, but he was quite pushy, so if you're not interested, just decline. The owner is a very nice guy.

Mohammed is a charming guy. We exchanged some fun stories over tea and I bought one papyrus artwork, which glows in the dark. Fair, transparent prices, and no pressure to buy. His nephew then took me to another shop where I bought a few more gifts.

Mohammad is an amazing host, and this shop stands out for its low-pressure sales approach. The prices are very transparent, which is refreshing, and they even have some special papyrus pieces with hidden second paintings that you can only … More

reviews:
The highlight of my stay was definitely the friendly and helpful staff. Everyone was always smiling and willing to assist, which I truly appreciated. The hotel’s location is also very good — it is centrally located, close to the pyramid, Carrefour, restaurants, and shops. Museums are also just 10–15 minutes away, which is very convenient.

However, despite these positives, my overall stay was unfortunately not very satisfactory.

I believe the housekeeping team would benefit from additional training, and management should pay closer attention to the wear and tear of the property in order to maintain proper standards.

I booked my room through an agency, so I did not choose the room myself. I stayed for five days in Room 124, which I would strongly advise future guests to avoid.

The neighboring building is extremely close, making the room very noisy, and people from the next building can easily access the balcony, which raised serious safety concerns.

During my stay, I experienced the following issues:

* The balcony door lock was broken.
* The balcony was not cleaned.
* Hair was found on the toilet bowl.
* Urine stains were present in the toilet bowl.
* The entrance to the hotel does not give a good first impression.
* Continuous horn noise could be heard throughout the day.
* The room phone was not working (staff advised it was non-functional).
* The room door only locked properly when double locked; with a single lock, the door could still be opened. We slept two days with the single lock thinking it was locked.
* The room was very dusty, causing itching and coughing.
* Tea bags were left uncovered, collecting dust and affecting quality of the tea.

From a safety and cleanliness perspective, the hotel needs significant improvement. Regular maintenance and stronger housekeeping standards are clearly needed. Unfortunately, it felt that guest comfort and safety were not being prioritized enough.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this hotel, and I would not choose to stay here again.

name: Gamal Abdel Nasser Museum
description:
Gamal Abdel Nasser Hussein (15 January 1918 – 28 September 1970) was an Egyptian military officer and revolutionary who served as the second president of Egypt from 1954 until his death in 1970. Nasser led the Egyptian revolution of 1952 and introduced far-reaching land reforms the following year. Following a 1954 assassination attempt by a Muslim Brotherhood member, he cracked down on the organization, put President Mohamed Naguib under house arrest and assumed executive office. He was formally elected president in June 1956.
Nasser's popularity in Egypt and the Arab world skyrocketed after his nationalization of the Suez Canal and his political victory in the subsequent Suez Crisis, known in Egypt as the Tripartite Aggression. Calls for pan-Arab unity under his leadership increased, culminating with the formation of the United Arab Republic with Syria from 1958 to 1961. In 1962, Nasser began a series of major socialist measures and modernization reforms in Egypt. Despite setbacks to his pan-Arabist cause, by 1963 Nasser's supporters gained power in several Arab countries, but he became embroiled in the North Yemen Civil War, and eventually the much larger Arab Cold War. He began his third presidential term in March 1965 after his political opponents were banned from running. Following Egypt's defeat by Israel in the Six-Day War of 1967, Nasser resigned, but he returned to office after popular demonstrations called for his reinstatement. name: Synagogue Ben Ezra
description: Ornately adorned synagogue believed to have been built on the site where baby Moses was found.
address: 264J+7CV, Kom Ghorab, Old Cairo, Cairo Governorate 4244001
reviews:
ECHOES OF A SHARED HERITAGE - JOURNEY THORUGH BEN EZRA SYNAGOGUE

We visited the Ben Ezra Synagogue in the Coptic Church area of Old Cairo in January 2026 as part of a large group, and the experience was both moving and memorable. This was possibly the second or third time that I was entering a synagogue, although I recall having visited one in Israel more than twenty years ago and subsequently one in the UK. The structure, though no longer in active use, is remarkably beautiful and serene.
Knowing its long history and significance, including its association with the famed Cairo Geniza, added depth to the visit. I found myself reflecting on the period when the synagogue would have been vibrant and active, with a thriving Jewish community in Cairo participating in worship and social life. That sense of a once-living heritage was powerful.

The paintings, wooden work, and decorative elements inside are exquisite, and the architectural style—blending influences from the surrounding Coptic environment—gives the place a distinctive character. Despite being preserved now mainly as a heritage monument, the space retains a spiritual quietness.

There was also a sense of sadness that it is no longer in regular use, but at the same time gratitude that it has been maintained so well. Overall, it was a deeply fulfilling visit and an important reminder of Cairo’s layered religious and cultural past. I spent a few minutes in prayer here. A must visit monument in Coptic Cairo.

Our experience with the hotel exceeded expectations from the moment we arrived in Cairo. After an Uber driver attempted to charge us nearly $50, we immediately contacted the hotel for assistance. They promptly arranged an airport pickup for $25. The driver was professional, courteous, and extremely helpful, which immediately made us feel safe and comfortable—especially as this was our first visit to Egypt.

Upon arrival at the hotel, we were warmly welcomed by the receptionist and taken to the rooftop, where we were greeted with a truly breathtaking and unforgettable view. We were offered fresh orange juice as a welcome drink, which was a thoughtful touch.

The hotel also arranged an outstanding tour for only $20, including visits to the Pyramids, the Sphinx, the Grand Egyptian Museum, and Saqqara, with a private driver, a guide, two bottles of water, and lunch. This was far more reliable and transparent than many online tour providers.

Our room was spotless, beautifully decorated, and very comfortable. The amenities included a safe, a kettle with tea and coffee, and two bottles of water. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and we enjoyed a perfect night’s sleep. The Wi-Fi connection was excellent both in the room and throughout the hotel.

Breakfast was impressive, offering a wide variety of more than 15 items, and the bar and overall service were outstanding. Every staff member we interacted with was kind, attentive, and genuinely helpful.

We highly recommend this hotel and will definitely return on our next trip to Egypt.

The standout feature is, without question, the unobstructed, panoramic view of the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) from the rooftop terrace. To be 100% honest: while the view is 'Ultra-Premium,' the hotel maintains a boutique, intimate feel rather than a massive resort vibe. If you are in this area, don’t miss visiting this restaurant — it will definitely be a memorable experience.
Highly recommended for anyone who loves real Indian food! 👍

The real Giza. The hotel is tucked away between the shops, the little mini market next door with the friendly owner ideal for room snacks and ATM's a two minute walk away. If you want a sterile hotel where you're sealed away from the locals this isn't for you .
Our room was clean, reasonably modern and comfortable with a rainfall shower. Slightly disappointed with the tiny window but not all rooms can have a view. We did have to be proactive seeking things like replacement toilet rolls and the room wasn't made up or cleaned during our two night stay. The staff are friendly and helpful, especially the lady on reception.
Breakfast is a fairly limited affair and continental / Egyptian in style, there are boiled eggs and Falafel but otherwise no cooked. There is however a fullsome dinner menu but note they only accept cash, no cards, no putting on your room number.
Leaving the best until last it's the view of the pyramids and sphinx from the rooftop restaurant that really sells this hotel, it is absolutely stunning especially when the nearby mosque has its call to prayer, it is real Egypt.

This is to describe my experience of 2025 new year's eve in one of the venues " the big hall" at San Giovanni, El Manial Dist.
It was a 30 dollar per person set menu dinner with few singing shows and a belly dancer show. Food was accepted, not that fancy, a salad, main dish with choice of smoked salmon felet or slices of turkey brest with grevy both served with coices of vegetables, rice, fries and mached potatoes a side with desser. The service was good, fast and very friendly. The staff were cooperative and patient with a smile. The failure that turned the night into a very boaring experience was the DJ! The crowd was not helping at too as it was a mix of senior citizens and mostly families with young kids. They kept the lights on all night and it was very uncomfortable. I think it was much better if they put down lights and used a dimmed lights. The belly dancer show part was the best thing for that night. I think it was a management crisis or unprofessional way to plan and handle such kind of events. There was another party outdoor but their DJ along with a crowd of middle aged couples were on fire and was much funnier to be out there although it was so cold with 11 deggrees celsius.
The staff were well prepared to make sure that everyone was satisfied but for the other reasons at was a great failure and will be remembered as the worst in enjoying the surrounding atmosphere and new year's vibes.
At the end, the good company and the cold weather made that night unforgettable.

reviews:
Today, I had the opportunity to try out Wallen’s after reading some good reviews. The place itself is nice, work- and study-friendly, and offers Wi-Fi. I ordered a white mocha, which was actually very good, along with a tiramisu that was rich and delicious. The cookies were amazing, though a bit too sweet for my taste, and the flat white was also good.

My only major concern is that they allow indoor smoking, which was quite disappointing. Had I known this beforehand, I wouldn’t have visited. When I asked someone there about it, he explained that it’s the place’s policy and suggested I sit outside while he turned on the AC. I declined, as this didn’t make sense to me—smoking should be limited to outdoor areas. He even admitted this is a common complaint, yet the policy hasn’t changed.
To his credit, he adjusted the AC and checked on me twice to make sure I was more comfortable, which I genuinely appreciated.

That said, despite the great service and good food, I will not be coming back because of the indoor smoking policy.

name: Bab tooma (New cairo- Cloud 9)
description: Bab tooma (New cairo- Cloud 9), located at cloud 9 in the New Cairo 1 area of Cairo, is a standout restaurant specializing in Syrian and Levantine cuisine. It is well rated, holding a 4.0-star rating from 272 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. Visitors frequently note pleasant views, outdoor seating, and friendly service. It is typically open 10:00–02:00. All in all, Bab tooma (New cairo- Cloud 9) has earned a loyal following for its food and welcoming setting.
address: cloud 9, 1 settlement, Mohammed Nagib Axis, New Cairo 1, Cairo Governorate 4740310
reviews:
With new restaurants in Cairo diversifying into new and exciting cuisines every week, we don’t have to travel too far to enjoy the foods of other cultures. Similar to Cairo’s own medieval Victory Gate, Syrian restaurant, Bab Tooma, proudly attained its name from the famous ‘Thomas’ Gate’ in Damascus.

The décor of the New Cairo restaurant is also influenced by traditional Syrian tastes; however, it maintains an air of professionalism and leans toward the uniformity of international chains. Despite arriving close to midnight, we discovered that this is actually when the restaurant is at its busiest. We watched an influx of younger customers continue to arrive late into the night, turning Bab Tooma from a quiet diner into one of the liveliest, loudest hangouts in town.

The menu is varied and includes dishes influenced by recipes from all over the world. Amongst others, we found a large selection of starters, main courses, sandwiches, pastries and tagines. Rarely found in Egypt, the desserts included several classic sweet dishes from the Levantine region; Beirut Ghazl, Nabulsi konafa and halawa with cheese, as well as drinks such as rosewater and galab.

For appetizers, we dived straight in with orders of sogo’ and thyme man’oucheh (25LE) along with fried mozzarella sticks (25LE). For our mains we moved on to one four cheese (45LE), and one salami pizza (45LE) as well as a maqdous fata (45LE).

Unfortunately, the staff seemed to be overwhelmed and the first of our food was long in coming.

Unusually, the man’oucheh was cut into sheets rather than rolled, whilst the sogo’ filling was fresh and pleasant tasting. Sadly, the fried cheese was served cold and lost its crunch – and its appeal. Although far from extraordinary the pizzas were both satisfying and generously sized although the highlight of the meal came in the form of the traditional, Syrian maqdous fata – a dish made from kobba, egg plants, crispy bread and milk.

For dessert, we indulged in Beirut Ghazl (35LE) and cheese halawa (35LE).

Both the airy cheese halawa and Beirut Ghazl were much more delectable and very well made. Although similar to candyfloss, the Beirut Ghazl was topped with a range of flavourful ice-creams, adding a Lebanese twist to the dish. The cheese halawa, meanwhile, was delectably creamy and full of flavour. We had also ordered some Nabulsi konafa, but it came served almost completely frozen in the middle – twice.

Despite a number a mishaps putting a downer on our visit, we commend the number of traditional delicacies and dishes on offer. This combined with Bab Tooma’s vibrant and bubbly atmosphere means that you won’t for one moment forget that you are dining in a Syrian restaurant.

Best Bit
The Beirut Ghazl will satisfy even the most picky of sweet-toothed Cairenes.

Worst Bit
The service was incredibly slow

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Great for Hosting Guests – Fast Delivery & Tasty Food!

Although I don’t eat meat or chicken, Fire Hub has become my go-to place when I have guests over. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared, and I’ve never had a complaint from anyone I’ve ordered for.

Fast & Reliable Delivery 🚀

One of the best things about Fire Hub is how quick and efficient their delivery service is. Even when ordering for a group, the food arrives hot and fresh, which is a big plus. Whether it’s a last-minute order or a planned meal, they never disappoint in terms of timing and quality.

Vegetarian-Friendly Options 🌱🍝

Since I don’t eat meat or chicken, I usually go for their pasta dishes without chicken, and they are always delicious and fresh. The sauces are rich and flavorful, and the portion sizes are generous. It’s nice to have a restaurant where I can still enjoy great food while ordering for guests who prefer meat-based dishes.

Guests Love It! 🍔🍗

Whenever I order from here for friends or family, everyone loves the food. The burgers, fried chicken, and sides are all big hits, and they do a great job of maintaining quality across different dishes.

Final Verdict 💯

If you’re looking for a reliable place with fast delivery, great flavors, and something for everyone, Fire Hub is a solid choice. Even if you’re vegetarian, the pasta options are fresh and satisfying, and for those who enjoy meat, this place is a favorite. Highly recommended!

Title: Convenient for a Quick Stay, But with Drawbacks

Review:

I needed a last-minute room in Cairo before my early morning flight back to the USA and chose the Royal Inn in Nasr City, which came highly recommended on Booking.com. Here's my take:

The staff is welcoming, and the room offered several amenities, including a safe, two beds, a minibar, air conditioning, and it was both clean and quiet.

However, the hotel has its challenges. It's tricky to find and requires ascending several steps from the street to the entrance. The lobby is small, feels cramped and poorly lit. There’s no breakfast included with the stay, and no elevators are available. Fortunately, the staff assisted with my luggage, though a tip was expected and given.

While it has its drawbacks, the hotel served well for a brief overnight stay due to its proximity to the airport. Note that there are no exercise facilities.

description: Horus Horizon INN Pyramids View, located at Buld. 12 in the Al Batran area of Cairo, is an inviting hotel. reviews:
I would not stay here again.
The location is not very good despite the view. Being able to walk around to little stores or boutiques is a great perk for a hotel, and is worth paying a little more. People in this area are not used to tourists, and it’s not very safe to be out at night.
The hotel was very pushy with their tours, I booked two of them, the Nile dinner river cruise is a little overpriced but enjoyable.
The Egypt museum tour is very overpriced and I wouldn’t do it again. If you have time visit the older museum of Egyptian civilization in Cairo. They did upgrade my room and give me a free ride from the airport here for booking the tours, that was nice.
On some sites online it says airport shuttle but they will provide you a taxi for a hefty fee, Uber here is very cheap so don’t be tricked.
Breakfast starts at 8 which is normally fine, but if you want to get out to do a tour or go sightseeing early then you will miss breakfast. Breakfast the one time I had it, was very good.
The attitude of the staff is very weird here, I prefer to be left alone in hotels, especially as the English here isn’t great, but people wanted to know all the time where I was going or what I was doing, very weird ambiance.
It’s a good value hotel if you’re looking to save money.
My biggest issue with the hotel is that they only accept cash. This is fine at boutiques when you only have to pay small amounts but for the room and the tours, I was very unhappy with all the cash I had to take out at the atm. I got in from the airport very early and had no cash almost immediately, not a great feeling when you’re in a new area. Also there are not atms close to the hotel so you would need to go on a walk or get a ride.

description: TETOUAN SPA NEW CAIRO, located at In front of, Katameya Heights Road in the New Cairo 1 area of Cairo, is a well-regarded massage spa. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.8-star rating from 243 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. address: In front of, Katameya Heights Road, New Cairo 1, Cairo Governorate 11861
reviews:
Overall, we enjoyed the experience, we only did a full body relaxing massage. It’s ladies only, we came a few minutes late and faced a very short waiting time (5-10 minutes).

My masseuse was Rehab. She was great - not too rough, not too light. Very thorough and great ambiance. The only issue - and not sure if this was a communication error on my part since I am not Arab and only a beginner Arabic student - is that the lady at the front desk said 50 minutes, but the massage lasted closer to 25-30 minutes, with the rest in the sauna. My guest who was with me, she wasn’t taken to the sauna (we were in separate rooms; I don’t believe they have rooms for multiple women).

Additionally, at the end, they pushed me to post a five star review, and when I said my connection was weak (my data wasn’t working), had me connect to the WiFi to do it. That isn’t unique to this place, but I dislike the push for five star reviews because 1) an artificially high rating actually is suspicious (think, 20 people rate a place 5 stars versus 300 people rate a place with an average of 4.7 stars, statistics everyone) and 2) good places can have a few things to be aware of. No place is perfect.

Overall, I enjoyed the experience here, for a reasonable cost (1600 EGP for two), and they were responsive on WhatsApp.

Note that the spa is situated in the Triumph Hotel. If you enter from the main entrance, take the elevator down to the Ground Floor, and it’s all the way at the end of the hallway.

Firstly, we know that hotels in Egypt are rarely what they promise, however, honestly this place sucked. Upon arrival we were asked to cancel our Booking reservation due to “maintenance” and then pay in cash for another room- for a 20 USD discount said reception. However the new amount was still on par with our booking reservation and we were put in a worse room than we had booked. The room itself was ok, however stunk of cigarette smoke from the open fan grid to a courtyard outside and had a bathroom in a weird glass cube in the corner (not sound or light proof which is hardly romantic). It was loud (but everywhere in Cairo is), but the real disappointment was the immediate scam practice (so the hotel can avoid booking fees and tax, and downgrade us). reviews:
Mosque of Prince Bashtak, or later known as Mustafa Fadil Pasha mosque, is one of the lesser known historical mosques in Cairo.

Built in 1330s by Prince Bashtak, one of the very close figures to the Mamluk Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, and the husband of his daughter.

In 1861, mother of Mustafa Fadil Pasha, brother of Khedive Ismail, built a house, a sabil and a kuttab in front of the mosque, and ordered for the mosque to be renovated.

Nothing remains of the old mosque built by Bashtak except for the main entrance and the minaret. Everything else is from the 1800s renovations.

I would love for the area to be renovated and put on the touristic map of Old Cairo.

I stayed at the hotel for three days. It's a great place for price/value.
Location #1. Just a few steps from the Nile River. With a wonderful restaurant on the bank. Good quiet place to have breakfast (if you prefer it to the (decent) hotel breakfast) or lunch. Walking distance to the Cairo National Opera, and a must visit if there are any performances. There I saw the Chinese Ballet and it was really an amazing experience to see Chinese ballet in Cairo. A true globalization.
Just one metro stop from Tahrir Square (we've all seen it on TV). And there is the National Museum. A huge labyrinth of ancient artifacts that we have never seen or could imagine, such as 3,000-year-old flutes. Mummies and beautiful stone faces of Egyptian princesses. And my favorites: the portraits of the Fayum mummies.
#2 It's comfortable. I had my own reservations thinking that facing the busy El-Tahrir Street might be noisy. By no means. The hotel rooms start on the sixth floor, so it is quiet. The next day, the management offered me an even better room facing the backyard for the same price, and it had Western TV and everything.
#3 Management. They are extremely friendly, respond to all your requests and speak good English. It's like home, somewhere in NJ.
It's not 5***** but it's great value for travellers on a budget.

description: Tiring Historic Building, located at 2 Al Esielli in the El Mosky area of Cairo, is a well-regarded landmark. reviews:
Visible slightly to the north from the narrow overpass that links Opera Square to Azhar Street is a corner building with four kneeling Atlas statues lifting a glass globe. This was the Tiring Department Store, one of Cairo’s many houses of early twentieth century shopping and consumption of modern goods.
The store was founded in 1910 by Victor Tiring, an Austrian merchant born in Istanbul who specialized in Turkish tailoring. The Tiring family had built its first store in Vienna in 1882. The building was designed by Oscar Horowitz, a Czech architect who studied in Vienna and who designed similar shopping destinations within the Austro-Hungarian sphere. The Tiring Store in Cairo was completed in 1912 and when it opened it was the city’s premier shopping destination for imported luxury goods. With the events of World War I, the British occupation in Egypt had deemed all Austrians and Hungarians as enemies and forced their departure from Egypt. The Tiring department store was only in business for few years and its business was interrupted due to pressure from the colonial administration which forced it into liquidation by 1920.

One of the most beautiful architecture in Cairo, Though it's one of the most forgotten places in this huge city!

name: West Pyramids Hotel
description: West Pyramids Hotel, located at 4 El-Salam in the Al Haram area of Cairo, is a well-regarded hotel. reviews:
I spent 6 days in the West Pyramids Hotel with a lovely view from the balcany to the pyramids. The view was amazing, we were having breakfast while being able to see the pyramids just in front of us. The service itself was also amazing as the staff was always very kind and looking forward to help with anything. They were also very friendly when we asked some information about the area. I have also asked the staff from the hotel to book an uber from the hotel to the airport which they provided very kindly! If you go to Egipt you probably have seen people getting scammed with ubers and giving that option just gave me an extra tranquility. The uber itself is a bit more expensive but is worth the price as you get peace of mind. I would like to thank all the staff from the West Pyramids and highly recommend. The rooms are also clean daily if you would like to. They also offer activities like quad bike riding, tour to the pyramids etc. The only thing is that the tv in the room didn't work, but we have access to their wi-fi so in my opinion that was minor. The location is also very good, you just 5-10min walk away from the pyramids and you have a supermarket not too far away. If you need to get an uber it has also a good collection point just outside the hotel where you can wait for it. Thanks once again to the staff from West Pyramids Hotel.

Striking Fatimid-era congregational mosque from 1160, the last one built before the Ayyubids. Like other early mosques it's very simple. Main decoration is the Kufic script carved around the windows.

All the column capitals are different, each taken from different Christian buildings. The bronze on the exterior of the main door is from 1303 (the wood is new), and the minbar is from 1300. Definitely worth a quick visit.
A great example of historical mosques in Cairo, unfortunately, it has been deteriorating and it lack maintenance.
An amazing Fatimid mosque with very beautiful stucco and wood work

A Glimpse into Time: The Zoological Museum at Giza Zoo

🐾🐘🦓🦒🐍🦉✨

The Zoological Museum, nestled within the Giza Zoo, is not just a museum; it's a living testament to Egypt's commitment to wildlife preservation. Established in 1906 and relocated to its current site in 1914, the museum has undergone several renovations, with the latest redevelopment and reopening in August 2015, transforming it into a three-story marvel.

🏰 Historical Evolution:
The Zoological Museum stands as the pioneer animal museum within the Giza Zoo, a cornerstone of Egypt's natural history. Its journey began in 1906, and over the years, it has been rejuvenated in 1962, 1988, and the grand reopening in 2015. Step inside, and you'll find yourself traversing through time, witnessing the evolution of the museum itself.

🌍 Panoramic Diversity:
Designed to complement natural environments, the museum's panoramas boast a rich biological diversity. Housing rare or extinct mammals, birds, and preserved reptiles, the exhibits provide a captivating insight into Egypt's wildlife heritage. It's a breathtaking journey through ecosystems that have shaped the region over centuries.

📚 Educational Halls:
Within the museum's walls are two halls, one housing a complete scientific collection of Egyptian birds, reptiles, mammals, and rodents for research purposes. The other hosts training sessions for students and wildlife enthusiasts, led by experts dedicated to raising environmental awareness and preserving wildlife. Historic photographs of dignitaries who visited the zoo in bygone eras add a fascinating touch.

🔄 Renovation and Revival:
The museum has been a witness to its own history, experiencing renewal in 1962, followed by another in 1988. After an 18-year closure from 1998 to 2015, it emerged, renewed and reimagined, offering a modern and engaging experience for visitors.

🦓 A Collection of Stories:
Most of the animals and structures in the museum were once inhabitants of the zoo, memorialized through taxidermy due to age or illness. Additionally, there are specimens sourced externally, including the "Ostrich of the Nile" presented by King Farouk in 1943 and various preserved birds and mammals.

📸 Photography Friendly:
Capture the magic without worry! Photographing is allowed within the museum premises at no extra cost. Document your journey through time and share the wonders of the Zoological Museum with friends and family.

📊 Impressive Numbers:
With 1,352 preserved birds, 555 mammals, 259 reptiles, 115 skulls, 49 heads, and 35 skeletal structures, the museum is a treasure trove of zoological wonders. Some specimens date back over a century, echoing the rich history of the zoo itself and the late 19th century.

🕒 Practical Information:
📍 Location: Giza Zoo, Egypt
🕒 Hours: 10:00–15:00 (Closed on Tuesdays)
💰 Admission: 10 EGP

The Zoological Museum at Giza Zoo isn't just a collection of exhibits; it's a living narrative of Egypt's wildlife legacy. A visit here is not merely a trip through a museum but a journey through time and the wonders of the natural world.

Happy Exploring! 🌿🦒🦉🌺

The Coptic Orthodox Church of St. Barbara is a church in Coptic Cairo and one best known for its relic of Saint Barbara. The church isn’t all that interesting except for the traditional Coptic style altar with a screen, and the room housing … More

St. Barbara Church is one of many historical churches in Coptic Cairo that each has its unique story and historical significance.

The church was originally dedicated to Saints Cyrus & John, and when the remains of St. Barbara were brought here, a separate sanctuary was built. Thus, there are now two separate churches that were built on this location.

Athanasius, a wealthy scribe and a secretary of Abdulaziz Ibn Marwan (governor of Egypt between 685 and 705 AD), had built the church. A door found during one of the church's many restorations could date as early as the 4th century. Between 1072 and 1073, the church was fully restored to house the relics of Saint Barbara. These relics remain to this day.

The church was damaged again by another fire during the 12th century. The church was most recently renovated extensively between 1910 and 1922.

We were on a Nile cruise on this boat from the 24th November to the 1st December.
First the good news, the staff were in the main attentive and helpful, albeit lacking training in the cocktail bar - pouring a gin and tonic is not difficult. The food was very good with good variety and quantity.
Cruising down the Nile from the sundeck was a delight and the tours were excellent.
Unfortunately much of this was put in the shade by the appalling state of the boat itself.
Once we got the cabin we had paid for on the third try it turned out the bed sheets were filthy and had to be replaced. Attempts at freshening up the cabin with paint were spoilt by paint overrun and splashes on the dark wood surrounds. The shower tray was peeling paint and the basin leaked. Everywhere was evidence of an old boat that had not been correctly maintained resulting in a shabby condition, worn carpets and a tired look.
Photos I saw of fellow guest cabins showed black mould in the shower tray and a permanently leaking toilet cistern.
The communal toilets next to the restaurant were disgraceful with peeling paint, no paper towel or soap and wet floors.
Overall I would hesitate to rate the boat a 1 star and would definitely not recommend it to anyone regardless of price.

Just after the wali had opened the door and went about his business and just before the call for the mid-afternoon prayer and the gathering of worshipers. After the brief vestibule I entered the main prayer space. The cruciform planned prayer area had a central square space flanked by an iwan on each of its sides, shallow on the North and South and deeper on the West and East (qibla side). This central space was capped with a square stone band supporting four squinches (muqarnas) that supported an intricately decorated octagonal wooden lantern. The light that showered in was well defined and golden.

name: Mostafa Kamel Museum
description:
The Mostafa Kamel Museum is a museum in Cairo. It was officially opened in April 1956. Before that, it was a mausoleum containing the remains of the two leaders, Mustafa Kamel and Muhammad Farid. It also houses the remains of the intellectuals and activists, Abd al-Rahman al-Rafei and Fathi Radwan. The museum is built in the style of the Islamic mausoleum dome and includes two halls containing some of the belongings of the leader Mustafa Kamel represented in his books and letters in his handwriting, and some pictures of his friends and relatives, as well as some of his personal belongings of clothes, dining utensils, and his office room. The museum also includes oil paintings depicting the Denshway incident. On February 8, 2001, the museum reopened after being restored.
The museum was vandalized and its contents were stolen on January 28, 2011, during the 2011 Egyptian revolution, and it was recovered by the tourism police and was restored. The museum was further restored with internal and external renovation and the restoration of the garden, fences, and office furniture. The exhibit display also was updated with the addition of rare photographs that show historical moments of Kamel and his closest companions' lives. The museum opened again in April 2016. 
It is free for all visitors.
address: 27H4+VW8, Al Abageyah, El Khalifa, Cairo Governorate 4252335
reviews:
Mostafa Kamel Museum is a fascinating cultural site dedicated to the life and legacy of Mustafa Kamel, a prominent Egyptian nationalist and political leader. The museum houses a collection of personal artifacts, photographs, manuscripts, and historical documents that provide deep insight into his role in Egypt’s modern history.

The exhibits are well-organized, informative, and engaging for visitors interested in Egyptian politics, history, and the nationalist movement. The museum’s atmosphere is quiet and respectful, making it an ideal place for learning and reflection.

While relatively modest in size compared to larger museums, Mostafa Kamel Museum offers a rich and educational experience for those seeking to understand Egypt’s journey toward independence and the influential figures behind it.

We had a horrendous experience, the one nightmare of our Egypt trip (everywhere else was nice). We arrived at 11pm with our 10-year old throwing up from the horrendous driving of their driver (every other driver in Egypt was fine). They made us pay in advance (do not pay in advance! no other hotel makes you pay before checkout) and, before we could realize what had happened, they said they added a $20 “government tax” to the transaction. When we complained they then said it was a “booking fee”, yet our reservation was through booking.com so taxes were included. So they started by stealing $20 from us. It gets worst: they had made us take all our luggage out of the shuttle. Once we paid in the lobby they said “congrats we upgraded you, the driver will bring you to our other location 5 minutes away”. The 10 year old was crying because she did not want to go back with the awful driver. I told the hotel we don’t want an upgrade, we need to put the kids to bed (it was 11:30pm by then), they replied the original rooms were also in the other location. We did not have a choice, and arrived at the new location. We said we will take our luggage with us because we need to go to bed we don’t want to wait for our luggage. They made us go to the reception of the new hotel at the top floor without helping us at all, then after 15 more minutes made us come back down to the room (it was midnight). We had booked two different rooms, instead they gave us one room with one shower for 7 of us.. we were so exhausted we went in. We found the bathroom dirty, with pee on the toilet seat and inside the hole, very moldy and prior trash not taken out. I also included her a picture of the hallway outside our room, from a horror film (taken with flash as no light). Also there were no towels even to wash our hands, my husband spent 30minutes trying to get towels at midnight, after 30 minutes they gave him two wet towels for 7 of us. Other guests were there also mad looking for towels, they had no clean towels for anyone. We gave up, tried to sleep despite the strong street and road noises. I should also note in the meantime at 11pm I had told them we had not eaten the past day and needed food, they said no problem there is food at the rooftop of the new location until midnight. When we arrived he made me walk upstairs to the rooftop and they did not have any food so I went to get food in the streets. Finally, they also told us they would pack breakfast so we could leave at 8am (time of breakfast start). Whn my husband went upstairs to pick up the breakfast in the morning, he was told they did not do packed breakfast and it was against their policy to let guests take food out. In summary we barely slept, could not shower and eat. Stay away!!

reviews: It is one of so many historical mosques in Cairo

It is the mosque of the mystic Sheikh Muhammad Abu al-Saud al-Jarhi, who died in 933 AH. It is one of the ancient mosques of Egypt and is located east of the Amr ibn al-Aas Mosque in the Kom al-Jarhi area, about 500 meters past the King … More

One of the ancient mosques of Cairo, located east of the Mosque of Amr ibn al-As near the Kom al-Jarhi area, it is named after its founder, the Sufi master Abu al-Saud al-Jarhi, a prominent figure in the 10th century AH.

It consists of two parts: the front prayer hall, which comprises three arcades, built atop the old mosque constructed by Abd al-Rahman Katkhuda in 1158 AH. The current mosque is devoid of ornamentation and inscriptions. The minbar, mihrab, ceiling, and windows are all modern, as are the walls, which have been painted with contemporary paint. The original features of the mosque include six marble columns with restored capitals, and a door on the southern side topped by a triple arch.

reviews:
Systematic overbooking, downgrade, and total lack of management responsibility

This review follows an already unacceptable experience with another hotel the day before, and unfortunately the second day was even worse.

We arrived at 12:00 PM, left our luggage, and were clearly told not to worry because our check-in was confirmed (as we were told the day before when we texted them since we just had a bad experience). We then left to visit the Grand Egyptian Museum, based on that assurance.

When we returned at 4:30 PM, we were informed that there was an overbooking with a guest that did not check out and that we would be redirected to another hotel. We were told it was “the same level,” which was simply not true.

We went to see the alternative hotel ourselves and found that it was:
•	Clearly inferior to what we booked
•	A downgrade in quality, comfort, and location
•	Without the pyramid view we had specifically paid for

We immediately asked for a fair and honest solution at the same level as our original booking. None was offered.

To make matters worse:
•	we couldn’t talk to the manager, claiming he does not speak English
•	Responsibility was delegated to staff who had no authority and offered no real solutions
•	No compensation, no proper relocation, no accountability

In the end, we were forced to book another hotel ourselves, at a much higher price, far from the city center, without the pyramid view, and not comparable to what we originally reserved in October.

On top of this, we had to pay for:
•	Additional taxis to reach the new hotel
•	Extra transportation to make it in time for our New Year’s Eve dinner

This is not an isolated incident — it is a pattern of overbooking, poor planning, and complete disregard for guests. What is most unacceptable is the absence of management, the refusal to take responsibility, and the lack of honest, professional solutions.

I strongly warn future guests: do not rely on this hotel’s confirmations. If you are traveling during a busy period, for a special occasion, or expecting a specific standard, you are taking a serious risk.

Management should be ashamed of how this situation was handled.
