name: Fortress of Babylon
description:
Babylon Fortress (Coptic: ⲡⲁⲃⲓⲗⲱⲛ or Ⲃⲁⲃⲩⲗⲱⲛ) is an ancient Roman fortress on the eastern bank of the Nile Delta, located in the area known today as Old Cairo or Coptic Cairo. The fortress was built circa 300 AD by Emperor Diocletian in order to protect the entrance to an ancient canal, previously rebuilt by Trajan, that linked the Nile with the Red Sea. 
It was at the boundary between Lower and Middle Egypt, where the river craft paid tolls when ascending or descending the Nile. Within the fortress's former enclosure are the present-day Coptic Museum, a convent, and several churches, including the Church of St. George and the Hanging Church.
address: 264H+8X2, Mar Grgs, Koum Ghrab, Old Cairo, Cairo Governorate 4244001
reviews:
FORTRESS OF BABYLON - WHERE EMPIRES CONVERGE IN QUIET GRANDEUR

We visited the historic Fortress of Babylon in Cairo one pleasant afternoon in January 2026 as part of a large group from India touring Egypt. Located in the heart of Old Cairo’s Coptic quarter, this remarkable site offered us a deeply evocative journey through layers of civilisation. We were told that the ancient city of Memphis is not far from here.

The approach itself is memorable. Walking through the narrow, winding streets of Coptic Cairo, lined with ancient walls and timeless structures, we felt transported back centuries. Fortunately, the area was not very crowded that afternoon, allowing us to absorb the surroundings in relative calm and reflect on the immense historical significance of the place.

Standing before the towering stone remnants of the Roman-era fortress was truly surreal. These massive walls and bastions, built nearly two millennia ago, have silently witnessed the transition of Egypt from its ancient Pharaonic heritage to the Greek and later Roman periods. One cannot help but feel humbled by the continuity of history embodied here. The fortress once served as a strategic military stronghold along the Nile and later became the nucleus around which early Christian communities of Cairo flourished.

Today, the remains of the fortress coexist harmoniously with some of the most revered churches and monuments of Coptic Cairo, making the entire area a living museum of faith and history. Our visit here was not merely about viewing old stones but about experiencing a space where civilisations intersected and evolved. For anyone interested in history and heritage, the Fortress of Babylon offers a rare and contemplative encounter with the enduring legacy of Egypt’s past.

A very significant historical structure, whispering of a bygone Roman dominance over Egypt.

The fortress was built in 300 AD by Emperor Diocletian in order to protect the entrance to an ancient canal, previously rebuilt by Trajan, that linked the Nile with the Red Sea.

It was at the boundary between Lower and Middle Egypt, where the river craft paid tolls when ascending or descending the Nile.

According to the 7th-century writer John of Nikiu, the name "Babylon" was given by Nebuchadnezzar II, who conquered or campaigned in the area in 568 BC. He named it after his own home city. John also reported that the fortress was first founded by Nebuchadnezzar.

During the Arab conquest of Egypt the Byzantine fortress held out for about seven months before finally falling in December 640 to the Arab general 'Amr ibn al-'As.

Every detail in the design reflects elegance, power, and a deep connection to Egypt’s ancient history, brought to life in a modern way.

What I loved the most is how the space makes you feel small in the best way — reminding you that you’re standing in the heart of a future capital that’s being built to impress the world. And at night, with the lights on, the whole scene turns magical.

If you love photography or just want to experience a place that gives you pride in Egypt’s future — The Pillars Hall is a must-visit. It’s not just a place… it’s an experience.

ASK FOR "RAAOF" AS A DRIVER! I went all over the middle east and out of the dozen or so drivers I had, Raaof in Cairo was definitely the best! Bright young man, very good english, studied tourism and history in college so he can give you a lot of insight both past and present into Egypt. In addition to showing me all over Cairo, making sure my experience at the pyramids was amazing, and spending entire days with me, he also went above and beyond by picking me up at the airport even though I arrived at midnight, and dropping me off when I left at 4AM. Very trustworthy. He truly made my experience in Cairo epic but most importantly SAFE. He's much more then a driver, he's a guide (a very good one) and now a friend.

There are nicer more expensive places to stay but given the overall experience if you consider yourself a "traveler" more then a "tourist" you really need to stay here and spend a couple days with Mohamed and Raaof, let them show you Cairo with a locals perspective. They are both very professional and likeable guys.

name: The Gate Hotel Pyramids
description: The Gate Hotel Pyramids, located in the Nazlet Elsaman area of Cairo, is a standout hotel. It is well rated, holding a 4.2-star rating from 168 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. Visitors frequently note rooftop seating, pleasant views, and friendly service. address: X4GR+85Q, Abolhol Elsiahy, 29, Nazlet Elsaman, Giza Governorate
reviews:
We had a fantastic stay at this hotel with an unmatched view. Judging by the reviews, my guess is that the experience really depends on which room you book.

We treated ourselves to the one with the private terrace. This must be one of the closest hotels you can get with a direct view of pyramids and sphinx. The view from the terrace, especially at sunset, was absolutely stunning. You get a similar view from the hotel's restaurant (with less privacy of course).

The room itself was spacious and clean with a comfortable big bed, good hot shower and nice deco (see video). The terrace was hot during the day but does come with a large umbrella. All three pyramids and the sphinx are directly visible from the terrace.

The staff was friendly and attentive from check in to check out. There were some extensions going on on the rooftop and they communicated clearly with us regarding what to expect and came to assist us immediately and apologetically when some of the renovations impacted our terrace.

The food and drinks at the restaurant were average and there are definitely better places to eat in Egypt, so wouldn't necessarily recommend the hotel for dining. Note also that no alcohol is served on the premises and is hard to find in the area in general.

I read people in reviews complaining about the streets being dirty and smelling of horses. The whole area around the pyramids is very crowded and touristy and there are horse cart rides on offer as well as camels walking about. A natural side effect of this is that there'll be smell and dusty backstreets. There are also friendly stray dogs running around. Part of the package when visiting here. We didn't find it to be an issue and certainly couldn't smell anything from the room, terrace or the restaurant.

Also, it's important to keep in mind that this is a tourism area. Lots of street selling, high prices and it can be a bit chaotic. It's hot and dusty. The room with the private terrace was a peaceful safe haven to withdraw to while still being able to enjoy the pyramids.

Plus, the ticket office for the site is right opposite the hotel which makes it really convenient and easy to grab tickets early in the day and saves one walk on an already very walking heavy day.

All in all, for the view alone I truly recommend this place. Having the private terrace was intimate and romantic. We felt like we had the pyramids all to ourselves. Something super special, given the huge crowds that pass through on any given day.

I recently celebrated my graduation at L'Uliveto, and it was truly an unforgettable experience from start to finish.

We were warmly welcomed with a complimentary starter—freshly baked bread paired with a deliciously creamy tuna spread. It was a delightful way to begin the meal and set the tone for what was to come.

For the main course, we ordered the penne arrabbiata with shrimp, and it was absolutely delicious. The pasta was cooked perfectly, and the slight kick of spice made every bite rich and flavorful.

But the real star of the evening was the Italian pizza. The dough was thin, crispy, and incredibly fresh. Since it was a special occasion, they went the extra mile and made us a pizza with two different halves: one side was truffle funghi, earthy and aromatic, and the other was pastrami with cream cheese, which was indulgent and perfectly balanced. They even surprised us with a live pizza show, which added a magical, luxurious touch to the night. It was such a beautiful gesture that made me feel truly celebrated.

For drinks, we tried three different mocktails
The Virgin Maimi was my absolute favorite—refreshing with the perfect hint of coconut.

The Egyptian Breeze was a bold and zesty choice, ideal for sour lovers, with a strong cinnamon note that stood out beautifully.

As someone who doesn’t usually enjoy hibiscus, I was pleasantly surprised by their hibiscus mocktail, it was flavorful and refreshing.

The atmosphere was simply lovely, with an elegant ambiance and a breathtaking view of the Nile that made the evening even more special. The entire staff was kind, welcoming, and attentive—especially Peter, who went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. He was professional, helpful, and added a personal touch to our experience.

In every way, L'Uliveto made my graduation celebration truly extraordinary. It felt warm, joyful, and full of little thoughtful surprises. I can’t recommend this place enough if you’re looking for great food, a beautiful setting, and a memorable experience. Thank you to everyone at L'Uliveto for making it a night I’ll never forget. 🌿✨🎓

Lucky that we had already studied the extensive menu thoroughly before we decided we will dine at L'Uliveto so we quickly passed our selection to the waiter.

reviews:
Rooms - Rooms with view are good. Offer very good view of the Pyramids.
Washrooms- Clean but smells of gutter at times.
Food - Breakfast was buffet style but menu never changes. Guess this is normal in Egypt.
WiFi - Absolutely worst. We complained multiple times but staff seemed least bothered and there was no solution during our 3 days of stay.
Accessibility- On the main road. Getting uber is easy. Can walk to the pyramids. No decent restaurents nearby.
Surrounding- Poor as with entire Giza.
Sleep - Bed is very firm. There is a mosque nearby and you can hear azaan as early as 4.30 in morning repeating thereafter. Its very loud and can be problem for some.
Staff - Reception is good but restaurant staff while breakfast tries to be too friendly and you know why. One of them consistently asked to sign a dollar bill as a memory but it was to clear he wanted tip. We were struggling to book an uber after checkout due to WiFi issue but staff was least bother to come forward to help. Guess it was because we were no longer guest there.

Overall experience was just ok. There are 1000 hotels in the area and I think I will try another one next time.

reviews:
The Arabian or Arab horse (‎ [ ħisˤaːn ʕarabiː], DMG ḥiṣān ʿarabī) is a breed of horse that originated on the Arabian Peninsula. With a distinctive head shape and high tail carriage, the Arabian is one of the most easily recognizable horse breeds in the world. It is also one of the oldest breeds, with archaeological evidence of horses in the Middle East that resemble modern Arabians dating back 4,500 years. Throughout history, Arabian horses have spread around the world by both war and trade, used to improve other breeds by adding speed, refinement, endurance, and strong bone. Today, Arabian bloodlines are found in almost every modern breed of riding horse.

The Arabian developed in a desert climate and was prized by the nomadic Bedouin people, often being brought inside the family tent for shelter and protection from theft. Selective breeding for traits including an ability to form a cooperative relationship with humans created a horse breed that is good-natured, quick to learn, and willing to please. The Arabian also developed the high spirit and alertness needed in a horse used for raiding and war. This combination of willingness and sensitivity requires modern Arabian horse owners to handle their horses with competence and respect.

The Arabian is a versatile breed. Arabians dominate the discipline of endurance riding, and compete today in many other fields of equestrian sport. They are one of the top ten most popular horse breeds in the world. They are now found worldwide, including the United States and Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, continental Europe, South America (especially Brazil), and their land of origin, the Middle East.

This historic mosque built by the Fatamids originally and recently restored by the Egyptian govt in collaboration with the Bohra community is said to hold the shrine of Sayyida Ruqaia bint Ali (ra), the daughter of Imam Ali (as). reviews:
During our trip, we stayed at six hotels in different cities in Egypt, and this hotel is the best in its price range! It's perfectly located downtown – close to lots of cafes and restaurants, Cairo's most fashionable streets with European architecture, and two metro stations. The hotel itself is on the 7th floor and looks very nice and fresh – it's clear it was recently renovated. The staff are very friendly and pleasant, always ready to help! Our flight from Aswan was delayed, and we didn't arrive at the hotel until 2:00 AM to check in. We were graciously greeted at reception, and a boy from the kitchen even came and brought us drinks so we could relax in the lobby while the receptionist processed our paperwork.
We were quite annoying guests – first, our friend needed a place to stay for the evening, as his bus from Cairo wasn't until 1:00 AM, and the hotel staff kindly allowed him to rest in the hotel lobby. Then we needed to buy tickets to the new Grand Egyptian Museum, but they only accepted cards, which we didn't have. We asked reception to buy tickets online, and they helped us! Plus, my friend and I are from Tatarstan so we love to drink tea A LOT, so every day, even at midnight or later, we asked for tea—and there was always a hotel staff member awake at reception who kindly made it for us.
The room, like the rest of the hotel, was very clean. The beds were comfortable, there was a large closet with hangers and shelves, a nightstand and two nightlights, a TV, and good Wi-Fi. We had an en suite bathroom with hot water (not all hotels have that!)).
Thank you very much to the hotel staff for the warm welcome!

My stay at this hotel was truly one of the best experiences I’ve ever had. From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with a warm smile and genuine care for the guests’ comfort. What impressed me the most was the incredible location — the hotel offers a direct view of the Pyramids, and the scenery from both the room and the rooftop makes you feel like you’re living right in the heart of history. Watching the Sound & Light Show at night from the rooftop was breathtaking, and the sunrise and sunset views were simply unforgettable.

The room was spacious, spotless, and equipped with everything I needed. The bed was extremely comfortable, which made my sleep peaceful and deep. The bathroom was clean and well-maintained, which is something I personally value a lot. The Wi-Fi was fast and stable, allowing me to get some work done while still enjoying the view.

Breakfast on the rooftop was beyond amazing — delicious food, fresh coffee, and the Pyramids right in front of you! It honestly felt like being in a painting. I also really appreciated the staff; they were super friendly and always ready to help, whether arranging tours or providing transportation. I never felt like just another guest, but truly like a valued visitor.

In short, this hotel is not just a place to stay, it’s a complete experience that combines comfort, excellent service, and the unforgettable magic of history. I highly recommend it to anyone visiting Cairo or Giza, and I will definitely be coming back again soon.

We strongly and unequivocally do NOT recommend this hotel.

Hotel is on good place and has a good view of pyramids, unfortunately as close as we are to pyramids and after reading the reviews that they are just 10 min by walking it’s not true anymore. Entrance in front of hotel is permanently closed. You can’t walk to pyramids anymore. We came to check in at 12 but they told us that guests still didn’t check out, and check out is at 12 maximum !!!! We waited for thirty more minutes and asked again but receptionist said same thing again. They don’t follow rules, they could at least offer us different room at the moment. Then for next one hour whenever we ask the receptionist said they are cleaning and it will be ready in five minutes. Totally after 1 hour and half of waiting we got to our room and what we saw? Not the room that was cleaned for one hour. On the “new” bedsheet we found hair from previous guests, for shower they gave us one set of towels and they know it’s two of us here, they also left just one pair of slippers… there were two packages of coffee and tea but no water… we had. Even if room was not cleaned good, guys that clean them look very nice and polite. Also i would like to give a plus point to only male receptionist, while i was there he was working in night, he was very very kind and nice and he tried everything in his control to help us enjoy our stay. They don’t clean room every day, it’s on request. Unfortunately toilet smell is awful, you just can’t get rid of it. Wifi doesn’t work… when we wanted to check out receptionist asked for my phone to show her my reservation at booking even if no one ever asked me that. I was confused and i gave her my phone. Later after we left hotel i found out that she wrote a review without my permission. Of course she put 5 stars and wrote that it was excellent place. I felt betrayed. Im sad to leave this type of review when there were some on nice workers and good view of pyramids.

description: Abu Dahab Mosque, located at 24 Gameaa Al Azhar in the El Gamaliya area of Cairo, is a much-loved mosque. It is exceptionally well rated, holding a 4.7-star rating from 139 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. Visitors frequently note pleasant views and a traditional feel. address: 24 Gameaa Al Azhar, El-Darb El-Ahmar, El Gamaliya, Cairo Governorate 11311
reviews:
Abu Dhahab (nickname meaning “Father of Gold”) built this mosque when he was at the height of his power, in 1774. The project represents the last of the great religious complexes built by Mameluke beys for the benefit of Islam. The plan of the mosque is a modified copy of the Turkish mosque of Sinan Pasha in Boulaq but the minaret has nothing to do with Ottoman style: it resembles more closely the minaret of the Mosque of al-Ghuri, located not far away.
When Abu-Dhahab died in Palestine in 1775, while attacking the fortress of Acre, his body was brought back to Cairo and buried in the tomb that he built for himself. The tomb area is protected by bronze grilles and decorated with tiles crafted in Tunisia.
The guide of this mosque is one of the kindness persons I met in Cairo. I would recommend a visit on the roof, which gives you the chance to admire the majestic main façade of Al-Azhar mosque, located next door. A very interesting feature that could be seen while visiting the roof is a solar clock, which is beautiful and insanely accurate.
Unique architecture surrounded by Islamic traditional shops. It'll be better if they allow people to pray inside it. More

We stayed at this hotel for several nights and ate at the restaurant “The Blue” every day. The food was amazing and the service outstanding - a special thank you to Ahmed and Amr, who were very attentive and friendly! The most important thing for me as someone with coeliac disease was that they offered multiple gluten-free options, which were clearly marked on the menu (e.g., risotto, steak, salad, carpaccio, lamb, gelato). They also serve gluten-free bread. At breakfast, there is a small gluten-free section, boiled eggs, and lots of fruit. I didn’t have a reaction, and everything was absolutely delicious. Would recommend staying at this hotel (Kempinski) and eating at “The Blue” when visiting Cairo!

La chiesa è dedicata all'Evangelista Marco e ne conserva alcune reliquie trasportate dalla Basilica di San Marco a Venezia.

The cathedral of San Marco is the main Coptic church of Egypt and home of the Coptic Pope. Located in the district of Abbassia, the current building was built under Cirillo VI and inaugurated in 1968.

The church is dedicated to the Evangelist Mark and preserves some relics carried from the Basilica of San Marco in Venice.

Amir Khayrbak Funerary Complex is a remarkable historic site in Cairo, showcasing Mamluk architecture and craftsmanship. The complex includes a mosque, mausoleum, and various intricately decorated structures that highlight the elegance of … More

Fully restored madrasa and mosque. Burial site as well. Very simple with elaborate wood work and columns. Notice some columns are taken from ancient Egypt site and the entry stones are in part have hieroglyphics some rubbed away from use for over 800 years.

Little known as a monument, but this mosque is the last mamelouk style mosque just before the Turkey invasion for Egypt in 1516 A.D. its value comes from the unique coloured glass in its windows, also from the traitorous roul played by its founder Khayer bey delivering Egypt to 400 years of Turkey occupation

I went there, I love Islamic Cairo mosques.
Amir Khayer Bek, a former governor of Aleppo under
the last Mamluk sultan al-Ghuri, was appointed as the
fi rst Ottoman governor of Cairo following the Ottoman
conquest of Egypt in 1517. Khayrbek Mosque, a religious
and funerary complex, was built between 1502
and 1520 adjacent to Khayer Bek’s residence, the Alin
Aq Palace (13th–14th century). The sabil (public water
source) of Janim al-Hamzawy (1532) was erected
nearby, as were two Ottoman houses (17th century). In
1884, an earthquake caused serious damage to the
top of the Khayrbek Mosque minaret, leading to the
collapse of its pavilion. In 2002, in coordination with
the Supreme Council of Antiquities (SCA), AKTC started
reconstruction of the upper part of the minaret and a
conservation project involving the entire complex and
adjacent structures.

World wonder, world-class mismanagement.

The pyramids themselves are, of course, extraordinary. Unfortunately, the experience around them is one of the worst examples of tourism management I’ve ever encountered.
Despite extremely high entrance and ride prices (by any Western standard), the site is chaotic, aggressively commercialized, and ethically troubling. Camel rides in particular involve visibly underweight, injured, and overworked animals with poor tack and no apparent welfare oversight. Horses generally appear in better condition, but the contrast only highlights how bad the camel situation is.
Handlers are relentlessly pushy, “help” is forced with payment expected, and there is virtually no sense of regulation, professionalism, or accountability — astonishing for a closed, controlled site that generates massive revenue. This is not a poverty issue; it’s a governance failure.
What makes it especially frustrating is that this could be done well. Proper licensing, animal welfare enforcement, standardized pricing, and basic visitor management would improve conditions for animals, locals, and tourists alike — while still being profitable.
An unforgettable monument overshadowed by exploitation and chaos. See it once, but be prepared, and don’t expect a respectful or ethical visitor experience.

reviews:
CURRENTS OF CIVILISATION - THE BOAT GALLERY AT THE GEM

We visited the boat section toward the end of our tour of the main Grand Egyptian Museum complex in the last week of January 2026, as part of a large group. Emerging from the monumental galleries into this section was striking; it offered a quieter yet equally powerful perspective on ancient Egyptian life. The display left us deeply impressed and complemented the broader narrative of the museum. After entering this part of the museum what you could do is to take a lift to the top floor and come down the three levels through a sloping path.

The gallery provides a clear and engaging account of Nile-based boat traditions and the centrality of mobility in shaping Egyptian civilisation. From ceremonial vessels to utilitarian river craft, the exhibits illustrate how transportation, trade, and ritual movement were intertwined with daily life and state formation. The section gives visitors an excellent understanding of how the Nile functioned not merely as a river, but as the civilisational spine of Egypt.

What stands out is the implicit ecological sensitivity reflected in these traditions—boat design, material use, and navigation practices reveal a society closely aligned with its natural environment. The presentation helps connect technological ingenuity with environmental awareness.

Overall, this segment is an enriching conclusion to the museum visit. It broadens historical appreciation beyond monuments and artefacts, highlighting movement, ecology, and riverine knowledge as foundational elements of ancient Egyptian civilisation.

Must see museum, absolutely unique Solar Khufu’s Solar Boat.

The discovery of the Khufu Ship back In 1954 was an unintended discovery. The Khufu ship is one of the two ships rediscovered by Kamal El-Mallakh and is identified as the world's oldest intact ship built for the King Pharaoh Khufu from the 4th Dynasty around 2500 BC. The solar ship was discovered in the midst of the archeological excavations performed in the Giza area during the cleaning process of the Great Pyramids. After discovering a large limestone wall and digging to the very bottom of it 42 pieces of rocks were discovered. Unearthed, yet broken into thousands of pieces laid the Khufu Solar Boat.

Serving as a centerpiece of the Khufu Ship Museum and measuring at 43.6 m (143 ft) long and 5.9 m (19.5 ft) wide the Solar ship is displayed in all its might & glory.

reviews:
Madrasa and Mausoleum of al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub is a historic and architecturally impressive site in Cairo, reflecting the Mamluk era’s grandeur. The complex combines a religious school (madrasa) with the mausoleum of Sultan al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub, offering visitors insight into the educational and spiritual life of the period.

The architecture features elegant stonework, intricate geometric designs, and finely carved inscriptions, demonstrating the sophistication and artistry of Mamluk craftsmen. The serene courtyards and prayer halls provide a peaceful atmosphere, making it a contemplative space for visitors.

Less crowded than some of Cairo’s more famous monuments, this site allows for an immersive experience into the city’s Islamic heritage. It is a must-visit for history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and anyone interested in Cairo’s rich cultural and religious past.

name: Al-Gawhara Palace
description:
Al-Gawhara Palace (Qaṣr al-Gawhara), also known as Bijou Palace, is a palace and museum in Cairo, Egypt. The palace is situated south of the Mosque of Muhammad Ali in the Cairo Citadel. It was commissioned by Muhammad Ali Pasha in 1814.
The palace was designed and constructed by artisans contracted from a variety of countries, including Greeks, Turks, Bulgarians and Albanians. The artisans constructed a variety of elements as part of the palace complex: "barracks, schools, an arsenal, a gun-powder factory and a mint." The palace was constructed as a two-storey pavilion in the style of a Turkish kushk. It has Western style windows which were often topped with an oval oeil-de-boeuf. The French architect and engineer Pascal Coste was employed to add the residential quarters for the palace servants and functionaries. On one side of the palace was a haush (courtyard) and on the other, were views of the pyramids and the Nile.
In 1822, a fire destroyed the palace's wooden construction in a blaze that lasted for 2 days. Later, Muhammad Ali had the structure expanded and elaborated upon with the construction of "a large marble fountain, columned stone terraces and porticoes, parterres of flower beds and orange groves, and even a menagerie containing a lion, two tigers and an elephant, a gift of the British Lord Hastings."
Two years later, in 1824, fire again damaged the palace after explosions of gunpowder. Muhammad Ali imported large slabs of marble from Italy to ...

reviews:
This is one of those hotels that are great at review-farming but horrible otherwise. Let me walk you through my experience and you will understand what I mean.

We had booked 2 rooms at this hotel, about 2 weeks prior to our arrival. But at arrival, the hotel staff refused to accept our bookings. They kept saying they cant find the booking on their system. Despite showing them all the bookings proofs, vouchers, they still didn't agree to give our rooms. Rather, they kept saying they have last 2 rooms left and we can pay on the property to book them.

After about an hour and multiple calls from our travel agents, they finally "found" our bookings in their system.

The rooms: Very small, low ceilings, dysfunctional plumbing with very low pressure in the taps and non-functional in-room refrigerators. We called them multiple times during our stay to fix the plumbing and the fridges, but to no avail. We somehow completed our stay there.

The checkout: The story completely flips here. The same staff that was rude and unhelpful during our check-in and stay becomes super duper friendly, with wide smiles and long apologies for the inconvenience. New staff members show up as managers just to hear your experience and make tall promises to make everything hunky-dory for our next trip. All this in exchange for what? A good review for them on the socials (review-farming). They start shoving their QR codes in our faces asking for high ratings and good reviews, from every member of my family. They kept waiting for us to give the review, almost not letting us leave without one. It took us further 10-15 mins to get them off our faces and leave peacefully promising a good review on our way back.

We got duped because of the reviews of this hotel, which we now realized must have all been farmed by the hotel staff. Please don't fall for them.

The view of the pyramids was great though! Will give them that.

The location along the Nile boardwalk is great, and although we paid 20EGP for boardwalk entry it was nice to not be hassled by photographers and street vendors while enjoying the atmosphere.

We ordered a hookah while we were still deciding on food and drinks, but nobody came to take our food order until about 20 minutes later when they finally brought the hookah out. After we ordered the rest, it took over 30 minutes for the food to arrive and they didn’t bring the drinks out until we’d finished eating.

The hookah wasn’t working properly for the first 45 minutes we had it, even though we told staff about it multiple times. They eventually fixed it, by simply spreading the shisha out properly, after we had completely finished our meals and most of our drinks. We stayed a while longer to get the most out what we had paid for, but it was certainly not a good experience.

The food was also very disappointing. My wife ordered the lavender lemonade and the spaghetti bolognese. About 10 minutes after we ordered the waiter came back to tell us the lavender was unavailable so my wife had to choose another drink. After another 5 minutes the waiter came back to tell us bolognese was also unavailable, so wife ended up having to completely change her order. Both my chicken alfredo and my wife’s shrimp and mushroom appeared to be made from identical white sauce bases with penne, despite the menu describing a tomato based sauced with spaghetti for the shrimp and mushroom. Both were quite bland and watery.

We paid 1078EGP for the two pasta dishes, two drinks, and a double headed hookah. There are definitely far better food options along the boardwalk, but thankfully this one isn’t overly expensive given the disappointing quality and service.

reviews:
The Hanging Obelisk at the Grand Egyptian Museum

Experience one of Egypt’s most unique modern displays: the Hanging Obelisk. … More

The Hanging Obelisk at the Grand Egyptian Museum

At the entrance plaza of the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) stands a truly unique monument: the Hanging Obelisk of Ramses II. This is the first suspended obelisk in the world, and it offers visitors an extraordinary experience unlike any other.

Originally carved from pink granite in the reign of Pharaoh Ramses II (c. 1279–1213 BC), the obelisk once stood in Tanis (San al-Hagar) in the Nile Delta. Measuring about 16 meters in height and weighing over 110 tons with its base, it was transported to Cairo to become one of the architectural highlights of GEM.

What makes this obelisk remarkable is its innovative presentation. Instead of being mounted upright on solid ground, it is elevated on four massive supporting columns, creating a suspended effect that allows visitors to walk beneath it. For the first time in more than 3,500 years, guests can look upward into the base of the monument to see the royal cartouche of Ramses II engraved there—a feature that was hidden from view when the obelisk stood in its original location.

The concept was developed under the supervision of Major General Atef Moftah, general director of the GEM project, and executed by Orascom Construction and BESIX, with structural solutions designed to ensure both safety and visibility. Around its supporting base, the word “Egypt” is inscribed in multiple world languages, symbolizing Egypt’s message of universality.

Blending ancient craftsmanship with modern engineering, the Hanging Obelisk is more than an artifact—it is an introduction to Egypt’s timeless ability to innovate, inspire, and connect past with present. For many visitors, it is the first encounter with history as they step into the museum, and it sets the stage for the treasures that await inside.

🔝Khentkaus was very likely a daughter of king Neferirkare Kakai and queen Khentkaus II, while her husband was equally likely pharaoh Neferefre, and her son the future pharaoh Menkauhor Kaiu.

🔝Discovery of the tombEdit:

On January 4, 2015, the discovery of her tomb by Czech archaeologists was announced by Egyptian authorities. According to Egyptian Antiquities Minister Mamdouh Eldamaty, there had been no knowledge of the existence of Khentkaus III before this discovery. Two earlier Egyptian queens with the same name have been identified previously, however.

The tomb of Khentkaus III – marked as AC 30– was excavated in Abusir, where there are several pyramids dedicated to pharaohs of the Fifth Dynasty, including Neferefre.The tomb was found near Neferefre's funerary complex by a Czech archaeological team led by Miroslav Bárta of Charles University in Prague, with Egyptian collaboration.

The name and rank of Khentkaus was inscribed on the inner walls of the tomb, probably by the builders.Her burial place is a mastaba with an underground burial chamber that is reached via a shaft.The reliefs in the tomb identified her both as "the wife of the king" and "the mother of the king", implying her son ascended the throne.Statuettes and twenty-four travertine utensils, along with four copper utensils (which were part of the funerary objects), also have been found in the tomb. The tomb is dated to the middle of the Fifth Dynasty.

The archaeologists who uncovered the tomb believed it to be that of Neferefre's wife, because it was close to his complex, in a small cemetery southeast of the complex.Eldamaty stated: "This discovery will help us shed light on certain unknown aspects of the Fifth Dynasty, which along with the Fourth Dynasty, witnessed the construction of the first pyramids."
The architecture of Tomb of Queen Khentkawes is as old as sphinx! The other sphinx head facing west is here!

The pyramid of Khentkaus I or step tomb of Khentkaus I is a Fourth Dynasty two-stepped tomb built for the Queen Mother Khentkaus I in Giza. The tomb, built in two phases coinciding with its two steps, was originally known as the fourth … More

The tomb bears the name "Khentkaus III", a queen that was not known to archaeologists before. It was discovered during excavations carried out by a Czech mission, in cooperation with the Ministry of Antiquities in the archaeological area of ​​"Abu Sir", west of Cairo.
Also found were 24 vessels made of limestone, and 4 copper tools, which represent part of the funerary furniture for the owner of the tomb. Inscriptions were also discovered on the side walls of the burial chamber, bearing between its lines the name and titles of the owner of the tomb, including "the king's wife", and "" The king's mother."

reviews:
Oud Café – A Perfect Sohour Spot with Great Shisha & Service

If you’re looking for a cozy and welcoming place to enjoy sohour, Oud Café is a top-notch choice. The ambiance is relaxed, making it a great spot to unwind, whether you’re there for a late-night meal, a good shisha session, or to watch a football game with friends.

Food & Sohour Experience

The sohour menu was fantastic – everything we ordered was freshly cooked and made to order. We had foul, eggs, fries, and cheese, all served hot and flavorful. The ingredients were fresh, and the cooking was spot-on, delivering the perfect balance of taste and tradition. If you’re looking for an authentic Egyptian-style sohour, Oud Café does not disappoint.

Shisha & Service

One of the highlights of our visit was the amazing shisha experience. The shisha master, Mohamed, did a stellar job—he prepared one of the best shishas we’ve had in a long time, with rich flavor and smooth pulls. He was also quick and attentive with the coals, ensuring that the session remained enjoyable without interruption.

Service-wise, the café shines. Our waiter, Mohamed, was exceptionally friendly and funny, making us feel right at home. His attentiveness and hospitality elevated the whole experience. It’s rare to find staff who genuinely engage with customers, and he definitely made our visit even more enjoyable.

Atmosphere & Football Viewing

Oud Café is also an excellent place to watch football matches. The seating is comfortable, the screens are well-placed, and the vibe during a game is lively yet laid-back. Whether you’re a casual fan or a hardcore supporter, the setup makes it a fun place to enjoy the action.

Final Verdict

⭐ Food: 9/10 – Fresh, delicious, and well-prepared.
⭐ Shisha: 10/10 – Smooth, flavorful, and perfectly managed.
⭐ Service: 10/10 – Friendly, engaging, and attentive staff.
⭐ Ambiance: 9/10 – Relaxing, social, and ideal for both chilling and watching sports.
⭐ Overall Experience: 9.5/10 – A must-visit spot for sohour, shisha, or just a great time with friends.

Would definitely come back again and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a chill spot with great food and excellent service!

The hotel sits within walking distance of the Ramses Hilton and the Egyptian Museum, putting guests close to the Nile Corniche and central Downtown sights.
Its position makes reaching both Tahrir Square and the cafés and restaurants of Zamalek quick and inexpensive by foot or short taxi ride.
Economy rooms are small and designed mainly for sleeping, with some interior units having no window, which can feel enclosed for longer stays.
Basic amenities like air conditioning, private bathroom, and Wi‑Fi are provided, but guests should not expect premium finishes or views at this price level.
Nightly rates are budget friendly compared with riverfront chain hotels nearby, making it a good choice for solo travelers or couples watching their costs.
The trade-off is limited in-room comfort and features, but the savings allow more budget for tours, dining, and activities around Downtown and Zamalek.
Best for guests who plan to spend most of their time out in the city and mainly need a clean, central place to sleep.
Less ideal for those who value natural light, larger rooms, or resort-style facilities and are willing to pay more for a full-service riverside property.

name: Al-Kabsh Citadel
description: Al-Kabsh Citadel, located in the El Sayeda Zeinab area of Cairo, is a well-regarded landmark. It is highly rated, holding a 4.5-star rating from 108 reviews and standing as a popular neighborhood choice. It remains a worthwhile stop for both locals and visitors to Cairo.
address: 26HW+JVH, Lalet Al Kabsh, Tolon, El Sayeda Zeinab, Cairo Governorate 4261320
reviews:
Al-Kabsh Citadel is a historic fortress in Cairo, showcasing the city’s medieval military architecture. The citadel features robust stone walls, defensive towers, and strategic design elements that reflect the ingenuity of its builders.

Visitors can explore the exterior fortifications and appreciate the historical significance of the site as a defensive stronghold in Cairo’s urban and military history. The location offers a glimpse into the city’s past, providing context for its medieval urban planning and strategic importance.

Although less visited than larger landmarks, Al-Kabsh Citadel is a worthwhile stop for history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and anyone interested in Cairo’s defensive and cultural heritage.

The Citadel of the Ram: A Story of Redemption on the Hills of Historic Cairo
The Citadel of the Ram is not the name of a standing fortress or castle that can be visited today, but rather the name of a neighborhood and ancient historical … More

The Citadel of the Ram (Qal'at al-Kabsh) is a high area, built atop Mount Yashkur in Cairo. It has several entrances: one via Sayyida Nafisa Street, another via Ibn Tulun Street, and a third via Sayyida Zeinab Street. You'll find two staircases: a large one and a small one. From the top of the citadel, you can see all of Cairo, including the Mokattam Hills, the Cairo Tower, the Pyramids, and other beautiful landmarks. It also boasts a pleasant atmosphere. The Citadel of the Ram is built on the ruins of the ancient city of al-Qata'i, which was founded by Sultan Ahmad ibn Tulun, the founder of the Tulunid dynasty. Within the Citadel are several historical mosques, including the Mosque of Qaitbay (restored in 2006), the Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun (famous for its minaret), the Mosque of Amir Sarghatmish al-Nasiri, and the Mosque of Muhammad al-Jawli.

reviews:
We stayed here in October, the staff were very nice and helpful. We arrived at 5am and our room wasn’t available yet but they were very helpful to get us into another room until the morning when it was ready. Very old architecture building but the staff keeps the rooms pretty good. It felt stuffy but once the AC was on, the room was so much better. I would note that you are directly across from a mosque, so prayer time is extremely loud even inside the building. It’s not the hotels fault at all but it should be noted for future people to know. You will be awoken at 5am for the call the prayer outside😭 the keys to the rooms were cool skeleton keys and made it unique. Location is great otherwise and the price is good. We hired a guide through our hotel to take us to the pyramid and he was pretty good.

This was actually the best stay we had in Egypt. The location of the hotel is incredible..
Very central and plenty of restaurants around.
It’s situated in a gorgeous 19th century French styled building. 3M high ceilings and original parquet floors, generous space. The bathroom is clean and comfortable. There’s an elevator for the building which is really helpful.
Given the super central location, you might need earplugs depending on which room you are staying. I had no problem with it. The city wakes up late and it was still quiet around 7:30am.

Very good and quiet rooms. The Egyptian cotton bedsheets were very comfortable and gave us a really good night's sleep. It's a vintage style hotel, high ceiling, 24 hr hot water and a convenient refrigerator.

Although I must say I was very surprised to see our (working) refrigerator's power plug which was left unplugged after returning to our room one evening. This was after we explicitly told the staff NOT to make our room, when they asked us if we wanted our sheets changed etc. Thankfully nothing was lost from our room (and of course our sheet were as they were). So I don't know how the refrigerator's plug was unplugged. We certainly couldn't have done it as we had our yogurt in there which we wanted to eat cold upon our return.

Hany, and Youanna were of excellent help always ready to make sure customers were well taken care of. We will be sure to come again when we visit!

A Masterclass in How to Ruin Churrasco

The setting was gorgeous, the service was polished, the sides were delicious, and the wine hit all the right notes. For a moment I thought we were about to have a proper Four Seasons experience. Then the meat arrived, and the dream ended.

Apparently, churrasco now means “small random grill pieces tossed on skewers.” Who knew? The rotisserie, that small detail that defines the entire concept, was “not in use because it wasn’t busy enough.” That’s like saying the oven isn’t on because there aren’t enough pizzas. Every piece of meat that reached the table was well done, no matter how many times we asked for medium rare.

I paid premium prices for what felt like the world’s most exclusive minute steaks. Beautiful spot, great team, but someone needs to remind the kitchen that churrasco is cooked on the rotisserie, not just spoken of fondly.

Horrendous and traumatic experience – avoid at all costs

This was, without exaggeration, one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had. After spending over an hour trying to locate the property, we discovered that the address listed on Booking.com is incorrect. The “hotel” is in fact on the 4th floor of an ordinary apartment building, with absolutely no signage to indicate its presence. We called repeatedly for guidance and received no reply.

When we finally arrived at around 7pm, we were met by a very young boy, who claimed to be responsible for the bookings, accompanied by an equally young friend. We were casually informed that there was a “problem” and that our confirmed rooms were no longer available.

They then escorted us to another hotel from the same company. The rooms there were grotty, clearly inferior, and bore no resemblance whatsoever to what we had reserved and paid for. The entire situation felt deeply unprofessional and extremely suspicious.

We were left stranded in the evening and forced to make last-minute alternative arrangements, causing significant stress, inconvenience, and expense.

This experience was shocking, distressing, and completely unacceptable. I strongly advise others to avoid this establishment.

I had one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had with this property. I had booked in advance through Booking.com and had even requested an early check-in, which the hotel agreed to. The official check-in was 1 PM, and they confirmed I could check in by 11 AM.

When we arrived around 10:15 AM, they suddenly changed their story and said the earliest they could give the room was 11:30 AM. We waited, came back at 11:30, and then they pushed it to 12:30 PM because the previous guests hadn’t checked out which felt fair too.

We returned at 12:45 PM, and unbelievably, they asked us to wait another half hour. By the time it was already past the official check-in time (1:15 PM), they still had no room ready. When I asked how much longer, their behaviour became dismissive and unprofessional. Instead of giving us the room we booked, they tried to push us to a completely different “property” that looked more like someone’s personal house than a hotel room, and definitely not what was advertised.

When we refused and asked for the room we actually booked, they stalled another 15 minutes and then casually told us they couldn’t give us a room at all. They insisted we cancel the booking ourselves (they refused to cancel from their end), leaving us stranded at 1:30 PM with no hotel and no time to plan anything else. We had to scramble for a last-minute stay elsewhere, wasting almost an entire day.

On top of that, the hotel location is tucked away inside narrow lanes and not easy to find.

Unprofessional, unreliable, and completely disrespectful of guests’ time. I would never recommend this property to anyone.

reviews:
This is the best budget accomodation I have stayed in. The room was spacious and well decorated with ample storage and best of all very convenient to the pyramids. Breakfast was very good with a view of said pyramids from the roof. Best of all was the attention of the staff who were friendly and helpful throuhout my five day stay. I had planned most of my trip ahead of time (They would have helped me with this had I needed it), but they arranged transportation from and to the airport even helping me with my luggage at one in the morning when I had to leave for home. As a single senior traveller, I felt very safe and comfortable there and encourage others to venture out from tours and more conventional hotels to experience the hospitality of Egypt without breaking the bank. It is on the third floor with no elevator and you can hear the traffic outside, but I considered that part of the immersive experience of Cairo. My actual trip, which was mainly to see the Grand Egyptian Museum that had not yet opened on my last visit in 2023, was thrilling and I felt I saw another side of Egypt. I would do it again in a heartbeat and am so glad I chose this place to stay.

I definitely recommend this hotel for a trip to Cairo.

The staff here is the main advantage. We stayed from December 25th to January 1st, and even during the busy holiday period, they were incredibly attentive. As guests from Russia, we were greeted not just as clients, but with genuine warmth. They were always ready to help, offer advice, and did everything with a smile, creating a truly homely and calm atmosphere that you look forward to returning to after a hot day.

The rooms are clean, simple, but have everything you need.

But the main "wow" moment came the morning after check-in. From our room window, there was an absolutely direct, completely unobstructed view of the Giza plateau with its pyramids. Having breakfast with such a panorama is priceless.

And all of this comes at a very reasonable price. The balance of cost, view, cleanliness, and human kindness is top-notch.

The Mevlevi Takiya is an Ottoman-era building used by the Mevlevi Sufi order followers after its spread.

The place consists of three buildings, a school from the Mamluk era, a Tekiya from the Ottoman era and the Dervish Theater. The school was established by Prince Shams al-Din Sangar Al-Saadi in 721 AH / 1321 AD, then it became known as the dome of Hassan Sadaka Al-Shrabishi in 745 AH / 1344 AD.

The Mevlevi Takiya part was established in 1005 AH / 1595 AD and used as a residence for the poor, and its facade was characterized by combining the Mamluk and Ottoman styles.

The place also has tombs of Sufi saints and overall a very interesting place with different vibe from other surrounding historical structures.

Visitors can experience the serene and contemplative atmosphere of the complex, gaining insight into Sufi traditions, Islamic culture, and the role of such institutions in Cairo’s religious life. The intricate stonework, arches, and inscriptions highlight the architectural sophistication of the era.

Though relatively modest compared to larger landmarks, Takiya Al-Mawlawiyah provides a peaceful and culturally rich experience, making it a worthwhile stop for those interested in history, architecture, and spiritual heritage.

My en-suite room was spotlessly clean, bed was comfortable and the owner and the chap who welcomed me could not have been more helpful 👍 … More

Recommended by all means!
For me, it was a perfect accommodation during the conference at The American University in Cairo. For anyone attending any event at AUC, just the right choice. Less than 10 minutes pleasant walk from Smile Apartment 2 to AUC Gate 4 (Pepsi Gate). At the same time, after my 5 days stay, and after talking to so many colleagues who stayed elsewhere in Cairo, Smile 2 appears to be a very good choice for anyone who comes to Cairo.
1.	The Location: easily reachable by car from Cairo International airport, no need to go through the heavy traffic in the city centre. Less than 30 minutes’ drive by car or taxi. A quiet little street, less than 100 meters walk and one is on AUC avenue, the University is just across the road. For those doing sightseeing in the city centre: around 45 minutes by taxi to Zamalek island, for example. Make sure to double the time during rush hours if there are meetings/events to be on time for, just in case. Cairo traffic may be unpredictable. And still: the apartment, the service, the value for money, and most of all, the owner and his staff are so great, Smile 2 is worth choosing even if one focuses on the city centre.
2.	The neighborhood: decent and safe any time of the day. The part of New Cairo next to AUC campus still has some areas being developed, but overall, it already has everything: the shops, the cafes, good roads and very nice sidewalks next to AUC.
3.	Apartment quality: excellent room. Very functional. Comfortable bed, the just right mattress, pillows and blanket – I have always slept well. No noises, alien smells or whatever. Very clean laundry and room itself. The sink, the shower, the air conditioning- in a word, everything in good working condition. There was a fridge, a microwave oven and an electric kettle in my room. Just remember to get teabags and sugar if needed.
4.	The service: great, responsible and highly responsive owner and staff. Whatever one needs, just ask and help and/or advice is given, quickly and efficiently. One of the staff is in the lobby or by the entrance 24/7. Exceptionally convenient: one can check in, go out or return any time of the day or night. Very friendly! I absolutely fell in love with Egypt after this stay, especially because of the great Smile 2 apartment team, the great owner, Mr. Khaled and his staff (especially Mamdouh, he is amazing).
5.	The breakfasts: for 3 US dollars a day (the price at the time of my stay) one gets a hearty breakfast. Very tasty, too. Just tell the owner and/or the staff you need it one day before. Smile 2 has its own little yard, several tables with chairs, with beautiful trees and flowers around. Great atmosphere! I attached the photos of this yard, this was where I had my breakfasts in the mornings before going to conference events at AUC or in the city centre.
6.	Wifi access: free wifi for guests. The signal may be better downstairs in the lobby or in the inner yard, but one can still use e-mail, social networks or whatever in the room, too.
In summary, judging by what dozens of colleagues staying elsewhere in Cairo said about their accommodation, no matter which budget, I am convinced I made the best choice and I recommend it to others. Next time I come to Cairo, I will definitely choose Smile 2 apartment again.

reviews:
My 11-day stay at Nile X was extremely stressful and disappointing. Before booking my flight, I had communicated through the Booking.com chat that I would arrive around 5 am and asked if early check-in would be possible. I received an “ok” response, so I planned my travel accordingly. However, when I arrived I was told early check-in was not possible and was asked to pay an additional 60 USD to access the room between 6 am and noon. When I showed screenshots of the conversation, the owner denied that early check-in had been confirmed.
The location was also misleading. I had been told it would be very close to Zamalek X Hostel, but it turned out to be on a quiet and uncomfortable street, and the property itself is on the 19th floor, something that was never mentioned. The elevator felt unsafe and unstable.
The “Nile view” room description was also inaccurate. The windows were not double-glazed, so the room was extremely noisy, and the actual Nile view was minimal.
Several basic amenities advertised were missing or poor:
Breakfast advertised as included, but in practice there was almost nothing provided.
Kitchen was poorly equipped and unhygienic, lacking basic items like a proper frying pan, knife, or mugs. I ended up buying my own ingredients and making my own breakfast most days.
Bathroom lacked essentials, including toilet paper.
The bed was unstable, with loose wooden planks supporting the mattress. This was only partially fixed near the end of my stay.
Staff frequently asked me to pay the extra fee in cash and knocked repeatedly on my door, which felt uncomfortable and intrusive.
Overall, the stay involved misleading information, poor maintenance, lack of hygiene, and stressful interactions with management. Unfortunately, this experience made my time in Cairo far more difficult than it should have been.

A very comfortable stay with great potential ✨
I booked a single room, and it looked almost exactly like the photos — clean, modern, and well-prepared. The only difference was that the bathroom was noticeably smaller than expected, However, I was told it includes one of the best showers, which was a nice touch. I would rate the room comfort and bathroom size 4/5.

The location is a strong highlight. You’re just steps away from a main road, with everything around you — supermarkets, pharmacies, and daily essentials. Within the Sheikh Zayed area, it’s extremely convenient. However, since my main use was accessing the main axis, which takes around 20–25 minutes by car, I would rate the location 3/5.

What truly stands out is the staff. The staff were available 24/7, quick to respond, polite, and genuinely helpful. Service: 5/5.

A few things to keep in mind:
The hotel is quite new, so some facilities (like the restaurant) are not operating yet — but delivery is always an easy option.
Some services are still being finalized.
The in-room Wi-Fi is fast and free, but it doesn’t connect to smart TVs (so streaming platforms aren’t available).

In terms of value, considering that all services are not running yet, the price feels slightly on the higher side. A small adjustment (around $15–20 less) would make it perfectly aligned with the current offering. especially since this would better align with the average rates of nearby hotels — I mean come on $55 for just a room? That’s a bit ambitious 😄

Overall, it was a very comfortable stay with great potential once everything is fully operational 😊

The Room with a Breathtaking View and Heartwarming Hospitality

Before travelling to Egypt, we’d read many reviews warning that locals often ask for extra money for services. Our experience at Halda Inn was the complete opposite: genuine hospitality and thoughtful, no-strings-attached service.

When we first arrived and saw the gate, the building looked quite old. But the moment we reached the 7th floor, it felt like stepping into a whole new world.

• Views: I’ll let the photos do the talking (all pictures were taken from the room - the bed and the balcony).

• Food: Breakfast was excellent! We loved it so much that we requested the same meal again the next day (we stayed for 2 nights).

• Location: Very close to the pyramids. Tours offer hotel pick-up and drop-off, and we were able to get an Uber & Careem easily whenever we needed. There are also many great food spots nearby (we tried some of the most authentic Egyptian food here)!

• Hospitality: This truly touched our hearts. We requested extra milk and tea during our stay, and when it was time to settle the bill, they refused to accept any additional payment. Every time we entered or left, we were greeted with a smile (and water bottles!) by Mr Khalid Alfaqih (the owner) and the wonderful staff and family.

All in all, a memorable stay; highly recommended!

We had an absolutely fantastic stay at the Palace Pyramids Hotel and couldn’t recommend it more highly.

The hotel itself is spotless, very well run, and feels genuinely safe and comfortable. The facilities are great, but the real show-stopper is the rooftop. The view of the pyramids from up there is honestly unbelievable. Having breakfast each morning while looking straight out at them was a pinch-yourself moment, and coming back in the evenings after a long day of exploring to see them again at sunset was just magical.

The rooms were very comfortable and felt completely secure - we were happy leaving valuables behind while we were out for the day, which says a lot when travelling.

What really makes this place special, though, is the people. Every single member of staff was kind, genuine, and incredibly helpful - nothing ever felt like too much trouble. Nadia, in particular, went above and beyond. On our first day she even jumped in a tuk-tuk with me and my dad to help us get local Egyptian SIM cards, knowing we didn’t speak Arabic. That level of care really sets the tone for the whole place. She also helped us design an itinerary as soon as we arrived, making sure everything we wanted to see was covered, and had it all ready to go by the next morning.

We were also lucky enough to have Ahmed, the owner of the hotel, personally guide us around Cairo for two days. As a Cairo-born, highly experienced guide, he was exceptional. We were able to get into every museum and site we wanted, often without the usual waiting or time slots - a huge bonus. More than that, he’s a warm, welcoming person who was happy to answer questions, adjust plans on the fly, and tailor each day to how we were feeling.

The hotel also arranged a day trip to Alexandria for us, including a driver and a brilliant local guide who was an archaeologist and clearly passionate about the sites she showed us. Everything was seamless.

Breakfast each morning was a lovely spread, and sitting there with that view never got old.

We truly had a once-in-a-lifetime trip and are already planning to return later this year. I can’t recommend staying here strongly enough.

One final note: before coming to Egypt, we’d heard all the usual stories about scams and needing to be on guard. Our experience couldn’t have been further from that. Everyone we met was kind, welcoming, and genuinely wanted us to feel at home. The warmth and energy of the people here — and especially at this hotel - completely changed our perspective. Egypt is vibrant, generous, and a little chaotic in the best possible way, and this hotel and its staff are a perfect reflection of that.

It has taken me two years to write this review, but I feel it is important to warn others: please be careful when staying at this hotel.

During my stay, a maid entered my room and stole money. Management later confirmed that they had camera footage showing the maid entering my room after it had already been cleaned. Because of this incident, I was forced to cut my stay short.

The situation became even more unsettling the next day. I left the hotel briefly to run an errand, but before leaving I packed all my belongings and placed my bags by the door. When I returned, management asked me, “Are you leaving early?”

This made me question how they knew my bags were packed if I had not told anyone. It raised the uncomfortable possibility that someone may have entered my room while I was away.

What a shame. I have traveled back and forth to Cairo, Egypt for over ten years. Never have I had such a frightening and disappointing experience.

reviews:
Mosque and Madrasa of Umm al-Sultan Sha‘ban is a historic Mamluk-era religious complex built in the late 14th century during the reign of Sultan al-Ashraf Sha‘ban ibn Husayn, and was dedicated to his mother, Khawand Baraka, who was popularly known as “Umm al-Sultan Sha‘ban” (Mother of Sultan Sha‘ban).

Construction began around 1368–1369 CE (770 AH). The complex served several functions at once, combining a mosque, madrasa (Islamic school), mausoleum, sabil (public water fountain), and kuttab (Qur’an school for children). This multifunctional design was a hallmark of Mamluk architecture and charitable foundations in medieval Cairo.

Architecturally, the monument is an excellent example of Bahri Mamluk design. It contains the tombs of the Sultan and his mother.
Mesmerizing mosque and madrasa that captures the essence of Egyptian architecture and beauty. The interior is very tranquil and the exterior is astounding too. A must visit

description: City Star Hotel, located at 11 El-Tahrir Square in the Qasr El Nil area of Cairo, is a popular hotel. address: 11 El-Tahrir Square, Ismailia, Qasr El Nil, Cairo Governorate 11512
reviews:
City Star Hotel, Tahrir Square – A Night Out of Necessity
City Star Hotel is centrally located near Tahrir Square, but don’t assume that seeing a metro sign nearby means easy access. Several metro entrances in the area are gated or closed, including ones right outside the hotel, which can be confusing if you’re unfamiliar with Cairo.
The hotel is good value for money, and you can pay by card, although you’ll likely feel the exchange rate. The staff were friendly and generally helpful, as long as you weren’t dealing with them in the middle of the night. English was spoken at a borderline adequate level, enough to get by but not much more.
The building itself houses multiple businesses, which adds to the confusion. The elevator operator initially took us to the wrong floor, and only thanks to another tenant did we find the reception — which, unexpectedly, is on the first floor. Our room was on the second floor, where the elevator door was literally wired shut.
The room was extremely small, roughly only about 50% larger than the beds themselves. The bathroom was tiny, with the toilet touching the shower curtain. That said, considering we had missed the last bus to Luxor, I was simply grateful to have found a room for the night.
Everything in the room was very old. I genuinely laughed when I realized the paintings on the wall were glued on — possibly as an anti-theft measure. Noise from the street is intense, and earplugs are essential. Noise-canceling headphones, exhaustion, and even chamomile tea help too.
At first glance, the room looked clean. However, when I tried to rotate the bed to get some distance from my snoring brother, I discovered a very thick layer of dust underneath, along with used cotton swabs and bits of plastic or rubber that I’d rather not identify.
Soundproofing is almost nonexistent. Our room was at the end of the corridor, and I could hear my brother snoring from the staircase. Even with the door closed, there was such a large gap that you could see directly into the room.
Breakfast matched other guests’ reviews: you get what you pay for. Thankfully, the area is full of nearby options if you want something better.
Wi-Fi comes with unique credentials printed on a piece of paper and works on only one device. If you need it on a second phone or a laptop, you’ll have to ask reception for more logins.
As for water temperature, I didn’t understand the complaints — the heater in our bathroom was set to what felt like 90°C. But that's what the indicator said.
This isn’t a hotel you stay at for comfort. It’s a place you stay because you need a roof over your head, close to everything, and at a reasonable price — and for one night, that was enough.

reviews:
The art course relied heavily on participants’ prior experience or intuition, which might work if you’re only looking for a casual space to create, but not if you’re expecting to learn techniques or develop skills. Additionally, we were told there would be follow-up support, including a WhatsApp group to share material details and where to purchase them, but this was never provided.
Second, the session duration was not followed. Although each session was advertised as 3 hours, some lasted only 1 to 1.5 hours.
Finally, although the group size was relatively small, the space itself felt limited for the number of participants. Also, the number of participants compared to available tools felt unbalanced. Tools were shared among attendees, which gave the impression of limited investment in the overall experience. The people running the workshop are very kind and welcoming though.
Overall, this workshop may suit those looking for an unstructured, self-guided art session, but it falls short if you’re expecting a guided learning experience or good value for time and cost.

⭐ Highly Recommended Family-Friendly Stay in the Heart of Cairo ⭐

We stayed at Cairo Boutique Hotel around November–December 2025 for about five days, and it was a wonderful experience for our entire family. We were traveling with our toddler, our five-year-old, and my spouse, and the hotel suited our needs perfectly.
The hotel is located in a very central downtown area, making it easy to walk to nearby restaurants and explore the city without hassle. Despite being in the heart of Cairo, the stay felt comfortable and relaxed.

One of the highlights is that the hotel is set in a beautiful old historic building, which adds a lot of charm and character. The elevator is truly iconic and reflects the old-world character of the building. The rooms are very spacious, well-ventilated, and extremely comfortable—something we truly appreciated while staying with young kids.

The staff - Mohammad Atta, Nesma Elsaged and Abdullah deserve special mention. They were incredibly friendly, caring, and always willing to help, making us feel welcome throughout our stay. Their attentiveness really stood out, especially when traveling with a toddler.

The hotel also assisted us with local transportation, which was a huge plus. We arranged an airport pickup through the hotel, and it was very reasonably priced. I would highly recommend doing this, as it helps avoid overpaying when arriving as a tourist. You can simply call or message the hotel in advance, and they take care of everything smoothly.

Overall, we had a fantastic stay and would highly recommend Cairo Boutique Hotel to anyone visiting Cairo—especially families looking for a comfortable, well-located place with warm and helpful staff.

reviews:
An Exceptional First Experience in Egypt – Eyes of Egypt Boutique Hotel

As first-time visitors to Egypt 🇪🇬, arriving from Scandinavia, we had many expectations and uncertainties about what to expect. Our main hopes were to experience the awe-inspiring Pyramids and the Sphinx, as well as to visit the newly opened Grand Egyptian Museum. For this reason, we chose to stay close to these iconic landmarks.

After careful consideration, we selected Eyes of Egypt Boutique Hotel, primarily for its breathtaking pyramid views—and it exceeded all our expectations.

The hotel kindly arranged airport pickup, which we were deeply grateful for, as we arrived in the middle of the night. What truly impressed us from the very beginning was the personal welcome by the owner himself, along with his warm, attentive, and professional staff.

At first glance, the hotel’s exterior may not reveal what awaits inside. However, once you enter, you are welcomed into a space that feels luxurious, elegant, and thoughtfully designed—truly comparable to a five-star boutique hotel. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the hospitality is exceptional.

The staff went above and beyond to make us feel welcome in Egypt. We were offered traditional tea, a delicious Egyptian breakfast, and helpful guidance on using local Uber services and food delivery. Every detail was handled with care and genuine kindness.

The owner, Waleed, is an incredibly dedicated and resilient entrepreneur. His hands-on approach, flexibility, and sincere care for his guests are evident in every aspect of the hotel. Special thanks and gratitude to the wonderful team—Ali, Mohamed, Makmod, Yousef, and Jasmine—who all delivered outstanding service with professionalism and heartfelt kindness.

The boutique hotel is beautifully located on the 6th floor, offering spectacular views and a peaceful atmosphere. While the surrounding area may not reflect the elegance of the hotel’s interior, we always felt completely safe and comfortable. Unlike other areas we visited, we were not disturbed by taxi offers or street vendors, making this hotel a true sanctuary.

What truly made this stay unforgettable was the personal touch from the owner and his wife, whose warmth and generosity created an experience that will remain in our hearts.

We extend our sincere thanks to the entire team at Eyes of Egypt Boutique Hotel for their kindness and exceptional hospitality. We highly recommend this hotel to all travelers—and especially to our friends and fellow travelers from Scandinavia.

★★★★★ 5/5 — Rooftop breakfast facing the Giza Pyramids + next-level hospitality and unbeatable tour value

If you’re choosing a place in Giza, this guesthouse is the kind of stay that turns a normal trip into a memorable one. It’s clean, comfortable, and excellent value—but what truly makes it outstanding is the family-style hospitality and the rooftop breakfast with a direct view toward the Giza Pyramids.

The unforgettable part: rooftop breakfast with pyramid view
Waking up and having breakfast on the rooftop while looking straight toward the Giza Pyramids is extraordinary. It’s the kind of moment you don’t get from most accommodations—even many “pyramid view” listings. Sitting there in the morning with the Pyramids in front of you felt special and instantly set the tone for the entire day.

Hospitality that feels genuinely personal
The host has amazing energy—friendly, respectful, and proactive. This didn’t feel like a standard “check-in and disappear” stay. They consistently helped in real, practical ways:
- The host made breakfast himself, which felt warm and home-like.
- They were very attentive and truly helpful, not just polite.
- They helped us carry and manage our luggage, which matters a lot when you’re moving around Cairo.
- They also provided laundry service, which was incredibly convenient during a busy itinerary.

Transport support that removes all the stress
One of the biggest advantages here is how easy they make logistics:
- The host helped us get around, including rides to places like the museum and the bus station.
- They offer an airport pick-up service and it was surprisingly affordable—a big relief after landing, especially if you don’t want to negotiate taxis or deal with unfamiliar apps late at night.

Full-day pyramids trip (best value compared to platforms)
Another major highlight: the son drove us for a full-day trip to several pyramid sites (not only one stop). This was a game changer:
- It felt like a flexible private day trip—less rushed and more comfortable.
- They helped plan the route and made the day smooth from start to finish.
- Price-wise, the tours they arranged were much cheaper than Klook for similar itineraries, which gave us far better value without sacrificing comfort.

Room, comfort, and cleanliness
This is not a luxury chain hotel, but for what most travelers need, it’s excellent:
- Large room, twin beds, and a TV.
- The room felt practical and comfortable after long sightseeing days.
- The bathroom was clean, and overall everything was well kept.

Who this place is perfect for
- Anyone who wants a true pyramid-view moment (especially breakfast on the rooftop)
- Travelers who value warm, family-run hospitality
- Visitors who want airport pickup, help with transport, and affordable private tours
- People who prefer a stay where the host can actually help you navigate Giza/Cairo easily

Tips for future guests (to get the best experience)
- Message them early about airport pickup and your pyramid itinerary (Giza + other pyramid sites). They’re responsive and can arrange it smoothly.
- If you’re interested in a full-day tour, tell them what you want to prioritize so they can structure the day efficiently.
- Don’t skip the rooftop in the morning and sunset—the view is the kind of travel memory you’ll want photos of.

Overall: An outstanding stay that combines a rare rooftop pyramid-view breakfast, genuinely caring hosts, and excellent-value tours/transport. We felt looked after from arrival to departure, and we’d happily stay again.

reviews:
What a discovery!
This refreshing flea market in central downtown Cairo is something you wouldn’t expect to find. Be ready to find some hidden treasures that are probably out of some old Egyptian houses. The market is a nice walk and you can find a lot of different specialised merchants: coins, stamps, homeware, posters and much more.
This takes place on Saturdays only which adds up to making this market special, I do recommend however going as early as possible because special pieces might get sold quickly. Also make sure to negotiate, you will be surprised at how low you can get some prices.
If you are going with a car, make sure to park in the very close parking nearby, which is just infront of the Central Bank building.
Mike’s tip: after the market, walk to Latif Wassily to have some of the freshest baked goods in town, in a historic bakery.
